The expression captures both merging-induced and band-flip-induced charge flips. We find that, during a band flip, the topological charge of the BIC reverses with the formation of lines of circular polarization that cross at the $Γ$ point. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. Breaking vertical symmetry makes both kinds of charge flips channel-differentiated, creating a parameter interval in which the BIC carries opposite topological charges in the two channels and forms a Janus BIC. We show that Janus BICs also emerge in experimentally accessible one- and two-dimensional silicon-based photonic lattices. Our results link the topological charge of a BIC directly to the band structure and the channel-resolved radiation amplitudes and establish a basis for channel-selective control of polarization singularities.

items.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
items.summary: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. The proposed model incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation (PDE) into this transformation process, guiding the changes between initial and target samples using physical knowledge. The model further combines the physical dynamics with statistical patterns captured from data to learn this transformation, adaptively adjusting their relative contributions at each location. The model is trained and evaluated using one year of global TEC data generated by the Thermosphere Ionosphere Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM). The results demonstrate that our model improves both spatial and temporal forecasting accuracy over representative benchmarks, including statistical, deep learning, and generative AI methods at all lead times and across latitudes. The average root mean square error (RMSE) is 39.2% lower than that of ConvLSTM and 23.8% lower than that of the same framework without physical guidance. The learned contribution weights vary systematically with latitude and across geographic locations, showing how the physical contribution changes across the forecast domain. These findings demonstrate that explicit physical guidance improves generative forecasts of global TEC and highlight the value of incorporating physical dynamics into generative AI modeling.

items.title: Study of Multilayer TiNx/Ti/TiNx Films Formed In Situ for High-Efficiency Integrated Microheaters
items.summary: A technology for the in situ formation of a three-layer TiN$_x$/Ti/TiN$_x$ functional material within a single vacuum cycle is presented, together with the results of investigations of its structural and electrophysical properties. The maximum critical power density reached approximately 140 MW/cm$^2$. Under continuous operation at 90% of the critical power, the structures remained operational for 24 h. The characteristics of microbridges without and with a protective SiO$_x$ layer were compared. The presence of the coating modifies the electrothermal operating regime of the structures and enables estimated temperatures of approximately 500-700 degrees Celsius to be reached.

items.title: Data-driven synthesis of high-fidelity triaxial magnetic waveforms for quantum control
items.summary: We present a system for generating arbitrary, triaxial magnetic waveforms with a spectral content spanning from DC to tens of kHz, a critical capability for quantum control and spin manipulation. To compensate for amplifier-coil dynamics, we implement a data-driven approach to identify a numerical compensation model. The method parametrizes the system response using a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter calibrated on the specific waveform to be generated. The application of a driving signal designed via frequency-domain inversion of the identified model enables the synthesis of complex field sequences with sharp transitions between static and single- or multi-frequency temporal segments. The work is validated with experimental results demonstrating waveform fidelity and transient performance, thereby showcasing the precision and feasibility of the method.

items.title: Surveying exogenous species in Saturn with ALMA I. Detecting and Mapping CO
items.summary: The origin of carbon monoxide (CO) in Saturn's stratosphere remains uncertain, with proposed sources including internal thermochemical production, cometary impacts, and exogenic material from the rings and icy moons (i.e. Enceladus). We aim to constrain the vertical and meridional distribution of stratospheric CO and assess the relative contributions of these potential sources. Here, we analysed high-spectral-resolution ALMA observations of the CO (J=3-2) line obtained on 25 May 2018, sampling Saturn's limb from 20°S to 69°N. CO vertical profiles were retrieved using a line-by-line radiative transfer model combined with spectral inversion techniques, testing multiple prior scenarios representative of different source hypotheses. CO is confined to a narrow layer between 0.1 and 1 mbar, with a robust negative vertical gradient and mean abundances of (3.7+/- 0.8) x 10$^{-8}$ at 0.1 mbar and (7.2 +/- 0.9) x 10$^{-8}$ at 1 mbar. The meridional distribution is statistically homogeneous, with a marginal enhancement near 60° N plausibly related to Enceladus. No significant equatorial enhancement is detected. The absence of a strong equatorial enhancement rules out a long-lived steady source associated with ring infall. The observations are most consistent with a relatively recent ($\approx$200-year-old or younger) cometary impact whose material has since been horizontally mixed, while any Cassini Grand Finale ring influx was either too recent or inefficient to affect CO abundances at the probed pressure levels.

items.title: A Comparison of Electric-Field Profile Reconstruction Methods based on the E-FISH Diagnostic
items.summary: Electric-field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH) is a non-intrusive, non-resonant technique for measuring electric fields in moderate-to-atmospheric pressure plasmas. However, its nonlinear, path-integrated nature introduces measurement uncertainty, preventing a unique relationship between the measured signal and local electric field. One approach to overcome this limitation is to acquire spatial EFISH profiles and invert them to reconstruct the underlying electric-field distribution. Although several inversion methods have been employed, their reconstruction accuracy and overall performance have yet to be systematically evaluated. This study compares three methods: machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion, using EFISH measurements from four electrode geometries with distinct electric-field distributions. Their performance is evaluated in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness to sparse data and noise, and ability to reconstruct asymmetric profiles. All three methods successfully reconstruct electric-field profiles, but exhibit distinct advantages and limitations. Machine learning provides high accuracy, computational speed, and noise resilience, but performs poorly on profiles that differ substantially from its training data, particularly asymmetric profiles. Linear inversion accommodates a broader range of field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile. Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields but performs well for horizontal field polarization. The complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivate a potential hybrid approach for reconstructing electric fields with unknown spatial distributions. Overall, this study identifies key trade-offs among the methods and provides guidance for selecting suitable reconstruction strategies under different measurement conditions.

items.title: Emergent energy scales in magnonic systems with relative motion
items.summary: Relative motion between interacting systems can generate emergent energy scales that are absent in isolated systems. While uniform motion can be eliminated by a Galilean transformation, relative motion between interacting systems generally cannot. By coupling to an excitation's spatial structure, relative motion generates a Doppler frequency determined by its wavevector and the relative velocity, providing a mechanism for driving nonequilibrium phenomena. In this tutorial, we illustrate these ideas using magnonic systems as a concrete platform. We first discuss motion-induced magnon transport between relatively moving ferromagnets, in which the Doppler frequency serves as an effective nonequilibrium bias in the perturbative regime. This mechanism produces magnon currents even without conventional driving forces such as temperature gradients or chemical potential differences. We then introduce motion-induced parametric instabilities. When the emergent scale becomes sufficiently large to resonantly create magnon pairs, the perturbative description breaks down, and the magnonic vacuum becomes unstable. This instability occurs above a critical velocity threshold and leads to spontaneous magnon-pair creation. Connections to related phenomena, including quantum friction, Cherenkov emission, and Zel'dovich superradiance, are also highlighted. The concept of an emergent energy scale provides a unifying framework for understanding transport phenomena and instabilities in quantum systems with relative motion.

items.title: The Natural Formulation of Cubic-Phase Dynamics in the Linear Potential
items.summary: A quantum wave packet in a linear potential, i.e. a constant force such as gravity, accumulates a cubic-in-time phase, universal across Schrödinger-type platforms. The natural formulation of the cubic phase dynamics follows from their canonical realization, the Airy eigenstates. The eigenforce, the potential gradient for which the Airy profile is stationary and hence the intrinsic force behind its known self-acceleration absent any applied force, derives from the eigenvalue problem and characterizes the state uniquely up to a rigid translation. Alongside the applied force, it underlies the analytically closed form of these dynamics, comprising three known contributions, intrinsic, force-induced, and a cross term. The force-induced one alone is shape-independent, whereas the Airy eigenstate renders the other two non-dispersing. The cubic coefficient factorizes into two Newtonian force balances, vanishing at the stationary eigenstate and at a non-trivial zero where the phase cancels while the packet keeps accelerating. This exposes the eigenforce as an effective antagonist to the applied force, not only in the caustic's self-acceleration but here also within the phase, while leaving the centroid untouched by Ehrenfest's theorem. Spatially uniform within each packet, it escapes direct measurement, accessible only as the relative phase of two colliding packets, each in its own potential. The relative cubic coefficient is symmetry-forbidden for identical packets and activated by preparation asymmetry. Simulated interference of two truncated Airy packets demonstrates the extraction. Spanning ultracold atoms, paraxial optics, and surface-gravity water waves, it provides a platform-independent probe of the cubic phase and, through its force dependence, of the constant force itself.

items.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
items.summary: Background and purpose: Radiotherapy planning agents based on large language models (LLMs) decide when to submit a plan or request review but are evaluated mainly by dose. This study developed OpenGray, a benchmark of planning tasks with known correct decisions. Materials and methods: OpenGray adds tasks with known answers to the OpenKBP-Opt head-and-neck dataset, including two contradictions with dose goals proven incompatible and a feasible control with a stored plan meeting every hard goal. Four systems, from a rule-based planning script to a full LLM agent, were evaluated on 30 patients, the LLM-based ones with a commercial (Terra) and a local (Ministral 3 8B) LLM. Decisions, achieved dose, problem recognition, and technical failures were recorded and also read from logs of 39 stereotactic radiosurgery runs of SAGE, a clinical LLM agent. Results: With Terra, the script preceded by an LLM review and the full agent had decision accuracies of 95.4% and 92.1%, respectively, yet escalated only 50% (95% confidence interval, 25-75%) and 25% (10-40%) of overlap contradictions, which required arithmetic on the anatomy. All four systems submitted every feasible control, but 24% of these plans missed a hard goal that the stored plan had met. In four SAGE runs, one goal failed at every attempt; the agent identified it in every reply but had no action for stopping. Conclusions: Favorable aggregate scores concealed specific decision failures. Planning agents should be evaluated on their decisions as well as their dose and given an explicit action for stopping and requesting review.

items.title: Hologram generation using attention for Fraunhofer diffraction
items.summary: Controlling optical wavefronts in the strict far-field regime is a fully global inverse problem. Fraunhofer propagation is a single Fourier transform of the aperture, so every modulator pixel couples to every point of the reconstruction and no spatial locality survives for the convolutional priors that dominate learned holography to exploit. Iterative phase retrieval stagnates and trades computation for quality, and camera-in-the-loop methods remain iterative and near-field. Here we show that this global coupling maps naturally onto self-attention, generating a phase-only hologram in a single forward pass of 12 to 24 ms. On hardware, every simulation-trained method collapses to a common floor between 15.8 and 16.1 dB median PSNR set by model-reality mismatch, despite spanning 27.7 to 56.5 dB median PSNR in ideal simulation. Placing the physical optics inside the training loop, which we call self-attention in-the-loop (SAIL), reaches 19.53 dB median PSNR and exceeds the strongest camera-adapted baseline by 0.79 dB on 18 of 18 targets (0.43 dB on 14 of 18 under a more faithful forward model). Most importantly, we show self-attention allows one shared network to serve 18 targets, and as the task complexity increases, the attention mechanism activates. These results establish self-attention as a scalable framework for far-field holography, and attention-based modeling as a general approach to inverse problems governed by long-range interactions in wave physics.

items.title: Beyond urban boundaries: Percolation reveals land-consumptive growth in India
items.summary: Cities often extend beyond their administrative boundaries, complicating assessments of urban sustainability. Using Global Human Settlement Layer data for India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975--2025), we develop a percolation-based framework for urban delineation. Within district-based regions, we apply unrestricted DBSCAN to spatial coordinates of 100-m cells with positive population and built-up surface. We treat neighborhood distance as the percolation control parameter and the proportion of eligible cells in the largest connected cluster as the empirical order parameter. Sharp increases in this proportion reveal characteristic percolation transitions. Post-transition connection lengths declined (median:650m to 350m), indicating that previously disconnected settlements coalesce at progressively shorter spatial distances alongside increasing urban land consumption. Urban footprint increased from 447.6 to 1,382.7km$^2$, while population densities declined. SDG11.3.1 land-consumption-to-population-growth ratios generally exceeded unity. Zipf and allometric relationships describe cross-sectional urban structure, but land-consumptive growth shows little relationship with city size. Urban delineation thus shapes sustainability assessments.

items.title: The dynamical memory of tidal stellar streams: Joint inference of the Galactic potential and the progenitor of GD-1 with flow matching
items.summary: Stellar streams offer one of the most sensitive probes of the Milky Way`s gravitational potential, as their phase-space morphology encodes both the tidal field of the host galaxy and the internal structure of their progenitors. In this work, we introduce a framework that leverages Flow Matching and Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) to jointly infer the parameters of the GD-1 progenitor and the global properties of the Milky Way potential. Our aim is to move beyond traditional techniques (e.g. orbit-fitting and action-angle methods) by constructing a fully Bayesian, likelihood-free posterior over both host-galaxy parameters and progenitor properties, thereby capturing the intrinsic coupling between tidal stripping dynamics and the underlying potential. To achieve this, we generate a large suite of mock GD-1-like streams using our differentiable N-body code \textsc{\texttt{Odisseo}}, sampling self-consistent initial conditions from a Plummer sphere and evolving them in a flexible Milky Way potential model. We then apply conditional Flow Matching to learn the vector field that transports a base Gaussian distribution into the posterior, enabling efficient, amortized inference directly from stream phase-space data. We demonstrate that our method successfully recovers the true parameters of a fiducial GD-1 simulation, producing well-calibrated posteriors and accurately reproducing parameter degeneracies arising from progenitor-host interactions. Flow Matching provides a powerful, flexible framework for Galactic Archaeology. Our approach enables joint inference on progenitor and Galactic parameters, capturing complex dependencies that are difficult to model with classical likelihood-based methods.

items.title: Mapping Artistic Engagement with Quantum Technologies
items.summary: Quantum technologies (QT) are increasingly being taken up in artistic practices, for example in the form of visual artworks or quantum computer music. However, more comprehensive empirical studies on the temporal development and the different forms of QT-related art are still lacking. Therefore, this study conducted a systematic mapping and classification of QT-related artworks. To this end, a medium-independent corpus was established, and the artworks were classified into four categories: QT-Inspired, QT-Sourced, Simulated QT, and QT-Generated. This classification was LLM-assisted and checked against human-coded reference data as well as through manual review of unclear cases. In total, 281 QT-related artworks from 2010 to August 2025 were identified. The corpus shows a substantial increase in QT-related artworks since 2019, with a considerable share attributed to only a few artists. The different forms of QT relations coexist, while an increasing use of active hardware-based and simulated processes in artistic practices can be documented, particularly since 2021. Although no clear development trajectories between these categories can be identified, the observed development coincides with advances in QT and their improved accessibility. Thus, this study provides an empirical basis for further analyzing the development of QT-related art, the possible emergence of a "quantum art scene," and the reciprocal relationships between art and quantum technologies.

items.title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
items.summary: Unsteady flow over a 30 $μ$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

items.title: Comparative analysis of tungsten armor and a liquid-lithium film as first walls for the HiPER laser-fusion chamber: thermal response, vapor shielding and helium transmission to the steel
items.summary: Tungsten armor and liquid-metal films, the usual sacrificial first walls of laser-fusion chambers, were modeled separately. Both go through one calculation for the three HiPER scenarios: NRL 154 MJ spectra scaled by yield, binned to keep each ion species' number and energy, a common deposition model, and a one-dimensional enthalpy solver with melting, evaporation and parameterized vapor shielding. In Demo (154 MJ, 6.5 m, 10 Hz), a 1 mm tungsten armor peaks 378 K below melting without neutron heating (275-319 K with it). A degraded near-surface conductivity can erase this margin, which also depends on the ion-spectra construction. The steel interface exceeds the 925 K limit, and the surface accumulates the 10^18-10^19 m^-2 helium fluences associated with the onset of surface modification within 10-98 shots (not a lifetime). A lithium film keeps the steel below 925 K from 44 um and below the 873 K compatibility limit from 56 um, more with partial renewal. Burn ions then implant helium; keeping the steel below 10^18 m^-2 for 10^6 shots needs 184 um, which binds in every scenario. The film evaporates 7.4x10^-4 kg m^-2 per shot (range 4.2-8.4x10^-4 kg m^-2, full renewal). Vapor shielding, with a nearly un-ionized vapor (Saha estimate), changes this by -21 % to +5 % for the Saha-supported stopping factor s = 1 and -34 % to +8 % across s = 1-2. Both walls are thermally viable in Prototype and marginal for tungsten in Demo. The deciding issues are tungsten damage evolution, lithium film survival and chamber clearing.

items.title: Residual dynamics determine dissipation in strongly coupled linear Langevin systems
items.summary: Interactions shape the properties of many physical and biological nonequilibrium systems, but whether collective operation raises or lowers entropy production remains difficult to predict. Here, we show that strong coupling suppresses irreversible circulation associated with the directly coupled degrees of freedom. In identical two-dimensional systems, this suppression is monotonic for nonzero coupling modes and guarantees a monotonic decrease of the entropy production rate (EPR), with the corresponding probability currents vanishing in the strong-coupling limit. In higher dimensions, suppressing the circulation associated with the coupled degrees of freedom does not generally eliminate all irreversible circulation, since the remaining degrees of freedom can still sustain nonequilibrium currents. The EPR of these residual dynamics sets the strong-coupling limit, providing a criterion for whether a given choice of coupled variables leads to lower dissipation than the uncoupled system. The approach to this limit depends on how the finite-coupling current correction aligns with the residual current. Further, we show that convergence to residual dynamics in the strong-coupling limit also applies to coupled non-identical systems. Finally, we demonstrate the predicted EPR reduction in nonlinear models of vertebrate hair-cell bundles and bacterial chemotaxis.

items.title: Superlinear cities, finite limits: Three characteristic scales of urban agglomeration
items.summary: Urban scaling research has established that many socioeconomic outputs increase superlinearly with city population, implying rising per-capita output. Although urban scaling models have incorporated infrastructural and dissipative costs, they have generally not identified the finite population scales implied by independently scaling benefits and diseconomies. We connect the classical urban-economic trade-off between agglomeration benefits and costs to a generalized scaling framework in which these quantities follow distinct power laws. When diseconomies scale more rapidly than benefits the model yields three ordered characteristic populations: the first (smallest) maximizes net benefit per capita; the second maximizes total net benefit; and the third (largest), at which aggregate benefits equal diseconomies. Their absolute values depend on the magnitudes of benefits and costs, but their relative separation depends only on the scaling exponents. We illustrate these relationships using published scaling estimates from several countries, and examine aggregate and extensive--intensive scaling across 102 Australian Significant Urban Areas. Aggregate employee income, rental payments and daily journey to work commuting distances for journeys scale superlinearly, although the aggregate rent--income exponent difference is statistically inconclusive. Mean rent per reporting renter household and estimated mean distance for daily commutes increase more rapidly with city population than mean employee income per earner. These findings reveal intensive differences obscured by aggregate scaling. The framework shows how superlinear agglomeration benefits can coexist with still faster-scaling diseconomies and produce finite characteristic urban scales without requiring benefits themselves to become sublinear.

items.title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-Driven Recurrent Motion of Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Skyrmions for Magnetic Clocking
items.summary: Magnetic skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets have emerged as attractive information carriers for spintronic technologies due to their compensated topology, which mitigates the skyrmion Hall effect and facilitates reliable current-driven transport. Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled Néel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. Under spin-orbit torque excitation, the SAF skyrmions exhibit resilient longitudinal transport with minimal transverse deflection using periodic boundary conditions. Periodic boundary conditions serve as an idealized model for closed-loop racetrack geometries, facilitating the study of continuous transport cycles and long-range steady-state dynamics. The oscillation frequency is readily modified by the applied current density and material characteristics, offering a pathway to field-free nanoscale timing components. Moreover, the threshold-activated initiation of recurrent transport mimics tonic-spiking behavior, indicating possible use in neuromorphic signal generation. This work establishes SAF skyrmions as versatile building elements for future spintronic functional devices by integrating topological protection, controllable transport, and cyclic dynamics.

items.title: Data-driven stochastic reconstruction of dengue epidemic dynamics: state-dependent stochasticity and temporal organization
items.summary: Dengue epidemics exhibit strong stochastic variability, temporal memory and complex temporal organization that are difficult to capture using conventional deterministic epidemic models. However, the dependence of epidemic fluctuations on the underlying dynamical state and their influence on reconstruction across temporal scales remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we develop a data-driven stochastic framework to investigate dengue epidemic dynamics using daily infection data from Imphal West District, Manipur, India, for 2023-2025. We use Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) to separate deterministic and stochastic epidemic components. Logarithmic regression and autocorrelation analyses reveal empirically state-dependent noise amplitudes and persistent temporal correlations, supporting a phenomenological description involving multiplicative, temporally structures stochasticity. Polynomial and logistic-type drift functions are subsequently fitted to the deterministic components and integrated to reconstruct the epidemic incidence trajectories. Although polynomial drift provides high in-sample agreement with the deterministic dynamics, complexity-entropy analysis reveals that the reconstruction depends on the epidemic year and the embedding delay. A paired circular moving-block bootstrap further demonstrates that observed minimizing delays exhibit different levels of stability across the various reconstructions and years. Finally, we conducted a noise-amplitude sensitivity analysis, and it reveals pronounced changes in the optimal embedding delay and minimum Euclidean distance in the complexity-entropy plane. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach to characterizing structured stochastic fluctuations and assessing the temporal organization of epidemic dynamics.

items.title: The impact of the sulfur allotropes and sulfur hydrides on the Venus cloud chemistry
items.summary: Venus is home to vivid sulfur chemistry, with SO$_2$ as the major sulfur gas species and a global cloud layer between 47 and~70 km composed of H$_2$SO$_4$ and H$_2$O. The chemistry in the clouds has been extensively studied with 1D models, but none is able to reproduce the three orders of magnitude decrease of SO$_2$ inside the clouds. Sulfur allotrope chemistry could be a candidate for buffering sulfur atoms, as it can grow into long chains. Sulfur hydrides such as H$_2$S is considered as one of the main sulfur-bearing compounds, possibly linked to surface reactions or have a volcanic origin like on Earth. In this study, we use for the first time a 3D model to study the climatology of the sulfur allotrope in gas and condensed phase and hydride chemistry in the clouds with an explicit photolysis calculation and updated UV cross-section. H$_2$S is close to ppmv levels below the cloud base, the third most abundant sulfur-bearing species in this region after SO$_2$ and OCS. Below the clouds, S$_8$ gas phase is the most abundant sulfur allotrope. Above, the photolysis and condensation are preponderant, and the gas phase decreases to extremely low values. Polysulfur can therefore not be the unknown absorber at cloud-top altitudes. The condensed phase polysulfurs are present from 30 to above 100~km. S$_2$ condensed phase is the most abundant due to its low saturation mixing ratios. Polysulfur species represent a substantial sulfur reservoir in the upper cloud, equivalent to a few ppmv.

items.title: Local Metrics for Exact Streaming on Curvilinear Lattices: A Curvilinear D3Q27 Cumulant Lattice-Boltzmann Method
items.summary: A three-dimensional curvilinear lattice-Boltzmann method is introduced for simulations on smoothly deformed grids while retaining exact one-to-one streaming on a uniform computational lattice. The coordinate transformation is represented locally through a metric-Gaussian equilibrium and a Christoffel-connection source in moment space. A dynamically reconstructed homogeneous-state perturbation streaming procedure preserves homogeneous physical states on warped meshes without interpolation in the advection step. The method is implemented on a D3Q27 lattice with a cumulant collision operator, while the geometric construction remains compatible with other local collision models. The formulation is assessed using two sets of tests. First, static non-orthogonal warped-cube cases validate the bulk curvilinear solver through a convected helical shear wave, the Taylor--Green vortex, and Arnold--Beltrami--Childress flow. These tests verify viscous decay, clean freestream preservation, vortex-breakdown dynamics, and the nonlinear inertial--pressure balance induced by geometric acceleration. Second, wall-bounded and moving-boundary demonstrations assess the boundary-compatible extension through warped plane Poiseuille flow, arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) peristaltic pumping, and a two-way fluid--structure interaction (FSI) case with added-mass frequency shift. The results show that the proposed curvilinear LBM avoids interpolation-based transport, reduces geometry-locked numerical modes, preserves global mass and momentum to round-off accuracy in the tested warped periodic cases, and extends to wall-bounded ALE/FSI configurations with conservative treatment of mass and physically consistent momentum exchange.

items.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
items.summary: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.

items.title: Descartes Curvature Geometry, Compact-Cycle Amplitudes, and the GST Cabibbo Seed
items.summary: Several apparently distinct formulations of the charged-lepton mass relation $p_2/e_1^2 = 2/3$ share a common algebraic object: the ratio of flavor-breaking to flavor-symmetric amplitude components on an internal family space. We show that (i) the relation expressed as a Fourier-mode constraint on Shulga's compact cycle, (ii) the same relation as a Descartes curvature condition in the sense of Kocik, and (iii) the Soddy completion of the resulting circle configuration are related by exact algebra, with no approximations. The Soddy completion defines a companion scale $F^2 = α^2 μ_\star$ with $α= \sqrt{3/2} - 1$ and $μ_\star = \sum_\ell m_\ell$; identifying this scale with $\bar{m}^{\rm MS}_s(μ_\star)$ yields a light-quark mass cascade with the ratio $m_d/m_s = 5/2 - \sqrt{6}$. Combined with the leading Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation, this gives the down-sector Cabibbo seed $\sqrt{m_d/m_s} = \sqrt{3/2} - 1 = 0.22474\ldots$, numerically close to the measured $|V_{us}| = 0.22503 \pm 0.00068$ ($0.4σ$). A full CKM evaluation requires the up-sector phase correction, which we defer. The correspondence is testable by future lattice QCD+QED determinations of $m_d/m_s$; explicit failure modes are listed.

items.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
items.summary: $^{99m}$Tc [t$_{1/2}$=6.0072 h, IT: 99.9963%, E_$γ$=140.51 keV (89%)] is the most widely used radionuclide for SPECT imaging. It is mainly obtained from $^{99}$Mo/$^{99m}$Tc generators, with $^{99}$Mo [t$_{1/2}$=65.924 h, $β^{-}$:100%] produced by fission of $^{235}$U in nuclear reactors. The aging of reactors dedicated to $^{99}$Mo production and increasingly frequent maintenance shutdowns highlight the need for alternative production routes. Among accelerator-based approaches, direct production of $^{99m}$Tc from enriched $^{100}$Mo targets using low-energy proton beams is particularly promising. Within a collaboration between the Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP) of the University of Bern and the Department of Nuclear and High Energy Physics of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, we investigated $^{99m}$Tc production with medical cyclotrons. Cross sections of proton-induced reactions on solid molybdenum targets were measured to characterise the Tc radionuclides produced during irradiation and optimise production conditions. Based on these data, a proton energy of approximately 16 MeV and a highly enriched $^{100}$Mo target of about 0.5 mm thickness were identified as suitable conditions. For a 10 h irradiation, these parameters provide a calculated $^{99m}$Tc yield of approximately 1.7 GBq/$μ$A while maintaining radionuclidic purity within European Pharmacopoeia limits. Production tests were subsequently performed to validate the measurements and demonstrate the feasibility of this production route.

items.title: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
items.summary: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware and thus trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QPPI), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information, and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. We validate the approach across simulations, static reference targets, fixed muscle tissue and living dynamically moving cells. QPPI enables all-optical and label-free studies of contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes. It provides both structural and functional readouts at sufficient frame rates to resolve fast cardiomyocyte contractions. Conventional fluorescent labels bleach over time, perturb physiology, and preclude long-term monitoring. Instead, QPPI enables long-term, label-free interrogation of dynamic cellular processes at quantitative contrast and provides structural readouts similar to those provided by established fluorescent labels, such as frame-by-frame sarcomere length. It also offers previously inaccessible measurements, like quantitative analysis of retardance changes during muscle contraction, which provides a direct optical signature of muscle photoelasticity.

items.title: Odd slip at chiral active surfaces
items.summary: Odd slip at solid-liquid interfaces, characterized by a velocity component perpendicular to the applied shear stress, introduces a novel class of odd transport phenomena with transverse momentum transfer at boundaries, distinct from odd viscosity, odd elasticity, or odd diffusivity. This effect arises on chiral active surfaces with persistent energy input and defined handedness, such as carpets of rotating biological or synthetic cilia with flexible anchoring. Although odd slip itself is dissipationless, its maintenance in active systems comes at an energetic cost, which we estimate from the microscopic model. With respect to its orientation dependence, odd slip can be classified as pseudo-scalar or pseudo-vectorial. We use a perturbative expansion to determine the resistance tensors of problems with different levels of broken symmetries. They reveal how the surface chirality and body asymmetry together violate the Onsager symmetry, but uphold the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity. Strikingly, suspensions of particles with odd slip embedded in a conventional Newtonian bulk fluid exhibit odd viscosity, providing a new minimal mechanism for its emergence beyond current microscopic models.

items.title: Integrated electro-optic attention nonlinearities for transformers
items.summary: Transformers achieve state-of-the-art performance in language processing and computer vision. Their computation increasingly depends on hardware that can keep pace not only with large matrix multiplications, but also with nonlinear operations like Softmax within the core attention mechanism. On digital accelerators, Softmax accounts for only a small fraction of total operations, yet it can disproportionately impact overall inference latency. Here, we use thin-film lithium niobate Mach-Zehnder modulators (MZM) as analog computing elements for low-latency Transformer attention. Our high-speed nonlinearities based on the intrinsic sinusoidal MZM response achieve performance close to digital baselines in Vision Transformers and GPT-2, even under 4-bit input and output quantization. We experimentally characterize the electro-optic response at symbol rates up to 10 GBaud and assess model robustness under corresponding noise conditions. Accounting for the full signal chain, our analysis indicates more than an order of magnitude lower latency relative to previous custom electronic and photonic Softmax implementations. These results establish analog electro-optic devices as nonlinear function units well suited for integration into emerging co-packaged electronic-photonic hardware, offering a path toward high-speed Transformer inference.

items.title: Impact of Cumulus Parameterization and Cloud Microphysics on WRF Simulation of an Extreme Rainfall Event over Maharashtra, India: A 3 by 3 Factorial Assessment
items.summary: Simulating extreme monsoon rainfall over the Konkan coast and Western Ghats remains challenging at 9 km resolution, where convection is partly resolved and partly parameterised. This study evaluates the sensitivity of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations of the 5-7 July 2026 Maharashtra rainfall event to cumulus and cloud microphysics schemes. Nine simulations employed a 3 x 3 factorial design combining WSM6, WDM6 and Thompson microphysics with Kain-Fritsch, Tiedtke and Grell-Freitas cumulus schemes. Rainfall was evaluated against IMD 0.25-degree gridded observations, with IMERG and ERA5 as additional references. A descriptive factorial decomposition showed that cumulus parameterisation accounted for 97.3% of across-experiment variation in mean rainfall, 88.2% in RMSE and 84.7% in spatial correlation, while microphysics contributed 2.0%, 2.1% and 9.3%, respectively. Kain-Fritsch produced the highest spatial correlations (0.533-0.581) but substantially overestimated rainfall. Tiedtke achieved the smallest mean biases and RMSE, although compensating regional errors concealed a 28-34% rainfall deficit over the Konkan-Ghats belt and substantial underestimation on 7 July. Grell-Freitas showed large wet biases and relatively high RMSE. All nine simulations displaced the event-total rainfall maximum approximately 140-195 km northward. WSM6-Tiedtke achieved the lowest RMSE, whereas Thompson-Kain-Fritsch better represented the rainfall spatial pattern. The findings demonstrate that, for this event and fixed model configuration, cumulus parameterisation exerted substantially greater influence on simulated rainfall than cloud microphysics. However, a single-event, single-member experimental design does not establish a universally optimal physics configuration.

items.title: Wall modes in rotating penetrative internally heated convection
items.summary: Rotating internally heated convection has been studied almost exclusively in laterally periodic domains, which cannot support the sidewall-attached modes that appear for sufficient rotation rates in rotating Rayleigh--Bénard convection in containers. We conduct direct numerical simulations of internally heated convection with isothermal plates and an adiabatic sidewall in cylinders of aspect ratio $Γ= 1/2$, $1$, and $2$ at $\Ra = 10^8$ and $\Pran = 1$, comparing them with a doubly periodic layer. When rotation is strong enough to stabilise the flow in a doubly periodic layer at the same $R$ ($\Ek \lessapprox 2 \times 10^{-5}$), the cylinders continue transporting heat via a wall mode down to $\Ek = 5.62 \times 10^{-6}$. This mode consists of a wave attached to the sidewall, with a radial thickness of roughly $0.03$ layer depths independent of $Γ$, leaving a stationary interior. Although unstable stratification is confined to the upper half of the conductive state, the mode also penetrates the lower half while retaining stable mean stratification in the measured lower-layer interval. Its azimuthal wavenumber scales roughly with $Γ$, yielding a wall parallel wavelength on the order of the layer depth, and it drifts retrograde as a rigid wave slower in wider cylinders and at lower $\Ek$. Analogous to rotating Rayleigh--Bénard convection, the wall modes reported here extend the observed range of sustained convection relative to the periodic reference and may complicate experimental comparisons.

items.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and the noise emission directivity. This leads to over-conservative policies and unexploited wind power. Yet, turbine yaw can simultaneously affect wake interactions and the direction of noise emission, offering an additional degree of freedom for farm-level noise control. We therefore propose Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximise farm power while satisfying a local noise constraint in a defined region. To enable training at a reduced computational cost, a low-fidelity acoustic model is coupled with the steady-state FLORIS simulator. The RL agent effectively learns how to redirect wakes and noise directivity away from the protected region while redistributing power across the farm. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfies the 40 dB noise constraint throughout the full range of turbulent winds, with an average power deficit of only 2% relative to greedy unimpeded control, and up to 7.7% at high wind speeds. In comparison, the industry-standard noise-reduced operation (NRO) baseline here generates an average power loss of 17%. When deployed in the higher-fidelity FAST.Farm simulator, the policy largely retains its performance under steady and turbulent inflow, despite differences in simulation fidelity. These results demonstrate the potential of combining yaw control and power derating through RL to improve the power-noise trade-off in wind farm operation.

items.title: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the EAST tokamak
items.summary: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) is reported in this work. In this regime, internal transport barriers(ITBs) and a flat core safety factor profile were maintained simultaneously by fishbone modes. First,the drive of low-frequency flows by fishbone modes is clarified, which subsequently suppresses turbulence transport. Besides, fishbone-induced poloidally symmetric (m = 0) toroidal current sheets were first reported experimentally, which drive outward current redistribution that mitigates core current peaking. Together, these effects enable hybrid operation with stable ITBs and robust magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability, revealing a self-organized pathway for sustaining hybrid scenario for fusion reactors.

items.title: Can future reirradiation justify upfront proton therapy? An extension of model-based proton therapy selection beyond primary-course NTCP benefit
items.summary: Objective: Current model-based proton therapy selection values normal tissue sparing only through its immediate reduction in normal tissue complication probability (NTCP). If reirradiation later adds further dose to the normal tissue, sparing achieved during primary treatment may become more clinically valuable. We investigated whether, and under which conditions, this contingent benefit could justify upfront proton therapy. Approach: We formulated a reirradiation-aware criterion that weights the NTCP benefits of upfront proton therapy after primary treatment alone or followed by reirradiation by their respective probabilities. Proton therapy is recommended when the expected benefit reaches a referral threshold T. Assuming a common logistic NTCP model for both scenarios, we derived screening conditions from the paired primary photon and proton plans to identify patients for whom future reirradiation could justify additional referral. We then quantified the minimum reirradiation probability and admissible added risk-score contributions for additional referral, and mapped referral patterns across primary profiles and reirradiation scenarios. Main results: Additional referral occurred for patients with substantial primary normal tissue sparing but a small immediate NTCP reduction because both plans lay on a flat region of the NTCP curve. In these cases, reirradiation could add sufficient normal tissue dose for the retained sparing to yield a larger NTCP benefit. Higher reirradiation probability expanded eligibility, whereas greater exposure could reduce the NTCP benefit as both predictions approached saturation. Significance: The proposed framework identifies well-defined patient profiles for which upfront proton therapy may be justified even if the NTCP benefit of proton therapy in the first treatment is below the threshold T.

items.title: sft-wick: A formalism and package for Feynman-diagram expansion and evaluation in stochastic field theories
items.summary: When stochastic field dynamics are cast into a path-integral formulation, perturbation theory becomes systematic but the resulting expansion quickly grows combinatorially large. The setting targeted here includes fields with several components and several dimensions, matrix propagators, tensor-valued couplings, and non-Gaussian driving noise specified by arbitrary n-point cumulants. Wick pairings grow factorially, and component indices must be routed through the tensor-valued vertices. The useful output is not a raw contraction list, but a diagram table: one entry per topology, with multiplicities, coupling sums, signs, and causal constraints resolved. We present sft-wick, an open-source Python package that constructs these diagram tables and computes their integrals numerically. Given an action and an observable, it enumerates topologically distinct Feynman diagrams, derives their algebraic coefficients, and evaluates the resulting diagram integrals from user-supplied response and cumulant functions. The core algorithm enumerates spatial topologies before routing component indices, avoiding contraction-by-contraction Wick expansion. Response-field constraints, including vanishing response-response contractions, the Ito prescription, and the absence of causal response loops, are enforced during enumeration. Predictions are validated against direct Langevin simulations in two worked examples, with Gaussian and with non-Gaussian driving noise, and agree with the simulations within stated error budgets.

items.title: Quantum theory of photonic vortices and quantum statistics of twisted photons
items.summary: The topological charge of a photonic vortex is an essential quantity in singular optics and the critical parameter to characterize the vorticity of twisted light. However, the definition of the photonic topological charge remains elusive. Here we put forth a theoretical formalism to provide a comprehensive treatment of photonic vortices. We introduce quantum operators for the photon current density and helicity current density based on the continuity equations from the paraxial Helmholtz equation. Our formalism allows us to introduce flow velocity and circulation for photonic currents in parallel to their counterparts in superfluids. The quantized circulation of the photonic currents is conserved during propagation and it gives an explicit definition of the photonic topological charge as the winding number of a photonic vortex. In particular, we predict helicity current generated pure helicity vortices, in which the photon current vanishes. Finally, we show an interesting effect that the quantum statistics of twisted photon pairs are essentially determined by their spin states.

items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.summary: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

items.title: Advancing global crop simulations with differentiable modelling
items.summary: Global gridded crop models (GGCMs) are crucial for assessing the performance of food producing systems, for example under climate change or their contribution to environmental challenges. However, systematic calibration of their parameters remains a long-standing challenge. Persisting uncertainties in these parameters propagate into future crop projections, thereby affecting and potentially biasing food security assessments. Here we present a fully process-based differentiable GGCM implementation that offers a fundamentally new approach to parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, yield loss attribution, and management optimization. Using automatic differentiation, we optimize selected model parameters against site-scale carbon and water flux observations, reducing normalized root-mean-square errors at held-out sites by 24.8-36.2% compared to the default state-of-the-art model. Without calibration against yield data, the optimized model better captures detrended yield anomalies across 61.2-64.3% of global crop area and reduces low-yield errors by 3.4-43.5% for wheat, rice, maize and soybean. It also ranks among the best performers in comparison with GGCMI Phase 3 models. Future simulations show that calibration reduces the projected end-of-century rice production increase from 55.1% to 22.1% under SSP5-8.5. Parameter ensembles further reveal that parameterizations with comparable historical skill can produce markedly different future production responses. Beyond calibration, differentiability enables the attribution of crop losses under extreme events and supports the design of adaptive crop management strategies. For the 2018 European drought, we identify spring heat and water limitation as major contributors to wheat yield losses and develop more effective irrigation strategies for mitigating simulated regional yield losses.

items.title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
items.summary: In this paper we study the dynamics of relativistic detonation waves theoretically and numerically. The reaction is physically accounted for by an extra term in the definition of the total energy density and by an additional equation for the evolution of the mass fraction of the reactant, while leaving formally unmodified the equations of mass and energy-momentum conservation. In this way, the Rankine-Hugoniot relations maintain the same formal structure of the inert version. For the numerical solution we use a finite volume ALE scheme with a second order TVD space-time reconstruction for the homogeneous part of the system, where the mesh velocity is chosen equal to the shock speed, and we combine it through operator splitting with a locally implicit algorithm for the potentially stiff reaction source terms that arise in the equation of the reactant. We furthermore propose a particularly efficient algorithm for the conversion from the conserved to the primitive variables, which for the relativistic Euler equations is known to be nontrivial. Following this approach, we can successfully solve the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering profile of a relativistic detonation wave, up to Lorentz factors of the shock front $γ_s\sim 7$. Our analysis allowed us to highlight a new special relativistic effect, which has remained unnoticed so far. While in Newtonian detonations the Zel'dovich pressure jump decreases monotonically with the mass flux through the shock front, in the relativistic case it shows a minimum and then rises monotonically as a function of the mass flux. This may have interesting physical implications on the amount of energy that can be extracted from a relativistic detonation wave.

items.title: 4D sensitivity kernels for infrasound atmospheric propagation: considering the need and impact of time dependent observation operators for acoustic wave observations in data assimilation methods
items.summary: The long range propagation of acoustic waves in Earth's atmosphere is sensitive to winds and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Thus, infrasound observations have a strong potential to improve numerical weather models by data assimilation methods. However, because acoustic waves propagate slowly, the atmospheric parameters can change during the propagation of the acoustic waves. This change of atmosphere properties is usually not taken into account by infrasound simulation tools which generally assume stationary atmosphere models. In order to close this modeling gap, we present here a method to compute the linear sensitivities of infrasound observables to atmospheric parameters varying both in space and time. We show that adjoint based methods can easily handle this computation of 4D sensitivity kernels, also called time variable observation operators in the data assimilation community. Then, we discuss the capabilities of various data assimilation methods to handle such observation operators. We demonstrate that only variational methods with data assimilation windows longer than the propagation duration of the long range infrasound can accommodate these observations, as well as their ensemble counterparts. Finally, we demonstrate the benefit of assimilating such long range infrasound observations, and we quantify the relative impact of linear approximation of observation operators and stationary approximation of the atmosphere model by assimilating propagation time observations of circumnavigating Lamb waves in Lorenz'96 low-order model. The results of this data assimilation experiment demonstrate that the time variability of atmospheric parameters should be taken into account even for infrasound propagation times limited to 2 or 3 time steps of the atmosphere model.

items.title: Quantum structured light: Non-classical spin texture of twisted single-photon pulses
items.summary: Classical structured light with controlled polarization and orbital angular momentum (OAM) of electromagnetic waves has varied applications in optical trapping, bio-sensing, optical communications and quantum simulations. The classical electromagnetic theory of such structured light beams and pulses have advanced significantly over the last two decades. However, a framework for the quantum density of spin and OAM for single-photons remains elusive. Here, we develop a theoretical framework and put forth the concept of quantum structured light for space-time wavepackets at the single-photon level. Our work marks a paradigm shift beyond scalar-field theory as well as the paraxial approximation and can be utilized to study the quantum properties of the spin and OAM of all classes of twisted quantum light pulses. We capture the uncertainty in full three-dimensional (3D) projections of vector spin demonstrating their quantum behavior beyond the conventional concept of classical polarization. Even in laser beams with high OAM along the propagation direction, we predict the existence of large OAM quantum fluctuations in the transverse plane which can be verified experimentally. We show that the spin density generates modulated helical texture beyond the paraxial limit and exhibits distinct statistics for Fock-state vs. coherent-state twisted pulses. We introduce the quantum correlator of photon spin density to characterize the nonlocal spin noise providing a rigorous parallel with fermionic spin noise operators. Our work paves the way for quantum spin-OAM physics in twisted single photon pulses and also opens explorations for new phases of light with long-range spin order.

items.title: Inverse Design of Integrated Photonic Components for Visible-Light Applications
items.summary: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) operating in the visible spectral range are crucial for quantum technologies, optical sensing, and nonlinear optics applications. However, their development is hampered by limited integration density and operational bandwidth, linked to low refractive index contrast and restricted parameter space in intuition-based PIC design. We address these bottlenecks with an adjoint-based, fabrication-aware inverse design workflow tailored for visible-spectrum photonics. By expanding the capabilities of FDTDX, an open-source, GPU-accelerated FDTD solver, we provide a versatile memory and runtime efficient inverse design platform. Demonstrating this approach on a silicon nitride (Si3N4) platform, we design, fabricate, and experimentally validate ultra-compact, broadband components for light routing, multiplexing, and polarization control. This work provides a scalable framework for high-density, high-performance visible-light PICs.

items.title: On dependence of the source deactivation factor on the magnitude of main earthquake shock
items.summary: We have discovered an inverse relationship between the earthquake source deactivation coefficient and the magnitude of the main shock. Recently, this pattern was confirmed through an analysis of earthquakes in the Central Himalayas (Poudel et al., 2026). On the one hand, independent confirmation of a previously unknown pattern strengthens our confidence in the relevance of the phenomenological theory of aftershocks, upon which we have based our method for processing and analyzing aftershocks. On the other hand, Poudel et al. (2026) presented our method in a distorted manner. Poudel et al. mistakenly believe that our method is based on a modified Omori law. Both circumstances provide an occasion and a basis for a simple and clear explanation of the essence of our approach to the study of aftershocks. First and foremost, our approach to the problem is diametrically opposed to Omori approach. Omori law and its modification, proposed by Hirano and Utsu, describe the decay of aftershocks. In contrast, we formulated and solved the inverse problem. The essence of the inverse problem lies in the need to calculate the source deactivation coefficient based on aftershock observation data, without making any prior assumptions regarding the law governing the decay of aftershocks. A crucial concept in our theory is the rather complex notion of the proper time of a source. Proper time differs radically from astronomical time. The paper describes the continuous and discrete representations of proper time. This paper is methodological in nature and may prove useful to researchers studying the dynamics of an earthquake source following the formation of a main rupture within the rock mass. Keywords: earthquake source, main shock, relaxation, deactivation coefficient, proper time, inverse problem.

items.title: Seismic background mitigation with the Lunar Gravitational-wave Antenna
items.summary: Lunar gravitational-wave (GW) detectors relying on the measurement of the response of the Moon to GWs are susceptible to a seismic background, which might pose a fundamental sensitivity limitation. The Lunar Gravitational-wave Antenna (LGWA) was conceived as an array of accelerometers with the idea that data can be processed to distinguish between a GW signal and the seismic background. As a result, the seismic noise of the GW measurement would be mitigated. However, so far, no quantitative assessment of the mitigation of the seismic background has been provided. In this article, we derive the analytical expressions for the optimal squared signal-to-noise ratio for a two-station array in an isotropic, random, Gaussian seismic field. Our numerical analysis reveals that the capacity to mitigate the seismic noise critically depends on the distance between the two stations relative to the seismic-correlation length. We demonstrate that optimal placement of the two stations can yield significant improvements in the equivalent seismic noise amplitude spectral density (ASD), approximately a factor of 2.3 at 0.3 Hz, compared to the measurement with a single station in the seismic-noise-dominated limit. The equivalent ASD of the seismic noise also exhibits distinct oscillatory and mitigation features arising from the Bessel-function structure of the noise correlation.

items.title: Learning the solution operator of standing waves with a Fourier neural operator
items.summary: The standing wave problem concerns the space-time periodic motion at the free surface of a two-dimensional, infinitely deep, irrotational flow of an incompressible inviscid fluid under gravity. Although spectrally accurate computations have revealed a rich array of nonlinear wave phenomena, repeatedly evaluating their evolution over large parameter spaces remains challenging, particularly when resolving fine-scale spatial oscillations. We employ a Fourier neural operator (FNO) architecture to learn the solution operator along a numerically computed one-parameter family of symmetric standing waves. Given a wave profile at an instant of rest and a normalized observation time, the learned operator predicts the fluid surface, the velocity potential and the dipole density at the surface at that time. In-distribution tests yield uniformly small relative errors within the training range. Two out-of-distribution experiments characterize extrapolation toward contrasting physical regimes. Toward the free-fall limit, errors concentrate near the sharpening crest, consistent with the spectral truncation in the FNO architecture. Toward the linear limit, absolute errors remain small whereas relative errors increase as the amplitude vanishes. A residual of the governing equations, evaluated independently of reference solutions, complements these tests and provides a diagnostic for exploratory predictions beyond the available data.

items.title: Antisymmetric thermopower without magnetism in three-phase composites
items.summary: A thermopower that turns a temperature gradient into a perpendicular electric field in every in-plane direction has relied on magnetism. Reciprocity permits it without magnetism, yet under a three-fold or higher axis it vanishes both in reciprocal elastic band transport and in composites of two isotropic phases with ideal interfaces. Here we show that composites of three isotropic phases carry it, and that under such an axis three is the minimum. A third, linearly independent transport matrix escapes the exact two-phase reduction; at weak contrast the first allowed axial term is cubic, proportional to a determinant of the three matrices times material-weighted, handed three-point correlations. Treating the phases as colours identifies the arrangements that allow the response, and crystal nets from reticular chemistry supply printable three-dimensional ones. Certified two-sided bounds give axial Seebeck coefficients of 49.5-50.2 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a planar cell and 76-84 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a printable woodpile; reflections in planes containing the axis reverse the response, and recolouring 24 nets to restore their parent symmetry switches it off. Around a line heat source the axial driving field has the $1/r$ azimuthal form of the magnetic field of a straight wire and drives circulating currents.

items.title: Temperature-Dependent Performance of NaI(Tl) Crystal with Dual-Channel SiPM Readout for Low-Mass Dark Matter Searches
items.summary: We report the first temperature-dependent characterization of a NaI(Tl) crystal readout by two silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) directly coupled to opposite ends of the crystal for rare-event searches. A $6 \text{ mm} \times 6 \text{ mm} \times 13 \text{ mm}$ NaI(Tl) crystal was directly coupled to two SiPMs and characterized in a liquid nitrogen-cooled cryostat over a temperature range of 94$-$293 K. The light yield, energy resolution, and scintillation decay time were measured using $γ$-ray peak from a $^{241}$Am source. After correcting for optical crosstalk contributions, the light yield increased, reaching $17.7 \pm 1.1$ photoelectrons/keV at 238 K, corresponding to a 34.5% enhancement relative to room temperature (293 K). Furthermore, dual-channel configuration effectively suppresses random thermal noise via coincidence triggers, which together with the observed increase in light yield, provides a critical pathway toward lowering the energy threshold for dark matter and coherent elastic neutrino$-$nucleus scattering searches.

items.title: Dissolution-induced mode transition of crack propagation in carbonate rocks: From brittle fracture to diffuse damage
items.summary: In chemically reactive environments, the mechanical integrity of geomaterials is fundamentally compromised by solid matrix dissolution. In this study, we propose a fully coupled chemo-mechanical phase-field framework to capture the dynamic interplay between mineral dissolution and fracture propagation. A key feature of the proposed model is the dynamic coupling of local mass removal to the fracture length scale, while also incorporating the damage-accelerated reaction-diffusion processes. Our results capture the development of an enlarged fracture process zone driven by chemical mass removal. This chemically induced widening blunts the sharp crack tip, alleviating the near-tip stress concentrations and causing a pronounced degradation in material stiffness before failure. Furthermore, we reveal a distinct ductilization effect, characterized by a more gradual accumulation of damage and a delayed onset of macroscopic failure. We show that the transition between brittle and ductile failure modes is dictated by the competing timescales of chemical degradation and mechanical deformation. Highly acidic environments enhance matrix dissolution and promote ductile fracture, whereas rapid mechanical loading limits chemical interaction and preserves brittle failure mode.

items.title: Generalized Onsager-Regularized Lattice Boltzmann framework
items.summary: This work presents a novel strategy to address Navier-Stokes modelling errors arising on first-nearest neighbour lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods and introduces fully local corrections through Onsager-Regularized (OReg) non-equilibrium populations. The proposed mechanism, which admits partially and completely corrected OReg models, is used to develop representative partially and completely corrected models for the six-moment-constrained guided equilibrium (GEq) representation on the D2Q9 lattice. The former realization only addresses compatibility condition violations and improves the accuracy by two/four orders of magnitude at reference/arbitrary lattice temperatures respectively, while the latter additionally corrects stress tensor modelling errors, resulting in a fully corrected exact model. Numerical benchmarks of the corrected schemes demonstrate improved accuracy and stability in comparison to the Lattice-BGK, regularized, and uncorrected OReg-GEq schemes thus presenting a promising avenue for OReg based thermohydrodynamic extensions.

items.title: A Non-Foster Superconducting Broadband Matching Network
items.summary: The nonlinear inductance of the Josephson junction has enabled the development of a wide range of continuous-variable amplifiers and qubit-based devices with unprecedented sensitivity. We present an alternative use of the Josephson junction in the context of broadband impedance matching. The idea poses a potential solution to a longstanding problem in the field of high energy particle physics. The axion, a compelling candidate for the dark matter, converts to a weak electromagnetic signal at an as-yet unknown frequency. As such, the ideal axion detector does not compromise bandwidth for sensitivity, a trade-off intrinsic to all linear, time-invariant and passive circuits. We propose a circuit that uses a Josephson junction in an impedance matching network to overcome these gain-bandwidth constraints and increase the scan rate of axion searches. The Josephson junction can be biased to exhibit negative inductance capable of canceling geometric inductance similar to a capacitor but across a wider frequency range.

items.title: Development of a real-time FPGA-based CNN trigger operating on full-granularity calorimeter images
items.summary: We present a real-time field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for event classification on full calorimeter images that retain crystal-level shower information. To meet the resource and latency constraints of trigger electronics, the network parameters and hidden activations were quantized to 8 bits with quantization-aware training, and a lossless space-to-depth reorganization rearranged the input image into fewer spatial positions, reducing the estimated CNN inference latency by more than an order of magnitude. The approach was evaluated with the J-PARC KOTO detector, recorded data, and data-acquisition (DAQ) constraints as a benchmark, targeting the online separation of the rare $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ decay from its dominant $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ background. As a proof of principle, the firmware was implemented and validated on an AMD Versal Premium VPK120 evaluation board. On 100,000 test events, inference on the board rejected $(99.34\pm0.04)\%$ of the recorded background sample enriched in $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ decays at a nominal $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ efficiency of 95%, with a measured CNN inference latency of 17.9 $μ$s. Combining the measured image-assembly and CNN inference latencies with the estimated link-transfer and score-return times gives a projected end-to-end latency of 25.9 $μ$s, within the adopted 32 $μ$s DAQ latency budget. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using full-granularity calorimeter images for CNN-based event selection that achieves high background rejection while keeping the trigger latency within tens of microseconds.

items.title: Fast diagonalization for matrix-free inversion of the nodal even-parity operator in hybrid finite element SPN transport
items.summary: The hybrid finite element method stores a dense inverse of the nodal even-parity operator for every node and energy group, and that storage limits the spatial and angular expansion orders, more tightly still on a GPU, whose memory is smaller than that of a host. This work introduces fast diagonalization for the nodal even-parity operator of the hybrid finite element SPN method: the stored dense inverse is replaced by the eigendecompositions of a planar, an axial and an angular factor, and the inverse is applied without being formed explicitly. Every even-parity moment of the SPN equations obeys an equation of the same diffusion form, with no mixed derivatives, so the angular coupling is the same in every spatial direction. On a node extruded along the axis, the operator is then an exact Kronecker sum of the three factors. The factorization merely recasts the computation, so the discretization and the solution are unchanged, and the nodes are not required to be identical to one another. The method is implemented for CPU and GPU hardware and compared with the dense inverse within one solver. On a pressurized water reactor core in SP3, the two paths agree to within round-off error, the storage falls from 3.76 GB to 821 kB, and the calculation is 4.15 times faster. On a 33-group fast reactor core, the dense inverse would occupy 24.9 GB and the dense path would need more memory than both the device and the host provide, whereas the factors occupy only 1.26 MB, so the solution can be obtained. The factorization thus reduces the storage of the nodal inverse by more than three orders of magnitude and brings multigroup core calculations at their required spatial expansion orders within the memory of a single GPU.

items.title: Particle-dependent radioluminescence color response of Eu-doped CaF$_2$ associated with energy-loss density
items.summary: Europium-doped calcium fluoride (Eu:CaF$_2$) exhibits characteristic blue Eu$^{2+}$ and red Eu$^{3+}$ emissions. In our previous study, the Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ radioluminescence intensity ratio under $α$-particle irradiation was approximately twice that under X-ray irradiation. Here, we investigate the relationship between this emission ratio and energy-loss density using H, Li, C, and Ni ion beams produced by a tandem accelerator.
