items.title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
items.summary: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

items.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
items.summary: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.

items.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
items.summary: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$β$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.summary: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with near-optimal quadrature squeezing. The ability to generate a wide variety of Wigner-negative states with mature semiconductor technology opens promising opportunities for continuous-variable optical quantum technologies.

items.title: Fundamental Limit for One versus Two Point Sources Detection using Direct Imaging
items.summary: We consider the task of distinguishing between a single weak incoherent optical point source and two weak incoherent optical point sources located symmetrically about the first source. $θ$ is the separation between the two point sources scaled to the Point Spread Function (PSF) width in the image plane. Using an ideal focal plane array of intensity detectors (ideal direct imaging), we quantify the performance using the Bhattacharyya distance and find the scaling of its leading order term in terms of $θ$ in the sub-Rayleigh regime. A suite of previous analyses of this problem lacked a comprehensive analysis for when the amplitude spread function (ASF) of the imaging system has zeros and reported a scaling that we find to be incorrect. We complete this analysis by explicitly calculating the leading order term of the Bhattacharyya distance for ideal direct imaging with any ASF, for small $θ$ and show the difference in scaling based on the presence or absence of zeros in the ASF. This is similar to the ASF dependent performance in the task of estimating the separation between the two point sources and the task of detecting a change to an object. We then apply our results to the specific example of a Gaussian and a Sinc ASF and show good agreement with numerical calculations. Our results allow the accurate comparison of other measurement schemes with ideal direct imaging, and to the quantum limit.

items.title: A Kinetic Study of the Interactions of an Acoustic Vibrating Surface with Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Instabilities
items.summary: The response of Mack mode instabilities to a simple acoustic vibrating surface (AVS) is studied using the Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method to capture and analyze spontaneous second-mode instability growth. The DSMC simulations, analyzed with the Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method, model flow over a flat plate at an unseeded freestream Mach number of 6 and unit Reynolds number $Re_1\sim 1.18\times10^7$ m$^{-1}$. Power spectral density (PSD) analysis was found to identify the dominant frequencies of 200 to 500 kHz, in line with linear stability theory (LST) predictions. Closed-form kinetic-theory expressions were derived to predict the amplitude of the DSMC fluctuations in the window-averaged snapshots. It was observed that the DSMC-simulated flowfield naturally developed second Mack mode instabilities without any external seeding, i.e., arising spontaneously from the kinetic fluctuations of the simulated gas and of amplitude higher than the predicted DSMC fluctuations. Targeted interaction with these flow instabilities is demonstrated for an AVS, where forcing at the unstable frequency of 250 kHz results in amplified waves downstream, while at the stable frequency of 400 kHz AVS-induced disturbances are damped. The AVS thus excites only the waves at its forcing frequency, leaving the instability waves at other frequencies and the mean flow essentially unaltered. The ability of the kinetic simulations to capture and describe linear perturbations at Reynolds numbers corresponding to those of Mach 6 flight at altitudes of $\sim 20$ km suggests that DSMC provides a theoretical understanding of controlling laminar-turbulent transition through AVS materials in hypersonic boundary layers.

items.title: Nonthermal Particle Acceleration by Magnetic Pumping in Pulsating Plasmas
items.summary: We present a new pulsating box setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression--expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results could be relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in certain high-beta space and astrophysical plasmas.

items.title: Relativistic Chiral MHD with application to the early Universe
items.summary: We present a systematic derivation of the equations of relativistic chiral magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) for a plasma of charged fermions in an expanding universe. Through a combination of a coordinate transformation and a rescaling of the dynamical variables, we bring the full system to the same form as in the Minkowski metric, with the Hubble expansion surviving only in the chirality-flipping rate and the kinematic viscosity. Retaining all four contributions to both the electric and the axial current yields terms absent from standard chiral MHD: charge-density corrections to the evolution equations for the chemical potentials, and an electric current proportional to the charge chemical potential $μ$ and the bulk velocity. The latter is mandated by current conservation, requires no chirality imbalance, and drives the charge-flow instability studied in a follow-up paper. For the radiation-dominated era, we evaluate all the coefficients in physical units and use them to estimate the magnetic Reynolds number, the attainable magnetic field strength, and the minimum temperature at which the chiral dynamo can operate. The resulting equations are cast in a form ready for direct numerical implementation.

items.title: QMOMKit: A C++ library for quadrature-based moment methods
items.summary: QMOMKit is an open-source C++ library for the phase-space evolution of population balance equations with quadrature-based moment methods. The present version implements the quadrature method of moments (QMOM) and the conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM). QMOMKit is designed to be independent of any particular application and can be used either as a standalone solver for spatially homogeneous population models or as a local phase-space solver coupled to a host application. It handles the numerical aspects of the evolution of a population in phase space, including quadrature reconstruction, advection of the quadrature abscissas, and changes to the population through moment sources and phase-space boundary contributions. The number of quadrature nodes is adapted to what the supplied moments support, subject to prescribed bounds of the phase-space coordinates, and the CQMOM implementation supports an arbitrary number of phase-space dimensions as well as any conditioning order. The principal numerical algorithms of QMOMKit are verified against analytical and manufactured solutions. Standalone spatially homogeneous applications, ranging from aerosol evaporation to particle dynamics and fragmentation, are compared with Monte Carlo solutions of the same population models, while coupling examples with OpenFOAM and deal.II demonstrate how QMOMKit can be embedded in finite-volume and discontinuous-Galerkin simulation frameworks. Together, these capabilities provide a tested and reusable foundation for a wide range of population-balance problems, and a basis for extending QMOMKit to other quadrature-based moment methods.

items.title: Towards operational data-driven regional weather forecasting: extreme-event skill and near-real-time verification with HRRRCast
items.summary: Improving convective-scale skill in data-driven regional weather models requires better representing rare high-impact events, training at native resolution, broadening variable output, and demonstrating performance in real-time settings. Here, we evaluate these challenges using HRRRCast, a data-driven convection-allowing emulator trained on the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) analysis data. HRRRCast combines native 3-km training, moderate sigmoid-weighted loss reweighting for reflectivity and precipitation, and broader system improvements including expansion of the training archive from 3 to 9 years (2016--2025), increased vertical resolution, expanded outputs, and architectural upgrades. The weighted loss improves high-threshold skill while preserving common-event behavior. Native-resolution training avoids aliasing from 6-km subsampling and substantially improves fractions skill score at convective scales, with gains that persist across pooling windows. HRRRCast has also been running in near-real-time mode for the past year. In seven months of independent observation-based verification, HRRRCast ensemble means improve several near-surface metrics relative to operational HRRR and maintain strong precipitation and reflectivity performance. Single-member reflectivity skill is strongest at 20--30 dBZ; at 40 dBZ, skill is near parity at 6-km pooling and better at pooling radii $\geq$30 km. Precipitation skill remains competitive through 1 in/h and extends to about 3 in/h in the best recent configuration. A focused comparison with HREF further shows useful low-cost probabilistic guidance for 3-h precipitation. At storm scale, HRRRCast exhibits a displacement--structure trade-off, with generally better storm placement than storm morphology.

items.title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
items.summary: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. This formulation organizes PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture. The resulting framework provides design principles for free-electron modulators that can control energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces, establishing LEM as a device-level platform for programmable femtosecond-to-attosecond matter-wave control.

items.title: Quantum circuit simulation with high-order optical tensor processing
items.summary: Classical simulation is essential for developing and testing quantum circuits, but the exponential growth of Hilbert space challenges conventional digital processors. Here, we introduce a classical optical quantum simulation architecture that treats gates and batches of input states as independent tensor dimensions rather than separate simulation instances, while mapping eligible tensor network contractions onto the same processor. Using co-designed multidimensional encoding and readout across spatial and wavelength degrees of freedom, we experimentally realize high-order tensor-matrix multiplication in a single propagation and process all computational-basis inputs for each 4-qubit gate. Using a physics-based optical propagation model, we further numerically evaluate the architecture for the Deutsch algorithm and for the tensor network of all 128 target instances of a 7-qubit Grover algorithm. These results establish a unified framework for gate-state batch and tensor network simulation, providing a route to exploit optical concurrency across quantum simulation tasks.

items.title: Enabling quantum communication in ultra-large-scale networks
items.summary: The recent development of small-scale quantum networks poses the question of which network-level mechanisms could enable quantum communication to operate at scale in a future Quantum Internet. The question can be answered within a well-established framework where a quantum network is mapped into a classical weighted graph, and communication reliability is assessed using methods from network theory. Previous work relied on this framework to determine sufficient conditions for viable network-wide communication only on special network topologies, such as regular lattices, and to devise communication protocols applicable only to small- and moderate-sized real networks. Here, we overcome both limitations by introducing a family of quantum communication protocols that scale to networks with hundreds of millions of nodes. We show that the competition between increasing communication distance and path redundancy determines their large-scale behavior, and that degree heterogeneity can provide sufficient redundancy to sustain communication in small-world networks. These conclusions are supported by a systematic analysis of both real network topologies and synthetic networks, and an analytical treatment in the limit of infinitely large random scale-free graphs.

items.title: A generative foundation model for 2D magnetized plasma turbulence
items.summary: We present a proof-of-principle study demonstrating a conditional generative foundation model for self-organizing magnetized plasma turbulence. Built on a multichannel flow-matching framework with a spectral decomposition strategy, the model is trained on direct numerical simulations of 2D modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (MHW) turbulence across the hydrodynamic to adiabatic parameter range. Without retraining, this \textit{single} model successfully performs three distinct downstream tasks: (i) unconditional generation of statistically faithful quasi-steady-state snapshots that recover the directional energy spectra and amplitude statistics, from which statistical transport quantities, including turbulent flux and effective diffusivity, alongside their uncertainties, are inferred directly; (ii) super-resolution from $4\times$ and $8\times$ downsampled observations to reconstruct fine-scale turbulence and large-scale zonal structures; and (iii) full-field inpainting from sparse spatial observations covering as little as $\sim 10\%$ of the domain. The generated fields faithfully reproduce regime-dependent turbulence vs. zonal-flow states and energy partitioning. Under extreme sparsity the long-correlation zonal flows are pinned by only a handful of observations, while the residual uncertainty concentrates in the small-scale turbulent fluctuations. These results establish flow-matching generative models as powerful, unified surrogates for state generation, statistical inference, and sparse-data reconstruction, providing a scalable baseline for 3D plasma turbulence and experimental applications.

items.title: RPAx Instabilities from Ground- and Excited-State References
items.summary: Random-phase approximation with exchange (RPAx) calculations based on ground- or excited-state references can yield complex excitation energies, causing the corresponding RPAx correlation energy to become complex as well. In this work, we investigate the origin of these complex energies using \ce{H2} in the 6-31G basis set as a minimal model. For the ground-state restricted Hartree-Fock reference, complex roots emerge at the well-known triplet instability associated with the appearance of a lower-lying unrestricted, symmetry-broken solution. For excited-state references, we identify two distinct mechanisms leading to complex excitation energies. The first is similarly associated with symmetry breaking. The second arises when a positive-energy excitation becomes degenerate with the positive-energy de-excitation associated with a negative-energy transition. Finally, we demonstrate the practical implications of these findings for spin-flip Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations of cyclobutadiene and state-specific core-ionization calculations for selected systems. These examples show that, in the absence of the relevant instabilities, methods sharing the generalized eigenvalue structure of RPAx can be applied to excited-state references without resorting to the Tamm-Dancoff or core-valence separation approximations, while retaining real excitation energies.

items.title: Attenuation of shoaling extreme wave crests by artificial salt marshes
items.summary: Laboratory experiments in a wave flume investigated the attenuation of shoaling extreme waves by artificial salt marshes placed immediately before an abrupt depth transition. Increasing vegetation density systematically reduced the excess kurtosis of the surface elevation distribution in the intermediate water depth regime. Nonetheless, attenuation exhibits a short saturation regime at low vegetation densities, whereas at very high densities, excess kurtosis decreases significantly across the gauges. However, kurtosis attenuation becomes ineffective as waves approach shallow-water conditions or as second-order nonlinear effects become significant. Furthermore, the highest experimental densities where the kurtosis is tamed exceed typical natural salt marsh stem densities. Thus, in natural settings, salt marshes are likely to provide only partial mitigation of extreme wave statistics in intermediate and shallow water depths, as the wave field retains some hazardous nonlinearity.

items.title: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
items.summary: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

items.title: Urban scaling and the dynamics of individual cities
items.summary: Cities are often compared through scaling laws, usually expressed as power-law relations between population size and aggregate urban quantities related to infrastructure, socioeconomic activity, or environmental impacts. These laws are influential because their exponent is often interpreted as describing what happens when a city grows, with implications for urban theory, planning, and policy. Here, we show that this interpretation is generally misleading. An exponent measured by comparing many cities at one date does not, in general, describe the trajectory of any individual city. Instead, it reflects a statistical pattern produced by cities with different histories, constraints, institutions, and growth paths. Apparent sublinear or superlinear scaling can therefore arise even when individual cities follow simpler dynamics, as we show for the area--population relation. Cross-sectional scaling laws can reveal system-level regularities, but should not be used alone to infer growth mechanisms or guide policy for a given city.

items.title: Rapid Vacuum Response Calculations for Non-axisymmetric Plasma Geometries
items.summary: We present a fast, open-source calculation of the vacuum response matrix and surface inductance in non-axisymmetric geometries capable of running with up to 10^5 boundary points in tens of seconds on a laptop. Ideal magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) stability modeling for free boundary modes requires the perturbed vacuum energy. We extend the VACUUM code to non-axisymmetric geometries in the new Julia implementation of the Generalized Perturbed Equilibrium Code, combining a collocation approach to the boundary integral equations with a high-order singularity correction scheme. The correction is recast into explicit quadrature weights acting on the collocation values, which allows the corrected operator to be assembled explicitly rather than applied to a given surface field, and the structure of that matrix under field-period and stellarator symmetry is then exploited to reduce storage and solve cost. We find that the vacuum response matrix converges at fourth order or greater in the grid spacing, reaching a given accuracy on a coarser grid than previous implementations without the high-order method. The non-axisymmetric calculation converges to the axisymmetric VACUUM result for a tokamak and the CAS3D result for a W7-X stellarator equilibrium. This work enables fast free boundary ideal MHD stability and perturbed equilibrium calculations in stellarators.

items.title: Iterative Construction of n-Dimensional Navier-Stokes Solutions with Non-Gradient Convection
items.summary: Exact periodic solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations arise when the convective field is a pure gradient and can be absorbed into the pressure. We construct solutions outside this class, in arbitrary spatial dimension, by an iteration in which each step solves a linear diffusion problem forced by the transverse part of the preceding convective field. The construction is dimension-independent, and for a cyclic family of initial fields the first two iterates are available in closed form. Carried out numerically in three dimensions, the iteration converges: at Re = 10 successive iterates contract with an observed factor 0.43 and the limit is a fixed point of the discretised map to a relative defect of 8.2 x 10^-5. The observed factor exceeds unity by Re = 30, which identifies the practical range of the iteration rather than a proved convergence boundary. We also show what goes wrong when the projection is omitted, as it was in an earlier iteration of the author's: the iterates cease to be divergence-free and an apparent growth appears that belongs to the expansion and not to the flow. For an n-dimensional generalisation of the initial field the fraction of the convective field not absorbed by pressure is exactly 2*sqrt(2)/3 in every dimension n >= 3, and the longitudinal fraction exactly 1/3. The divergence of each returned source is a sharp diagnostic, failing by sixteen orders of magnitude at the step where the projection is omitted; the cell kinetic energy is a weaker one, detecting gross failure only.

items.title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
items.summary: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.

items.title: Ensemble-size-dependence of deep-learning post-processing methods that minimize an (un)fair score: motivating examples and a proof-of-concept solution
items.summary: Fair scores reward ensemble forecast members that behave like samples from the same distribution as the verifying observations. They are therefore an attractive choice as loss functions to train data-driven ensemble forecasts or post-processing methods when large training ensembles are either unavailable or computationally prohibitive. The adjusted continuous ranked probability score (aCRPS) is a fair and ensemble-size-unbiased scoring rule when applied to ensembles with forecast members that are interpretable as conditionally independent draws from an underlying predictive distribution. However, distribution-aware post-processing methods that introduce structural dependency between members can violate this assumption, such that aCRPS no longer functions as a fair scoring rule. We demonstrate this effect using two approaches designed to minimize the expected aCRPS of a finite ensemble: (1) a linear member-by-member calibration, which couples members through a common dependency on the sample ensemble mean, and (2) a deep-learning method, which couples members via transformer self-attention across the ensemble dimension. In both cases, the results are sensitive to ensemble size and apparent gains in aCRPS can correspond to systematic unreliability characterized by over-dispersion. We introduce trajectory transformers as a proof-of-concept that ensemble-size independence can be achieved. This approach is an adaptation of the Post-processing Ensembles with Transformers (PoET) framework and applies self-attention over lead time while preserving the conditional independence required by aCRPS. When applied to weekly mean $T_{2m}$ forecasts from the ECMWF subseasonal forecasting system, this approach successfully reduces systematic model biases whilst also improving or maintaining forecast reliability regardless of the ensemble size used in training or real-time forecasts.

items.title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
items.summary: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

items.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
items.summary: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm B}/ω_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $Ω_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $Ω_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm p}/ω_0$; $ω_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

items.title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution with Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application to NGC 4486B
items.summary: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model. For a one-dimensional Airy slice we achieve an explicit multi-ratio separation inversion. For the physical two-dimensional circular-pupil PSF we obtain exact finite-pupil overlap integrals and locally invertible separation responses. Motivated by these analytical invariants, we examine Airy-informed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic Airy images with known separations. At 150,000 training images, the approximate mean absolute errors are 0.018 in plotted separation units, 10 times better comparing to 0.18 for non-Airy Gaussian PSF approximation. Applied to an archival Hubble Space Telescope image of the double nucleus of NGC 4486B, the Airy-informed CNN gives estimates of approximately 9.6--12.0 pc for training sets of 100,000--150,000 images, broadly consistent with the historical approximately 12 pc value. We distinguish exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator and identify the limits imposed by PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure.

items.title: Deriving the second law of thermodynamics and exploring its boundaries
items.summary: The second law of thermodynamics still lacks a general proof applicable to classical and quantum systems across broad ranges of degrees of nonequilibrium, particle interactions, and time scales. In this paper, we show that from Boltzmann's assumption of equal a priori probabilities, the second law naturally emerges via the phase-space continuity equation for the macrostate-level probability $f$ defined over fixed $Ω$-intervals, where $Ω$ is the number of microstates. Further analysis suggests a more general assumption underlying the second law: $f$ increases monotonically with $Ω$, i.e., $\partial f/\partial Ω> 0$. Based on these findings, the second law can be readily derived for fully chaotic systems. The derivation does not rely on dynamical details, highlighting the statistical nature of entropy increase. For the dilute hard-sphere gas model considered in the H-theorem, the second law may also be established through a simplified approach that requires the Boltzmann equation but does not use the H-function. In contrast, if the positive correlation between $f$ and $Ω$ breaks down, i.e., $\partial f/\partial Ω\leq 0$ (e.g., because of local nonchaoticity), the second law of thermodynamics may not apply: entropy can decrease spontaneously with no energetic penalty, and the system can reach an intrinsic-nonequilibrium steady state.

items.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
items.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

items.title: The Kubo-Thermalization Correspondence
items.summary: Quantum thermalization describes how interacting quantum systems relax toward thermal equilibrium, a central problem in modern physics. Yet most experimental information on many-body systems comes from short-time transition spectroscopy, typically interpreted within Kubo's linear-response framework. These perspectives-long-time equilibration versus short-time response-seem fundamentally disconnected. Here we establish an exact link between them: the \emph{Kubo-Thermalization correspondence}, which connects long-time thermalized magnetization under weak driving to short-time linear-response spectra for a spin coupled to a thermal bath. The correspondence holds even when the steady state differs substantially from the initial state and when each regime is individually difficult to describe theoretically. We experimentally confirm the correspondence using effective spin-$1/2$ impurities realized with ultracold fermions in two internal states coupled to a Fermi sea. Our results provide a rare exact statement about quantum thermalization and offer a novel route to infer thermalization dynamics from equilibrium response measurements in strongly interacting quantum systems, independent of microscopic details of the system--bath coupling.

items.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
items.summary: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

items.title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
items.summary: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.

items.title: Improving Signals, Declining Encoder: A Known-Answer Test of Label-Free Monitoring in Self-Supervised Learning
items.summary: Self-supervised training is monitored without labels, through the loss and statistics of the learned features. We report a case where we know the encoders lost part of what they had learned, so we can check whether these signals noticed. We trained LeJEPA encoders on synthetic images with known generating factors. In nine of ten seeds, the readability of those factors fell abruptly and stayed down, nearly always along the same direction in factor space. Meanwhile the loss kept falling, and most of the eleven label-free signals we tracked kept improving and rated the declining runs better than runs that did not decline. Standard change-point detection rarely flagged the decline near its onset, and selecting checkpoints by these signals mostly chose ones after it.

items.title: CrystalREPA: Transferring Physical Priors from Universal MLIPs to Crystal Generative Models
items.summary: Crystal generative models mainly learn what stable crystals look like, with little explicit supervision for what makes them stable. We reveal a substantial representation gap between state-of-the-art crystal generative models and pretrained universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) via energy probing, and show this gap can be closed by a simple training-time alignment. We propose Crystal REPresentation Alignment (CrystalREPA), a plug-and-play framework that aligns the atom-wise hidden states of generative encoders with frozen MLIP representations through an element-aware contrastive objective, transferring stability-aware atomistic priors with marginal training overhead and no additional inference cost. Across three generative frameworks, ten MLIP teachers, and two benchmark datasets, CrystalREPA consistently improves the thermodynamic stability, structural validity, and structural fidelity of generated crystals. Equally important, we find that an MLIP's transfer effectiveness is poorly predicted by its accuracy on standard leaderboards (e.g., Matbench Discovery) but strongly predicted by the distinguishability of its atom-wise representation space, yielding a practical, accuracy-independent criterion for selecting MLIP teachers for generative transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/Chengqian-Zhang/CrystalREPA.

items.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
items.summary: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.

items.title: SU(2)-Equivariant Spinor Message Passing for Molecular Magnetism
items.summary: Predicting molecular magnetic properties often requires costly electronic-structure calculations that account for spin-orbit coupling. Inspired by the spinor nature of the underlying electronic states, we introduce eSpinor, an SU(2)-equivariant graph neural network that propagates spinor features alongside the integer-rank tensors used in conventional equivariant models. We initialize spinors from eigenvectors of an approximate Hamiltonian that includes spin-orbit coupling. The network preserves their rotation laws and makes predictions independent of arbitrary eigenbasis choices. Comparisons with geometry-only and Hamiltonian-informed baselines assess the benefit of this architecture beyond supplying electronic information. On cobalt single-molecule magnet candidates, eSpinor improves magnetic anisotropy predictions, including for unseen ligands. It also improves excitation-energy predictions for dysprosium candidates with unseen ligands, extending the benefit to rotationally invariant scalar targets. For a dysprosium magnetic resonance imaging probe, it predicts real electron-spin correlations and low-field nuclear relaxation rates more accurately despite static crystal-field errors similar to the Hamiltonian-informed baseline. This dynamical advantage extends from water to methanol without retraining. These results support spinor message passing as a useful inductive bias for molecular magnetism in the tested systems and show why model selection should be guided by accuracy on the intended physical observables.

items.title: Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (DRE): A Radiometric Measure of Electric Light Source Efficiency
items.summary: Photopic luminous efficacy (lm/W) weights optical power strictly against human eye sensitivity V (lambda), creating a systemic metrological penalty for electric light sources engineered with broad spectral output in the ultraviolet (280-380 nm) or infrared (780-4000 nm) bands. Similarly, metrics evaluating chromaticity, color quality, or melanopic pathways assess photoreceptor responses strictly within the visual band, offering no measure of broad-spectrum physical radiant power conversion. To resolve this limitation, we introduce Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE), a radiometric framework that evaluates how efficiently an electric light source converts electrical power into an optical spectrum matching natural terrestrial daylight across domain Omega = [280 nm, 4000 nm]. The framework factorizes performance into primary physical quantities: domain-restricted Wall-Plug Efficiency (eta_wall [W_optical/W_elec]), measuring unweighted electrical-to-optical conversion, and Daylight Spectral Fidelity (eta_spec [unitless, 0-1]), quantifying geometric shape match to the ASTM G173 AM1.5G solar reference via total variation distance (1 - TVD). Multiplying total optical power by spectral fidelity yields the absolute Daylight-Referenced Output Power (P_dr [W]), establishing a direct physical flux quantity for lighting specification. Dividing by electrical drive power gives the summary metric Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE = eta_wall * eta_spec [W/W_elec]), measuring net reference-conforming radiant output per electrical Watt consumed. The mathematical architecture is reference-agnostic, domain-extensible, and maintains provable lower-bound monotonicity for eta_wall and eta_DRE under spectral truncation. Open-source reference software is provided to facilitate deployment and standardized rating of broad-spectrum light sources.

items.title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
items.summary: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.

items.title: State-augmented deep reinforcement learning for active flow control around an elliptical cylinder
items.summary: We employ reinforcement learning algorithms to develop control strategies for manipulating synthetic jets on an elliptical cylinder, targeting robust flow control across varying aspect ratios (Ar). Our results show that for high aspect ratios (Ar = 1 and 0.75), the learned strategies effectively mitigate vortex shedding, achieving drag reductions of 13.4% and 20.1%, respectively. As the Ar decreases, more complex wake dynamics challenge flow control. For Ar = 0.5 and 0.25, drag reductions of 26.88% and 30.37% are achieved, though vortex suppression becomes increasingly difficult. For extremely slender cylinders (Ar = 0.1), we enhance control performance by enriching dynamic feature representation and using Kalman filtering for state estimation. Unlike conventional methods, our approach successfully achieves complete vortex shedding suppression, a maximum drag reduction of 32.2%, and eliminates periodic oscillations, stabilizing the flow. These results demonstrate the efficacy of state-enhanced RL in controlling highly slender geometries.

items.title: Critical velocity and dissipation mechanism in finite superfluid $^4$He nanodroplets
items.summary: A hallmark of superfluidity is the frictionless motion of an object below the Landau critical velocity; Whether this concept applies to nanoscale droplets remains unclear. Using time-dependent density functional theory, we investigate the motion of a sodium atom on the surface and inside a superfluid helium nanodroplet. For surface motion, we identify a critical velocity above which energy dissipation through ripplon excitation and the formation of surface-bound quantized vortices leads to rapid deceleration. Inside the droplet, the atom is slowed down to a steady-state velocity that depends on the initial speed, contrasting experiments reporting a critical velocity for dopants ejected from droplets [Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 153002 (2013)]. Remarkably, the velocity of the ejected atom is nearly independent of its initial velocity. We demonstrate that this behavior results from the bursting of the bubble surrounding the atom at the droplet surface, challenging the previous experimental interpretation.

items.title: GNN-VIEW: Visual Inspection and Explanation of Graph-based Earth-System Models
items.summary: Machine learning Earth-system models are becoming increasingly important, and so is their development. Graph-based models, one of the most prominent approaches, allow developers to constrain the learning process before training via graph connectivity. Yet, developing these models remains challenging: the graph is built algorithmically with little intuition about the final result beyond static plotting, which requires extra work and is often not detailed enough. Even after successful training, how the model arrives at forecasts remains obscure. We present GNN-VIEW, an interactive browser-based tool that supports the development of such systems. GNN-VIEW exposes the graph's information pathways, allowing model developers to debug the graph structure before training. After training, GNN-VIEW uses attribution-based explainability to reveal which input features are used by the trained model for a given forecast. This helps developers understand why a model fails. We showcase the usefulness of GNN-VIEW in the construction stage of a graph for an ocean forecasting model, and in explaining poorly predicted precipitation of a trained weather forecasting model during Hurricane Laura.

items.title: Nuclear recoil effects with a realistic nuclear charge form factor
items.summary: We introduce a novel two-parameter Gamma model of the nuclear charge distribution as an alternative to the widely used Fermi distribution. The model yields simple analytical formulas for all moments of the charge distribution and closed-form expressions for the electrostatic potential and momentum-space form factor, the latter satisfying the correct analyticity requirements for a physical charged particle. We apply the model to calculate the nuclear recoil correction to the Lamb shift in electronic and muonic atoms and analyze its nuclear-model dependence. We find that the nuclear-size recoil corrections to energy levels of heavy muonic atoms are strongly sensitive to higher moments of the nuclear charge distribution, highlighting the importance of realistic nuclear modeling. To facilitate further calculations, we also provide the Fortran code RECFNS, designed for computing the nuclear recoil correction within the QED framework. The present work establishes a basis for future extensions to higher orders in the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio, hyperfine splitting, and radiative corrections.

items.title: Interference between multiple photoionization pathways in chiral molecules: Converging continuum results in Gaussian bases
items.summary: An accurate description of photoionization observables is a central challenge for theoretical models of molecular photoionization. Within standard electronic-structure approaches, the continuum states are represented by unoccupied Hartree-Fock orbitals expanded in Gaussian basis sets. Since these basis sets are optimized for bound states, computed observables may exhibit a noticeable basis-set dependence. Here, we augment these basis sets with diffuse functions and investigate the convergence of photoelectron circular dichroism (PECD), anisotropy parameters, and the forward backward ionization time delay in the multiphoton ionization of randomly oriented methyloxirane molecules. All observables converge systematically with the number of added diffuse functions, resolving previously observed basis-set discrepancies and indicating that the augmented basis sets provide a more accurate representation of the intermediate continuum states. In particular, our fully ab initio calculations yield forward-backward time delays in qualitative agreement with recent measurements, for which previous theoretical descriptions relied on empirical modeling. Diffuse augmentation thus provides a computationally efficient and transferable route to converged Gaussian-basis calculations for molecular multiphoton photoionization.

items.title: Toward fully stabilized flow control using deep reinforcement learning
items.summary: This study enhances the performance of flow control across various synthetic jet configurations by improving deep reinforcement learning techniques. The training results based on the foundational deep reinforcement learning framework indicate that as the Reynolds number increases, the effectiveness of synthetic jet control becomes increasingly sensitive to the position of the jet. When synthetic jets are positioned near the flow separation region, the control strategy consistently exhibits excellent performance. However, when synthetic jets are located farther from the separation region, the flow control performance diminishes, and the consumption of external energy increases. By enhancing dynamic state features and reshaping the reward function, we significantly improve control performance across various Reynolds numbers and synthetic jet positions. With the optimized framework, we achieve significant drag reduction effects ranging from 8% to 34% within the Reynolds number range of 100 to 400. The flow control strategy is capable of simultaneously achieving multiple control objectives, including reducing drag, suppressing lift, eliminating vortex shedding, and decreasing energy consumption. These findings highlight the potential of optimizing deep reinforcement learning frameworks to achieve more adaptive flow control strategies for various flow scenarios.

items.title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
items.summary: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

items.title: Information-thermodynamic principles unveil the response of complex networks to perturbations
items.summary: Understanding how complex networks respond to perturbations is key to uncovering their functional organization. We show that, for a maximum-entropy perturbation prior, standard diffusion cannot increase response entropy, a measure of the diversity of the system's response. To overcome this limitation, we develop a density-matrix-based information thermodynamics of perturbation responses along arbitrary dynamical trajectories. We show that this framework is grounded in an information-theoretic principle of least dissipation and introduces a generalized free energy that quantifies deviations from an instantaneous diffusive reference. We then illustrate the formalism using nonlinear complex networks, revealing regimes of enhanced response diversity that cannot be captured by standard diffusive descriptions.

items.title: Derivation of OH sum rules without Rayleigh--Jeans approximation: a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants
items.summary: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH $Λ$-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the $^{2}Π_{1/2}$ $J{=}1/2$ level, which has three transitions only, because its $F{=}0{\leftrightarrow}0$ line is strictly forbidden. The relation is $τ_{S_1}(v)/μ_{S_1}^{2}+τ_{S_2}(v)/μ_{S_2}^{2}=τ_{M_1}(v)/(aμ_{M_1}^{2})+τ_{M_2}(v)/(bμ_{M_2}^{2})$, where $a=2J^{2}+J-1$, $b=2J^{2}+3J$, and the $μ_i^{2}$ are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein $A$ coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. We suggest that it is a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants.

items.title: Recovering topological information of light by topological learning
items.summary: The evolution of modern-day communication networks towards enhanced capacity and robustness is driving interest in topological light wave as a next-generation information carrier. However, harnessing its potential is hindered by the lack of an effective topological reader, particularly when strong disorder renders conventional readout intractable. Here we address this by introducing TOPO$^{2}$, an artificial intelligence framework that leverages on topological learning to recover topological information from light. We demonstrate it on highly distorted optical fields with embedded Skyrmion topologies, showing that we can extract the topological numbers in a single shot with just a conventional camera. We showcase its capability in a TOPO$^{2}$-based communication scheme, sending and recovering information encoded in a topological alphabet, confirming that it outperforms conventional approaches. Our connection of topological photonics with topological AI as a powerful paradigm for robust high-capacity information encoding and processing opens a new path towards topological information optics.

items.title: Plasma and light: Shaping High Harmonic Generation in Time-Varying Media
items.summary: High harmonic generation in solids is typically described under the assumption of a stationary medium. This assumption is rarely questioned because the electronic properties of most media evolve on timescales much slower than the harmonic emission process itself. However, in strongly driven time-varying transparent conductive oxides the plasma frequency, carrier density, and effective mass can evolve on the same femtosecond timescale as harmonic generation. Under these conditions, harmonic generation and material evolution are no longer independent processes. Within this context, we consider a two-field pumping scheme in which a strong field generates a comb of high-order harmonics across a broad spectral window, while a weaker field simultaneously reshapes its own individual spectral lines. Distinct from geometry-dependent wave-mixing processes, the evolving electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear harmonic channels simultaneously. A fully self-consistent hydrodynamic-Maxwell framework reveals that even- and odd-order harmonics naturally emerge from free- and bound-electron dynamics without the typical need to invoke phenomenological nonlinearities. Our model captures the full spectral evolution on an ultra-broad bandwidth, while experiments performed on ITO confirm the distinct behavior of bulk-driven odd harmonics and interface-driven even harmonics under strong pumping. These results establish time-dependent plasma dynamics as a powerful new tool for broadband hyperspectral shaping of multiple harmonic channels beyond the framework of four-wave-mixing processes. Our findings are of particular relevance to ultrafast science, with potential applications in ultrafast pulse manipulation and the generation and control of tailored multi harmonic waveforms.

items.title: Scale-Dependent Statistics of Coherent Magnetic Structures in Early IMAP Observations
items.summary: We analyze early Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) magnetic field observations (November 2025 to May 2026) to quantify the statistical properties of helical magnetic structures and their relationship with turbulence intermittency. Intermittent structures, such as current sheets, are identified using the Partial Variance of Increments (PVI) method, and the scale-dependent normalized magnetic helicity is computed over scales corresponding to 0.5-3 correlation lengths. Prior studies have typically applied the PVI-helicity method to individual events; here we extend this technique to the ensemble statistics of a multi-month sample spanning many correlation times. To separate coherent helical structures from random turbulent fluctuations, significance thresholds for helicity are determined using phase-randomized surrogate realizations. We find a clear scale dependence in the occurrence, duration, and waiting time of coherent magnetic helicity, reminiscent of the scale-transfer arguments underlying inverse cascade, selective decay, and Taylor relaxation theories. Event duration and waiting-time distributions are well described by power-law and exponential models over different ranges, consistent with previous findings. In addition, PVI and magnetic helicity are anticorrelated, suggesting that high-PVI regions are preferentially associated with the boundaries of flux ropes, while their interiors tend to exhibit lower PVI and stronger magnetic helicity.

items.title: Label-Free Finite-Volume-Residual Training of Attention Graph Neural Networks for Coupled Thermo-Fluid Fields
items.summary: Neural surrogates are widely used in scientific machine learning for fast prediction of three-dimensional (3D) thermo-fluid fields. However, generating training data using conventional numerical solvers often incurs substantial computational and storage costs. We propose to train an attention graph neural network by minimizing the finite-volume method (FVM) residuals of the governing equations. These residuals are evaluated directly on the mesh, requiring no labeled data. We evaluate the trained surrogates against computational fluid dynamics (CFD) references and a data-supervised baseline across four scenarios. On the two steady-state benchmarks, each solved on the same mesh as its CFD reference, the FVM-loss model reproduces the reference flow and temperature fields with mean field-averaged normalized root-mean-square errors (nRMSEs) near 3%, including the buoyancy-energy coupling. On the two parametric transient cases, the FVM-loss model attains lower rollout errors than the supervised baseline in almost every field, while avoiding the data-generation cost entirely. These results indicate that the FVM loss can provide a practical training signal for neural surrogates and reduce the model development cost.

items.title: Relativistic Space-Charge-Limited Current in Electrostatic Limit for a Finite-Width Diode with Arbitrary Injection Energy
items.summary: We develop a weakly relativistic and electrostatic formulation of space-charge-limited current (SCLC) with arbitrary injection energy, covering the accelerating-diode and drift-space regimes. The one-dimensional (1D) relativistic SCLC model is obtained from a stationary-current condition, which is validated against the numerical solutions. Based on this relativistic 1D SCLC model, we investigate two different approaches to account for the effects of finite emission area for a two-dimensional (2D) planar diode of a finite width of $W$, which is larger than the gap spacing $D$. The field-balance (FB) approach evaluates the opposing space-charge fields at the potential minimum, whereas the density-weighted (DW) approach uses the mean absolute distance of electrons from that minimum. The two approaches yield different corrections at finite injection energy, even in the non-relativistic limit, with FB model predicting a larger leading-order enhancement. DW model reproduces our previously published classical coefficient and the classical drift-space limit, whereas the FB model gives a different result. Note both approaches are identical for zero injection velocity. Comparisons with 2D electrostatic particle-in-cell (ES-PIC) simulations, it is found that FB and DW model show better agreement for higher injection energy (= gap voltage) at smaller and larger $W/D$ emission area respectively.

items.title: Lanthanide Crystal Field Theory in the J-Mixing Regime: $f^n$ Configurations
items.summary: The low-energy sector of the lanthanide $f^n$ shell is to first approximation governed by the interplay of three interactions: Coulomb repulsion, spin-same-orbit coupling and the ligand crystal field potential. To rationalize the energy landscape in different chemical environments, it is desirable to extract the phenomenological crystal field parameters from experimental data; however, in practice, high-dimensional fitting procedures complicate their routine determination. Here, we present a computational extraction procedure based on real tensorial sets and the $U(7)$ canonical chain that, unlike existing operator equivalent methods, takes all $J$ multiplets of the lowest-energy $LS$ term into account, ensuring meaningful results even in the presence of considerable $J$-mixing. Two series of lanthanide compounds, [Ln(III)(C$_8$H$_8$)$_2$]$^-$} and doped Ln(III):Y$_2$O$_3$} (Ln $\in$ {Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu}) serve as examples for high- ($D_{8h}$) and low-symmetry ($C_2$) scenarios. Consequences for the generalisation toward actinides are briefly discussed.

items.title: Shannon Entropy as an Order Parameter for the Two-Dimensional Confined Coulomb Systems: Exact Balance Law, Topological Charge Sum Rule, and Boundary Saturation
items.summary: We establish a complete information-theoretic framework for the minimum-energy configurations of the two-dimensional Thomson problem on a hard-wall disk, based on the Shannon entropy of the Voronoi topological charge distribution. Two exact identities are proven and verified to machine precision for all studied systems of size $N=12-10^5$. First, an entropy balance law decomposes the total entropy into bulk, boundary, and mixing contributions without approximation. Second, a topological charge sum rule fixes the total charge at twice the number of boundary particles plus six; together with the disjointness of bulk and boundary coordination sets $-$ justified analytically via the Delaunay empty-circumcircle criterion and elastic disclination splitting $-$ it relates the three- and four-coordinated boundary populations directly to the bulk charge. Applying Euler's theorem to the outermost Delaunay annulus yields an exact shell-mismatch identity: the four-coordinated boundary population equals the adjacent interior shell population, whereas the three-coordinated population equals their step mismatch, directly detecting third-shell nucleation at $N=30$. Furthermore, we prove that the boundary entropy is bounded by $\ln2$ and that its saturation is equivalent to the bulk charge per boundary particle approaching $-1/2$, a regime restricted self-consistently to boundaries of at least $12$ particles. Numerically, we locate bulk nucleation at $N=56$, maximal global disorder at $N=146$, and boundary saturation above $N\sim10^3$, with a direct extension to spherical geometry.

items.title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
items.summary: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).

items.title: Chirpons: elementary local phase oscillations associated with complex zeros
items.summary: For a complex wave, the local phase variation provides the instantaneous frequency in time, the local wavenumber in space, and the local momentum in quantum mechanics. Here we study this quantity from the complex-zero structure of the analytic continuation of the wave. A single nonreal zero produces a localized Lorentzian phase variation on the real axis, whose position, width, sign, amplitude, and integrated phase are fixed by the zero itself. We call this elementary zero-associated oscillation a chirpon. The representation is exact for finite products and finite Fourier sums, and extends to entire and band-limited functions through canonical factorization. We illustrate the construction with superoscillatory sequences and discrete Fourier sums, showing how local anomalous oscillations can be reconstructed from periodic families of complex zeros. We further show how linear systems transform chirpons through the displacement of their associated complex zeros, and illustrate this dynamics for quadratic dispersive propagation and a resonant harmonic oscillator. This establishes a direct relation between local phase structure and the amplitude and phase response of the transfer function, suggesting a zero-based form of spectroscopy in which system parameters can be inferred from the motion, width, and orientation of chirpons. More broadly, the chirpon description provides a unified framework for instantaneous frequency, local wavenumber, superoscillation, backflow, and other local phase phenomena, while offering a new route for probing linear systems through the dynamics of their complex zeros.

items.title: A low-volume cold-atom microwave clock with an additively manufactured cavity
items.summary: We present the performance of a compact microwave interrogated atomic clock based on laser cooled $^{87}$$\rm{Rb}$ atoms. The clock utilizes a micro-fabricated grating magneto-optical trap (gMOT) to cool and trap atoms, and an additively manufactured microwave cavity for microwave interrogation. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $370$ at a 1 Hz bandwidth and mid-term instability of $6.7\times10^{-14}$ at an averaging time of $τ=3 \times 10^{4}$ s. In addition, a low cost mu-metal foil has been implemented on the vacuum chamber to reduce the quadratic Zeeman shift which was previously limiting stability beyond $τ= 10$ s.

items.title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
items.summary: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel. In most practical situations, hyperspectral images are affected by spectral variability (SV) also known as intra-class variability, which is caused by different physical phenomena including atmospheric effects, intrinsic variability of the pure materials and illumination or topographic changes. Nevertheless, the standard hyperspectral unmixing methods that rely on the Linear Mixing Model (LMM) do not consider these phenomena. Thus, neglecting them will spread errors throughout the linear hyperspectral unmixing process. To avoid this problem, this paper proposes two hyperspectral unmixing algorithms dedicated to a parametric model called Structured Additive Variability LMM (SAV-LMM). This mixing model handles SV in an additive manner by incorporating two terms into the standard LMM. Moreover, the designed algorithms are based on Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) and optimize a cost function which integrates additional penalization accounting for SV. Furthermore, a novel improved initialization scheme, which takes SV into account, is proposed. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for linearly unmixing hyperspectral images with SV compared to the tested state-of-the-art methods.
