The uniqueness of cell cluster codes in SCM constitutes an important property of the model. Previous studies have demonstrated the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on this analysis of connected cluster code characteristics, this paper proves the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters. The proof results and the new concepts introduced in this study help further refine the spatial chromatic model and provide a theoretical foundation for its subsequent applications.

items.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
items.summary: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature. Moreover, we also construct several counterexamples to demonstrate that generally the assumptions in our criteria cannot be weakened while keeping the K-property.

items.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).

items.title: Truncated $\mathcal{H}_2$ Optimal Model Order Reduction for Bilinear Quadratic Output Systems
items.summary: We develop an $\mathcal{H}_2$ model reduction framework for polynomial bilinear systems with quadratic outputs. We define the associated $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm and show its consistency with the established norm in the original (non-polynomial) BQO case. We derive first-order necessary conditions for $\mathcal{H}_2$ optimal model reduction of these polynomial systems and use them to construct an efficient iterative algorithm for computing reduced BQO models that approximately satisfy these conditions. Numerical results on two examples demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed reduction approach.

items.title: Class numbers and finiteness of norm Euclidean quadratic lattices over algebraic number fields
items.summary: Let $F$ be an algebraic number field and $\mathcal{O}_{F}$ the ring of integers of $F$. Let $L$ be an integral $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattice of rank $n\ge1$ on an anisotropic quadratic space $V$. We prove that if $L$ is norm Euclidean, then $L$ is $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-maximal of class number one, and the class number of $F$ equals the class number of $L\perp\mathbf{H}$, where $\mathbf{H}$ is the hyperbolic lattice with quadratic form $xy$. Under the same assumption, $F$ has class number one if $n\ge3$ and at most two if $n=1,2$. We also prove finiteness up to isometry for totally definite norm Euclidean lattices over totally real number fields in ranks at least three as the field varies, in rank two for fixed field degree, and in rank one over a fixed field. This confirms Clark's finiteness conjecture in ranks at least three.

items.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
items.summary: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

items.title: A Framework for Supervised and Unsupervised Learning via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
items.summary: We introduce a unified framework for supervised and unsupervised learning through density estimation using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). To this end, we introduce the notion of a nested RKHS, that is, an increasing sequence of RKHSs whose union is dense in an ambient $L^2$-space. This construction allows us to exploit the computational structure of RKHS methods at each finite approximation level while preserving the approximation power of the entire $L^2$-space. We first study statistical learning in a fixed RKHS. In both unsupervised and supervised settings, we establish strong convergence results for empirical averages of random elements taking values in an RKHS continuously embedded in $L^2$. We then use the nested RKHS structure to combine these statistical convergence results with the density of the union of the RKHSs in the ambient $L^2$-space. We apply this construction to probability density estimation and binary Bayesian classification. For density estimation, we construct explicit empirical estimators of the orthogonal projections of the target density onto the RKHSs and establish their almost sure convergence. A diagonal selection procedure then yields a sequence of estimators converging almost surely to the target density in $L^2$. For binary Bayesian classification, we formulate the approximation of the Bayes target as the minimization of suitable population and empirical risk functionals. We prove consistency of the empirical minimizers and use the nested structure to obtain convergence towards the Bayes target in $L^2$. We further provide a geometric interpretation in terms of hyperplanes and weighted distances in the ambient $L^2$-space. Finally, we show that the population risk admits a direct probabilistic interpretation in terms of the probability of misclassification.

items.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
items.summary: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.

items.title: Analytical properties of $q$-metallic numbers
items.summary: For an integer $n\geq 1$, consider the $n$-th metallic number $φ_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$ (e.g. $φ_1$ is the golden number) and denote by $[φ_n]_q$ its $q$-deformation in the sense of S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko. This is an algebraic continued fraction which admits an expansion into a power series $[φ_n]_q =\sum_{l=0}^{+\infty} κ_l(φ_n) q^l$ around $q=0$, with integral coefficients. By using techniques from analytic combinatorics, we establish several properties of the sequence $( κ_l(φ_n))_{l\geq 0}$ of Taylor coefficients: characterisation by recurrences or by differential equations, closed-form expressions when $n=1,2,3$, and asymptotics. We also present some remarkable identities induced by the action of the modular group $PSL(2,Z)$ and address, mainly through computer experimentations, the question of the logarithmic behaviour of the sequence $( κ_l(φ_n))_{l\geq 0}$. A particular accent is put on the comparison between the $q$-deformation $[φ_1]_q$ of the golden ratio and RNA secondary structures, the former being actually a signed version of the latter. By doing so, we would be pleased to bring the interest of combinatoricians to the newly discovered world of $q$-numbers.

items.title: A zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions in the weight aspect
items.summary: In this paper, we prove a zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions associated with Hecke eigencuspforms in the weight aspect. The proofs are based on the mollified second moment of these $L$-functions.

items.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
items.summary: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.

items.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
items.summary: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$ with codimension of Jelonek set greater than one, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is neither homeomorphic to a line nor can have a single end at infinity.

items.title: A switching proximal gradient method for constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems
items.summary: We study difference-of-convex optimization problems with several composite inequality constraints and develop a majorization-guided switching proximal gradient (MGSPG) method. Specifically, at each feasible outer point, quadratic majorization and linearization yield a strongly convex composite surrogate problem. To solve this surrogate approximately, we employ a switching proximal gradient (SPG) method, which takes a proximal gradient step for the objective when the current point is nearly feasible and for a most violated constraint otherwise. This construction requires neither projection onto the joint surrogate feasible set nor multiplier computation. By establishing a common invariant ball and using an increasing weight argument, we obtain an \(O(τ^{-1})\) inner complexity bound for SPG. Building on this bound, we show that, under boundedness of the feasible level set and a uniform Slater condition for the surrogates, MGSPG finds an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) selected component proximal gradient updates. Numerical experiments on SCAD-constrained and groupwise-constrained regression problems demonstrate the viability and computational efficiency of our method compared with existing optimization algorithms.

items.title: Multifidelity variational inference for derivative-free PDE-constrained inverse problems
items.summary: We develop a multifidelity black-box variational inference (MF-BBVI) approach for PDE-constrained Bayesian inverse problems in which forward solves are expensive and PDE gradients are unavailable. The method is built on score-function estimators for the evidence lower bound (ELBO), which avoid differentiation through the PDE model but are known to suffer from high variance. To address this high variance, we employ multifidelity approximate control-variate estimators that combine a small number of high-fidelity samples with a larger number of low-fidelity samples to reduce estimator variance and the number of high-fidelity evaluations required for optimization. We further develop a PDE-derivative-free second-order optimization strategy based on both gradient and Hessian score-function estimators. For low-fidelity model generation, we propose an on-the-fly strategy that builds and adaptively updates a reduced-order model (ROM) as the variational distribution evolves throughout the optimization. We investigate strategies for adapting the ROM and estimating the approximate control-variate gains, examining tradeoffs between estimator bias, variance reduction, and computational cost. The resulting approach facilitates derivative-free variational inference for large-scale inverse problems through a reduction in overall computational cost. We demonstrate the method on four numerical examples: a linear benchmark with an exact posterior and three PDE-constrained inverse problems.

items.title: On $p$-Adic Valuation Trees Arising from Laplace Transform of Fibonacci Polynomials
items.summary: We study the $p$-adic valuation trees associated with the sequence \[ e_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}F_n(t)\,dt, \] obtained by evaluating the Laplace transforms of the Fibonacci polynomials at $1$. We answer an open question of Givens and Moll in the negative by constructing an explicit counterexample showing that even internal branches need not be simple. We then reformulate the Givens--Moll lifting criteria for the even and odd subsequences in terms of the roots and derivatives of two associated polynomials. In particular, simple roots modulo $p$ give rise to simple internal branches. Finally, we develop a recursive lifting procedure that determines the unique surviving residue class at each level of a branch associated with a simple root and computes the $p$-adic valuations of the corresponding terms.

items.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
items.summary: Many operations run on a budget that must rarely run out, such as a wear allowance. A wrapper keeps the remaining budget in the state, subtracts a barrier that grows as the budget shrinks and clips the combined reward from below at -m, and a standard policy-gradient learner trains unchanged. The clip level m is a price of failure risk, since the trained value splits exactly into utility before failure, the cost of a margin and the price times the risk, so whatever policy training returns earns the most such utility net of that cost among policies with no greater risk, up to its optimization error. Its risk exceeds a comparison policy's by at most order 1/m when charged costs stay bounded, and value or validation data certify it. The main theoretical result is exponential convergence of the population training flow under any parameter regularizer convex along the motions of the network's units and strong enough against the price, biased toward the prior policy. This extends mean-field convergence of policy gradients from relative entropy to weight decay, which covers continuous-time training of finite networks. Relative entropy adds noise that lets learning leave flat regions, weight decay pulls the parameters toward a reference, and action regularization bounds the risk change by the distance to a trusted rule. Experiments on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task measure the bounds' slack. We state when another method is better, without claiming this one outperforms them.

items.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
items.summary: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.

items.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
items.summary: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.

items.title: Sharp anticanonical volume bounds for Gorenstein Fano fourfold of Picard number one
items.summary: Let $X$ be a complex $\mathbb Q$-factorial Gorenstein Fano fourfold with $ρ(X)=1$. If $X$ has canonical singularities, we prove that $(-K_X)^4\le3528$, with equality if and only if $(X\simeq \mathbb P(1,1,12,28,42)$. In fact, $(-K_X)^4\ge3130$ already implies this isomorphism. If $X$ has terminal singularities, we prove the sharp bound $(-K_X)^4\le648$, with equality if and only if $X\simeq \mathbb P(1,1,1,1,2)$. In the canonical case, we also obtain the sharp bound $(-K_X)^4\le1024$ when a positive generator of $Cl(X)/ \mathrm{tors}$ is Cartier outside a finite set. The proofs use jet estimates involving all Harder--Narasimhan slopes of the tangent sheaf, the geometry of algebraic foliations, and the integrality of intersection numbers on a general leaf. The equality case in the canonical bound is determined by two computations of divisorial section rings.

items.title: Optimal Control of Scalar Diffusions with Finite Action Sets
items.summary: We study a scalar finite-horizon controlled diffusion with a finite action set. An action may affect the drift, the instantaneous variance, or both, and performance is assessed by a uniformly convex terminal deviation cost. The model represents systems in which decisions are made continuously in time but only finitely many operating settings are available. Under uniform nondegeneracy and an explicit shape condition on the terminal cost, we show that the value function is classical at positive times, establish global positive upper and lower bounds for its second state derivative, and prove that the ratio of its first and second state derivatives is strictly increasing. This ordering implies that each action's optimality region is connected, the active actions occur in monotone order, and adjacent regions are separated by unique switching boundaries. It also yields an exact coefficient-based screen that removes actions that cannot be optimal on any open state region. For smooth continuous-action benchmarks, both the value loss from restricting the action set and the additional loss from rounding the continuous optimal feedback to the nearest available action decrease quadratically with the action-set resolution. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting action screens, threshold policies, and implementation losses.

items.title: Derived categories of log del Pezzo surfaces with $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities
items.summary: Let $X$ be a log del Pezzo surface with only $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities. We compare the derived categories of its minimal resolution, canonical stack, and singular surface. For every family in the Corti--Heuberger classification, Orlov's blow-up formula and the Ishii--Ueda correspondence give explicit full exceptional collections on the canonical stacks, of length $12-K_X^2+\frac{4k}{3}$ when $X$ has $k$ singular points. In the one-point index-one cascade, the canonical stacks are blow-ups of the weighted projective stack $\mathbb P(1,1,3)$ at distinct smooth points and admit explicit full strong exceptional collections of line bundles. For quasismooth hypersurfaces $X_{10}\subset\mathbb P(1,2,3,5)$, we construct a full strong exceptional collection of $13$ objects with an explicitly computed Euler matrix. The exceptional lattice determines the Brauer group: $\mathrm{Br}(X)=0$ for $k\leq5$, while $\mathrm{Br}(X)\cong\mathbb Z/3$ for $k=6$. We construct semiorthogonal decompositions of $D^b(\mathrm{coh}\,X)$ for the one- and three-point cascades and of a Brauer-twisted derived category for the six-point cascade.

items.title: Universality Criterion Sets for Definite Quadratic Lattices over Polynomial Rings
items.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\neq 2$. Under suitable assumptions on the dimensions of anisotropic quadratic forms over $k$ and $k(x)$, we show that a definite integral quadratic form over the polynomial ring $k[x]$ is universal if the form represents all scalars from $k$ and all scalar multiples of $x$. The coefficient field $k$ in our main result can be a finite field, a non-dyadic higher local field, a global function field, or a one-variable function field over $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{C}(t)$. We have a finite universality criterion set over $k[x]$ for some coefficient fields $k$, including some cases where $k$ has infinitely many square classes (e.g., $k=\mathbb{C}(t)$).

items.title: Irrationality of the conjugacy growth on Heisenberg groups
items.summary: We demonstrate that the conjugacy growth series for the Heisenberg groups $H_n(\mathbb{Z})$ is never algebraic, irrespective of the generating set. This makes progress towards the conjecture that all finitely presented groups that are not virtually abelian have irrational conjugacy growth series. Contrary to the group $H_3(\mathbb{Z})$, where the conjugacy growth is $n^2\log(n)$, the conjugacy growth of the other Heisenberg groups is polynomial, making these groups the first known nilpotent groups where the irrationality does not follow from the asymptotic growth.

items.title: Demand Estimation with Unobserved Stockout Substitution: Exact Likelihood Maximization
items.summary: When a product is sold out, customers who prefer it may buy a substitute or leave without purchasing. Efficient demand estimation in this setting is challenging when inventory is observed only at replenishments, because the stockout times, and hence the products available to each customer, are unobserved. Estimating demand efficiently under stockout substitution has been a challenging problem since Anupindi et al. (1998), and it has become more pressing as the scale of such problem instances grows thanks to innovations in retailing such as unmanned stores. We provide a complete solution to this problem for the multinomial logit (MNL) model, the most widely used model of customer choice. Using a continuous-time representation of the purchase process developed in Zhou et al. (2026), we show that the exact likelihood and its gradient are one-dimensional integrals, no matter how many products, customers, or stockouts there are. Both can be evaluated at a cost linear in the numbers of products and periods. Our method estimates demand for 2,000 products from 2,000 selling periods in under ten minutes.

items.title: The window process of slightly subcritical frozen percolation
items.summary: We study the frozen percolation model on the complete graph $K_n$, where each edge appears at rate~$1/n$ and connected components are destroyed by lightning strikes hitting vertices at rate $λ_n$ (thus the rate at which a connected component is destroyed is linear in its size). We focus on the slightly subcritical sub-regime of the self-organized critical (SOC) regime, assuming $(\ln n)^{4/3}n^{-1/3} \ll λ_n \ll 1$. Our main object of study is the so-called window process, which allows us to study the fine details of the mechanism that drives the SOC behavior of this dynamic random graph. We prove two scaling limit theorems. First, we show that the fluctuations of the window process around its deterministic fluid limit converge to a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, whose mean-reverting property captures the SOC nature of the model. Second, by zooming in on a finer space-time scale, we prove that the scaled increments of the window process converge to a tempered stable Lévy process.

items.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
items.summary: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.

items.title: Solvable Lie Foliations on Compact Five-Manifolds: Classification, Cohomological Obstruction, and Non-Homogeneous Examples
items.summary: We study $\GA$-Lie foliations on compact five-manifolds. We establish a structural classification of the holonomy group $Γ$ into five types according to its algebraic structure inside $\GA$. For three of these types (I, II, IIIa) we prove homogeneity via Meigniez's theorem and the Matsumoto--Tsuchiya theorem. For Type~IIIb we prove non-homogeneity by exhibiting a non-polycyclic holonomy group, extending the Dathe--Ndiaye construction \cite{DN11}. We introduce a cohomological class $[F]\in H^2(Γ^{\mathrm{ab}},[Γ,Γ])$ as a \emph{necessary} obstruction to homogeneity: if $\mathcal{F}$ is homogeneous and $Γ$ is polycyclic then $[F]=0$. We show that Type IIIb foliations satisfy $[F]\neq 0$. For Type IIIc, we prove that certain foliations are non-homogeneous by a direct argument when the generating translations are $\Q(λ)$-linearly independent; we exhibit explicit homogeneous examples showing that this type is \emph{not} universally non-homogeneous. Finally, we construct the first known non-homogeneous $\mathrm{Sol}$-Lie foliation in dimension five by a verified lattice deformation.

items.title: The maximum size of intersecting $k$-graphs with covering number $k$
items.summary: Let $m(k)$ be the maximum size of an intersecting $k$-graph with covering number $k$. In the present paper, it is proved that for all $k>e^{32}$, \[ m(k)\ge k^k\exp\bigl(-50\sqrt{k\log k}\bigr). \] Together with Zakharov's upper bound \cite{Z}, this implies $m(k)=k^k\exp\bigl(-k^{1/2+o(1)}\bigr)$.

items.title: General position on Brauer--Severi surfaces
items.summary: The blowing-up of the projective plane at a finite set of points yields a del Pezzo surface if and only if the points lie in general position. In this note, we generalize this result to Brauer--Severi surfaces over arbitrary ground fields. Using Galois descent, intersection theory and combinatorial arguments, we provide explicit arithmetic and geometric conditions on the centre of the blowing-up.

items.title: Failure of local extension of semipositive metrics in a smooth projective family
items.summary: We construct a smooth projective family of rational surfaces and an effective line bundle on its total space that give a negative answer to Păun's metric-extension question. The restricted bundle on the central fibre carries a semipositively curved singular Hermitian metric with analytic and minimal singularities, but this metric admits no semipositive extension to any neighbourhood of the whole fibre, even up to singularity type. The construction uses four-point blow-ups of the plane, with three centres becoming collinear on the central fibre. This change produces a nonzero integrable adjoint section on the central fibre, whereas the corresponding adjoint systems vanish on nearby noncentral fibres. If a metric extension existed, an $L^2$ extension theorem would extend that section, contradicting this vanishing.

items.title: Equilibrium Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy under Non-Exponential Discounting
items.summary: This paper studies an infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend problem for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion with observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting gives rise to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier strategy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The proof relies on uniform estimates for a system of coupled boundary-value problems and the Poincaré-Miranda theorem. We also verify that the resulting strategy satisfies the equilibrium variational inequalities. Numerical results show that greater dispersion in discount rates, with the initial average discount rate held fixed, raises both barriers. The effect of switching intensity can be nonmonotone and may reverse the ordering of the barriers.

items.title: From Global Optimization to Exact Coordinates: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem on the Unit Square Using Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Optimization
items.summary: We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) approach for the Heilbronn triangle problem on the unit square. The formulation exploits the boundary structure of optimal configurations, which we establish rigorously, to fix coordinates and orientation variables a priori. With this formulation, a general-purpose global solver solves the case $n=9$ to global optimality within its numerical tolerances in about eight minutes on a laptop and without any precomputation, compared with about 23 hours of total computation for the best previous approach. The same model also solves $n=10$ for the first time, in under seven hours, and confirms the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002). The numerical solutions then guide an exact symbolic reconstruction, and the minimum triangle area of every reconstructed configuration is verified in exact arithmetic. This yields exact coordinates for all $n\le 10$, including the configurations of Comellas and Yebra (2002) for $n=9$ and $n=10$, together with rigorous lower bounds. Finally, we derive structural properties of optimal configurations, formulate a conjecture on the number of critical triangles, and pose an open question. All code and data are publicly available.

items.title: Perfect sampling of Ising spin glasses with bounding chains
items.summary: We study perfect sampling algorithms for Ising spin glasses based on coupling from the past and bounding chains, on several graph families and coupling distributions. For the single-site bounding chain, we establish coalescence in $O(n\log n)$ updates under Dobrushin conditions. On sparse random graphs, our numerical results suggest that efficient sampling extends throughout the tree-uniqueness regime, with a slowdown beyond this threshold. On Erdős-Rényi random graphs $\mathcal{G}(n,d/n)$ with standard Gaussian couplings, we introduce a block bounding chain and prove its coalescence in $O(n\log n)$ block updates in the tree-uniqueness regime for sufficiently large $d$, each block update requiring $O(n)$ operations, adapting a proof in~\cite{Efthymiou_Zampetakis_2024} for the rapid mixing of block Glauber dynamics. On periodic lattices, our experiments instead suggest that the single-site bounding chain is limited by the looseness of its bounding envelope, whereas on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, slow coalescence is accompanied by damage spreading at every inverse temperature tested. These observations motivate alternative bounding representations and couplings as strategies to improve perfect sampling on spin glasses.

items.title: A Constructive Method to Maximize Entropy under Marginal Constraints
items.summary: We study the problem of maximizing R{é}nyi entropy of order $2$ (equivalently, minimizing the index of coincidence) over the set of joint distributions with prescribed marginals. A closed-form optimizer is known under a feasibility condition on the marginals; we show that this condition is highly restrictive. We then provide an explicit construction of an optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals. Our approach characterizes the optimizer's structure and yields an iterative algorithm that terminates in finite time, returning an exact solution after at most $p-1$ updates, where $p$ is the number of rows.

items.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
items.summary: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

items.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
items.summary: Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone. The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4ε^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $ε$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.

items.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
items.summary: We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type-$E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple. These are precisely the remaining exceptional Grassmannians for which generic semisimplicity of small quantum cohomology was still unknown.

items.title: Interactive Particle Systems on Hypergraphs, Drift Analysis and the WalkSAT algorithm
items.summary: We analyze the expected running time of WalkSAT, a well-known local search procedure for satisfiability solving, on satisfiable instances of the k-XOR SAT problem. We obtain estimates of this expected running time by reducing the problem to a setting amenable to classical techniques from drift analysis. A crucial ingredient of this reduction is the definition of (new, explosive) hypergraph versions of interacting particle systems, notably of coalescing and annihilating random walks as well as the voter model. The use of these tools allows to show that the expected running time of WalkSAT depends on structural parameter (we call odd Cheeger drift) of the dual of the formula hypergraph.

items.title: A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
items.summary: This paper develops reliable a posteriori error estimates for finite element approximation of an evolution equation with a positive-type memory kernels on bounded convex polygonal or polyhedral domains, including both smooth and weakly singular kernels. For the weakly singular kernel $t^{α-1}/Γ(α),\; 0<α<1,$ the model captures the transition from parabolic diffusion to wave propagation, recovering the corresponding limiting equations as $α\to0^+$ and $α\to1^-$, respectively, with the memory term governing the intermediate dynamics. The spatial discretization employs time-dependent finite element spaces, while the backward Euler method combined with numerical quadrature is used for time integration. A unified \emph{a posteriori} analysis is established for both semidiscrete and fully discrete approximations. Elliptic reconstruction yields optimal spatial error estimates, while a memory-lag estimate preserves the essential cancellation in the convolution term, yielding a first-order temporal estimator whose kernel dependence is characterized by its integral. The resulting estimators are robust, with constants independent of the final time, spatial mesh size, and time step. Their kernel dependence involves only computable quantities, avoiding exponential growth in time. Moreover, for the weakly singular kernel, the $α$-dependent factors remain uniformly bounded for $α\in(0,1).$ Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the theoretical results, and a space-time adaptive algorithm is also demonstrated on an L-shaped domain featuring a corner singularity and two temporal layers.

items.title: Smooth quotients of principally polarized abelian varieties
items.summary: We give an explicit characterization of all principally polarized abelian varieties $(A,Θ)$ such that there is a finite subgroup of automorphisms $G$ of $A$ that preserve the numerical class of $Θ$, and such that the quotient variety $A/G$ is smooth. We also give a complete classification of smooth quotients of Jacobians of curves.

items.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
items.summary: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

items.title: On a classical zero-sum invariant II: Disproof of a long-standing conjecture
items.summary: For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the smallest {nonnegative} integer $\ell$ such that every zero-sum free sequence $T$ over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ has the following property: all nonzero elements of $G$ that do not occur as a subsequence sum of $T$ lie in a proper coset of some subgroup of $G$. It is easy to check that $\mathsf d (G)-1 \le ν(G) \le \mathsf d (G)$, where $\mathsf d (G)$ is the small Davenport constant of $G$. A conjecture by Gao from the year 2000 stated that equality should always hold at the lower bound. This conjecture has since been confirmed for many families of groups (including all p-groups and groups of rank at most two). In this paper, we disprove the conjecture.

items.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
items.summary: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

items.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
items.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $F$ be a totally imaginary CM field and $F^+$ be the maximal totally real subfield such that $F/F^+$ is unramified at all finite places, and every place $v | p$ of $F^+$ is split in $F$. We allow arbitrary ramification of $p$ in $F^+$. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group over $F^+$ as defined in [2]. Fix a place $\mathfrak{p} | p$ in $F$. In this article, we determine explicit local Serre weights at $\mathfrak{p}$ attached to a modular mod $p$ Galois representation $\barρ_h$ of the absolute Galois group of $F$, associated to an eigenform $h$ of $G$. The eigenform $h$ has arbitrary weights and small slope at $\mathfrak{p}$. We also show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms with arbitrary ramification of $p$ in the totally real field. The eigenforms come from totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras over totally real fields, split at places above $p$. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$-modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.

items.title: Prismatoid Band-Unfolding Revisited
items.summary: It remains unknown if every prismatoid has a nonoverlapping edge-unfolding, a special case of the long-unsolved "Dürer's problem." Recently nested prismatoids have been settled [Rad24] by mixing (in some sense) the two natural unfoldings, petal-unfolding and band-unfolding. Band-unfolding fails due to a specific counterexample [O'R13b]. The main contribution of this paper is a characterization when a band-unfolding of a nested prismatoid does in fact result in a nonoverlapping unfolding. In particular, we show that the mentioned counterexample is in a sense the only possible counterexample. Although this result does not expand the class of shapes known to have an edge-unfolding, its proof expands our understanding in several ways, developing tools that may help resolve the non-nested case.

items.title: Mathematical Reality Capture: from the age of discoveries to mathematical topography and surveys
items.summary: A proof answers a precise question, but mathematical understanding also grows through the relationships that its answer makes visible. A point measurement likewise differs from a photograph or a three-dimensional reconstruction of a building. In this work, we argue that, with the help of AI, mathematics should move from a discipline focused on isolated investigations of mathematical objects towards one capable of mapping them systematically. We therefore introduce the idea of "Mathematical Reality Capture", inspired by digital surveying and the reconstruction of a scene from several viewpoints. An elementary example shows how comparing algebra and geometry can illuminate the same phenomenon, provided that we distinguish diversity of explanations from validity of proof. From this analogy we derive criteria for building verifiable atlases, an experiment with which to assess their usefulness, and a reflection on the role of mathematicians in interpreting them.

items.title: Regularity Effects on the Small-Diffusion Asymptotics of the Principal Eigenvalue: Non-convergence and Convergence
items.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior as \(d\to0^+\) of the principal eigenvalue \(λ(d)\) of the one-dimensional elliptic problem \[ \begin{cases} -dφ''(x)-2αm'(x)φ'(x)+c(x)φ(x) =λ(d)φ(x), & x\in(a,b),\\ φ'(a)=φ'(b)=0, \end{cases} \] where \(α>0\) is fixed, \(m\in C^{1,1}([a,b])\), and \(c\in C([a,b])\). We assume that \(m'=0\) only at \(x_0\in(a,b)\), where \(m\) attains a strict minimum. Within this class, we construct a counterexample $m\in C^{1,1}$ for which \(λ(d)\) has two distinct subsequential limits as \(d\to0^+\), leading to the non-convergence of $λ(d)$. We then consider another class of $C^{1,1}$ advection functions for which $m'(x)/(x-x_0)$ has positive one-sided limits at $x_0$. For this class, we prove that $λ(d)$ converges as $d\to0^+$. Thus, \(C^{1,1}\) regularity alone does not ensure convergence of the principal eigenvalue, even when \(m\) has exactly one strict interior critical minimal point.

items.title: A new approach to compactly supported stationary Euler flows
items.summary: We construct smooth, compactly supported stationary Euler flows in two and three dimensions. The three-dimensional flows are axisymmetric with swirl, and their pressure varies along some streamlines. The planar flows are not locally radial. Both constructions start from simple radial profiles, which we perturb by solving scalar elliptic equations on fixed domains. We choose these equations so that their solutions can be exactly constant on open sets and meet these constant regions smoothly. Comparison arguments produce the constant regions, while an a priori regularity theorem ensures that all derivatives vanish where a solution meets them. This gives compact support and smoothness without having to describe the boundary of the support.

items.title: Solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
items.summary: The present paper is devoted to exhibit solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic. With ambiguous non-conservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. This jump condition is obtained from the information given by the travelling wave solutions of the viscous extension of the system that involves the diffusion terms arising from the physics of the problem. We are then able to determine the simple waves of the non-conservative system studied here and we are able to construct some solutions of the Riemann problem of interest.

items.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
items.summary: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

items.title: Sharp helical maximal estimates in all dimensions
items.summary: We establish sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates for averages over smooth nondegenerate curves in $\mathbb R^n$ for $p>n$. More precisely, we show that for any nondegenerate curve $γ$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and the associated maximal operator \begin{equation} M f(x):=\sup_{t>0} \Big|\int_{-1}^1f(x-tγ(s))χ(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|, \end{equation} the estimate \begin{equation} \| Mf\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\lesssim_{γ,p,n} \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} \end{equation} holds for all $p>n$. A new ingredient is a weighted Kakeya-type estimate.

items.title: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation
items.summary: We construct explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress formulation of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media using Schrödingerisation. After rewriting the equations in symmetric matrix form(SMF), we use Fourier spectral discretization for source-driven periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions. The Schrödingerisation method transforms any linear PDEs into a system of Schrödinger-type PDEs -with unitary evolution- using the warped phase transformation that maps the equations in one higher dimension. For periodic problems, we develop circuits by combining controlled Fourier-mode rotations. For physical boundaries, interleaved encoding swaps the spatial and field-component registers, enabling a more efficient circuit construction using shift operators. We analyze $p$th-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and derive splitting-error and CNOT-gate estimates, under the assumptions of smooth auxiliary initialization and solution-state recovery. Comparison with classical partitioned splitting methods identifies a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence for the quantum state-evolution subroutine. Noiseless circuit simulations of a forced periodic problem and an impedance problem illustrate the constructions and quantify their errors against exact solutions and classical reference computations.

items.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
items.summary: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics. The example was found with the help of AI.

items.title: On Landsberg Unicorns of General $(α,β)$-Type
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the classes of \lq\lq unicorns" of general $(α,β)$-metric types, namely, Landsberg general $(α,β)$-metrics that are non-Berwaldian. We provide explicit solutions for these metrics, including several new classes. Furthermore, we identify and exclude the cases that yield degenerate metrics to guarantee the geometric validity of the established solutions.

items.title: Three quantitative central limit theorems for the unbounded excursion component of a Gaussian field
items.summary: For a class of smooth stationary Gaussian fields, we study the fluctuations of the volume, surface area and Euler characteristic of the unbounded excursion component in growing boxes $Λ_n=[-n,n]^d$. We establish nondegenerate central limit theorems for all three functionals throughout the supercritical regime in every dimension $d\geq 2$. We further quantify these central limit theorems by establishing Berry--Esseen bounds of order $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-(1-1/s)}\bigr)$ in Kolmogorov distance, where $s\in(1,2]$ depend on the regularity and decay assumptions. Especially for the Bargmann--Fock field, we obtain a Berry--Esseen bound of $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-1/2}\bigr)$ for all three functionals. A matching lower bound shows that this rate is sharp for the Euler characteristic. For the volume, we improve the previously known rate of $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-1/2}(\log|Λ_n|)^{2d}\bigr)$. We mainly use Stein's method and moment bounds for differences arising from white-noise resampling to finish our proof.

items.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
items.summary: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{é} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

items.title: Hypergeometric Motives from Toric Hypersurfaces
items.summary: In this paper, we study two compactifications of general hypersurfaces defined by the vanishing of linear combinations of $d+2$ monomials in $d$-dimensional algebraic tori. We prove that the number of their $\mathbb{F}_q$-points is given by finite hypergeometric sums under certain general conditions. In the process, we introduce the notion of a gamma triple, which allows us to extend the classical definition of finite hypergeometric sums to prime powers corresponding to the cyclotomic field of definition of the associated monodromy representation. As a special case of our main results, we study the Dwork family and obtain a formula for the number of its $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. Our results generalise the work of Beukers, Cohen, and Mellit for finite hypergeometric sums defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Equivariant formality and representation theory
items.summary: Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $K$ its connected Lie subgroup. Using the $K$-theoretic version of equivariant formality developed in [F2] which involves analysis of vector bundles over $G/K$, we find two characterizations of equivariant formality of the isotropy action of $K$ on $G/K$. The first one equates equivariant formality with a "smoothness" condition of the restriction map of the representation ring of $G$ to that of $K$. The second characterization asserts that equivariant formality amounts to the equivariant $K$-theoretic index pairing of two certain special $K$-theory classes being nontrivial in some sense. By applying these characterizations, we are able to give a representation theoretic criterion for equivariant formality of the isotropy action by a circle subgroup, as well as an invariant theory criterion for the case where $K$ is a torus of dimension one less than the rank of $G$, culminating in a complete classification of equivariant formality where $G$ is further assumed to be simple.

items.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
items.summary: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.

items.title: Global Existence and Scattering of a Class of Two-Dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg Systems
items.summary: For a class of two-dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg systems of quantum hydrodynamic type, we establish global existence and scattering for small, smooth, spatially localized perturbations of a constant equilibrium with irrotational velocity. This extends the three-dimensional well-posedness result of Song [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 2157--2224] to two dimensions. Our proof follows the space-time resonance approach developed by Deng, Ionescu, Pausader, and Pusateri for the three-dimensional gravity-capillary water-wave system. The new ingredients are twofold. First, to allow non-neutral initial data, we exploit the absence of space resonances and of time resonances---including those arising after the second and third iterations---and the improved approximate-finite-speed-of-propagation bounds. Second, in the energy estimates, we adapt the almost orthogonality argument used in the works of Ionescu--Pausader and Guo--Ionescu--Pausader to the regime in which the input and output frequencies are all comparable to $1$. In this regime, time resonances may occur and the relevant curvature quantity may vanish.

items.title: The homogeneity function of the fractional $p$-Laplacian and optimal asymptotic exponents for critical Hardy-Sobolev equations
items.summary: Let $N \geq 2$, $s\in (0,1)$, and $p \in (1, \infty)$ with $N>sp$. For the fractional $p$-Laplacian, the power function $|x|^{-γ}$ with $0<γ<\frac{N}{p-1}$ satisfies $$(-Δ_p)^s \big(|x|^{-γ}\big)=Φ(γ)|x|^{-γ(p-1)-sp} \, \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}.$$ Starting from the power function formula of Del Pezzo and Quaas (2026), we derive a paired integral representation of $Φ$, and show that $Φ$ is strictly increasing and then strictly decreasing, with a unique maximum at $\frac{N-sp}{p}$. This maximum $\barμ:=Φ(\frac{N-sp}{p})$ equals one half of the sharp fractional Hardy constant. Consequently, for every $0<μ<\barμ$, the equation $Φ(γ)=μ$ has exactly two roots $0<γ_{-}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p}<γ_{+}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p-1}$. These roots determine the homogeneous solutions $|x|^{-γ_{-}(μ)}$ and $|x|^{-γ_{+}(μ)}$ of the Hardy equation \begin{equation*} (-Δ_p)^s u - μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}}=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}, \; u> 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N \setminus \{0\}. \end{equation*} For $0<μ<\barμ$, we then study the following critical Hardy-Sobolev equation \begin{align}\tag{$\mathcal{P}$}\label{P} (-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}} = u^{\frac{Np}{N-sp}-1} \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N, \; u > 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N. \end{align} Let $p \geq 2$ and $U$ be a positive, radially symmetric, nonincreasing finite-energy weak solution to \eqref{P}. We prove that there exists $C>0$ for which \begin{align*} U(x) \leq C|x|^{-γ_-(μ)}\;\text{as }|x| \rightarrow 0,\quad \text{ and } \quad U(x)\le C|x|^{-γ_+(μ)} \; \text{as }|x| \rightarrow \infty. \end{align*} Further, we show that $γ_-(μ)$ and $γ_+(μ)$ are the optimal exponents describing the singularity at the origin and the decay at infinity respectively.

items.title: Quantitative periodic homogenization and uniform regularity for nonlocal equations
items.summary: In this work, we study quantitative homogenization for a class of nonlocal equations with periodically oscillating Hölder continuous coefficients. For Dirichlet problems in bounded $C^{1,α}$ domains, we prove $L^2$ convergence rates that are expected to be optimal. In addition, we establish interior Lipschitz estimates and optimal boundary Hölder estimates for weak solutions, with constants independent of the period of oscillation.

items.title: Counting and Sampling Git Graphs
items.summary: Version Control Systems, like Git and Mercurial, represent the history of a project as a Directed Acyclic Graph, capturing divergences and merges throughout development. A widely adopted workflow, the feature branch workflow, imposes a particularly simple structure: a single main branch and features branches evolving in parallel without interfering with one another. This work presents an enumerative study of these Git graphs. We first establish a bijection between Git graphs and a simpler combinatorial class, which we term cyclariums, and derive their exact count at size n, namely \( \sum\_{k=2}^n \sum\_{f = 1}^{k-1} {k \brack f} { n - k - 1 \choose k - f - 1} \). Using a saddle-point method, we further show that this number is asymptotically equivalent to \[ \frac{e^{1/8}}{2} \left(\frac{n}{2e}\right)^{\frac n 2} \exp\left(\frac 1 2 \ln\frac n 2 \sqrt{\frac n 2} + \sqrt{2 n} + \frac{(\ln\frac n 2)^2}{32} \right) \left(\frac n 2\right)^{-3/8}. \] Additionally, we analyze the limit laws of key parameters. Finally, we address random generation by designing both a uniform sampler and a Boltzmann sampler for these graphs.

items.title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
items.summary: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

items.title: Spectrum in alternative topological algebras and a new look at old theorems
items.summary: In this paper, we consider real and complex algebras as well as algebras over general fields. In Section 2, we revisit and prove several results on (quadratic) algebras over general fields. As an example, we demonstrate that a quadratic algebra over a field of characteristic not $2$ is flexible if and only if it is proper--a concept introduced in this paper. In Section 3, we show how to develop the spectral theory in the context of complex (resp. real) one-sided alternative topological algebras. Along the way, spectral theory is used to prove several topological counterparts of the well-known theorems of Frobenius, Hurwitz, Gelfand-Mazur, and Zorn. This is done, for example, in the context of left (resp. right) alternative topological algebras whose duals separate their elements. In Section 4, we consider real and complex algebras in various topological settings and reconsider and prove several results. For instance, it is shown that given a $ 1 < k \in \mathbb{N}$, on any locally complex algebra, there exists a unique nonzero vector space norm, say, $\|.\|$, satisfying the identity $\|a^k\| = \|a\|^k$ on the algebra. In Section 5, among other things, we revisit and slightly strengthen the celebrated theorems of Frobenius, Zorn, Gelfand-Mazur, and Hurwitz, and also give slight extensions of their topological counterparts, e.g., theorems of Albert, Kaplansky, and Urbanik-Wright to name a few, in several

items.title: Minimal depth $K$-types for wild double covers and Shimura correspondences
items.summary: Using distinguished pseudo-spherical representations of covering tori constructed in a companion work and Dat's parahoric induction, we construct a distinguished family of representations for an Iwahori subgroup $\bar{I}$ in $\bar{G}$, an $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne (BD) cover of a split connected reductive $p$-adic group $G$, under explicit hypotheses on the BD datum. No tameness assumption $\mathrm{gcd}(p,n)=1$ is imposed. The construction suggests a conjectural theory of Iwahori-types for BD covers beyond the tame case. We verify this for $2$-fold covers of almost simple simply-laced simply-connected Chevalley groups of rank at least $2$ over $2$-adic fields. In particular, for these non-tame $2$-fold covers we prove: 1) The pair $(\bar{I},σ)$ is a Bushnell-Kutzko type for the Bernstein block analogous to the block of unramified principal series in a linear reductive group. This is a non-tame analogue of the Borel-Casselman theorem. 2) The Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},σ^{\vee})$ has an Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation up to normalization. In types $A_{r},D_{2r+1},E_{6},E_{7}$ we obtain the complete presentation and show that $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},σ^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of an explicit linear group. This determines an equivalence of Bernstein blocks producing a local Shimura correspondence. 3) The representation $σ$ extends to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup $\bar{K}$. Among the genuine $\bar{K}$-representations, $σ$ has minimal depth with respect to the principal congruence filtration. It also yields a finite Shimura correspondence, generalizing a result of Savin.

items.title: Factorization of Elliptic Divisibility Sequences via Modular Curves
items.summary: In this paper, we give a structural factorization of elliptic divisibility sequences in terms of finitely many modular functions on the modular curve $X_1(N)$. More precisely, we express the functions obtained by pulling back division polynomials along the universal torsion section as products of fixed modular factors. Then we show that this factorization is compatible with the natural action of $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ on the modular curve $X_1(N)$ and so descends to the modular curve $X_0(N)$ via the norm map. As applications, we obtain a perfect power criterion, local and global growth estimates for the associated elliptic divisibility sequences.

items.title: The double of a simplicial complex
items.summary: We introduce the notion of doubling and r-tupling for simplicial complexes, a notion reminiscent to that of matching complexes in graph theory. We prove a connectivity result for such complexes and relate r-tupling to stabilizing r times faster in homological stability.

items.title: On Some Lie Group Invariant noncommutative functions
items.summary: We study noncommutative polynomials and functions invariant under linear actions of infinite (compact Lie) groups, with a focus on $SU(2)$ acting on two noncommuting variables. For $SU(2)$, we give a complete description of the invariant noncommutative polynomials: there are no invariants of odd degree, and in degree $2n$ the invariants are exactly the span of the $S_{2n}$-orbit of $(XY-YX)^n$. We also construct an explicit basis recursively from the operation $(A,B)\mapsto XAYB-YAXB$, and show that the space of degree-$2n$ invariants has dimension equal to the $n$-th Catalan number. All proofs proceed by direct computation with the Haar integral.

items.title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
items.summary: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.

items.title: Scaling limit and universality for one-dimensional long-range first-passage metric in the linear-growth regime
items.summary: We prove universal Gaussian and stable fluctuation limits for one-dimensional long-range first-passage percolation with edge times $\|x-y\|^αω_{x,y}$. The positive i.i.d. weights satisfy $\mathbb{P}(ω\le t)=t^{θ+o(1)}$ as $t\downarrow0$ and $\mathbb{E}(ω^ζ)<\infty$ for some $θ,ζ>0$. For $α>1+2/θ$, the passage time $T(0,n)$ has a positive deterministic linear growth rate $μ$. For $α>1+3/θ$, we establish a Gaussian central limit theorem with linear asymptotic variance, a functional version, and limit theorems for geodesic hop and cut point counts. For $1+2/θ<α<1+3/θ$, assuming a regularly varying lower tail, we obtain a totally left-skewed stable limit with index $β=θ(α-1)-1$ and an explicit scale, together with convergence to a spectrally negative stable Lévy process in the Skorokhod $M_1$ topology. The proof constructs i.i.d. blocks between hubs through which every crossing geodesic must pass. A spread-out comparison metric makes this regeneration available for every $ζ>0$, even when the edge law has infinite mean. The key estimate identifies the exact left-tail asymptotic of the centered block reward, generated by a single fast long edge. A monotone within-block approximation yields the functional stable limit.

items.title: Uniform parameter bounds for weighted exponential equations on simply connected domains
items.summary: We consider positive solutions of \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δu=pλh(x)u^{p-1}\mathrm{e}^{u^p}&\text{in }Ω,\\ u>0&\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0&\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded simply connected domain and $h\in C^2(\overlineΩ)$ is positive on $\overlineΩ$. The cases $p=1$ and $p=2$ correspond to the Liouville and Moser-Trudinger equations, respectively. We prove that the normalized parameter \begin{equation*} β=\frac{λp^2}{2}\left(\int_Ωh(\mathrm{e}^{u^p}-1)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2-p}{p}}\left(\int_Ωhu^p\mathrm{e}^{u^p}\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{p}} \end{equation*} is bounded by a constant depending only on $Ω$ and $h$, uniformly over all $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$ and positive solutions. At $p=2$, this excludes positive constrained critical points of the weighted Moser-Trudinger functional at sufficiently large Dirichlet energies. For $p=2$ and $h\equiv1$, we further prove that the energy converges uniformly to $4π$ as $λ\to0$ when $Ω$ is convex. We also develop a boundary exclusion argument for positive weights that rules out boundary blow-up for $1<p<2$ without a priori energy bound.

items.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
items.summary: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2016. The proof combines a key lemma with cycle decompositions of random graphs.

items.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
items.summary: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

items.title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
items.summary: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.

items.title: Persistent Hubs and Sharp Asymptotics in Eigenvector Preferential Attachment Trees
items.summary: We prove sharp almost-sure asymptotics for eigenvector preferential attachment trees in which each attachment uses eigenvector centrality with probability $α\in(0,1]$ and uniform selection with probability $1-α$. A unique persistent hub eventually has the maximum degree, which is asymptotic to $γ^2t^{2/3}$, where $γ=(9α/10)^{1/3}$. The Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue is asymptotic to $γt^{1/3}$, and the second-largest degree is asymptotic to $2γt^{1/3}$. The hub and its neighbors each carry asymptotically half of the squared Perron mass. We also identify the centrality profile by degree and an explicit mixture of geometric laws for the degree of a uniformly sampled vertex. A limiting distance profile quantifies the dandelion geometry, and vertices beyond the hub's neighbors have maximum degree of order at most $\log t$.

items.title: The existence of the compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$
items.summary: In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the open question posed by G.Birkhoff and R.S.Pierce in 1956 concerning the existence of a compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$. Using valuation rings theory, basis extension in infinite-dimensional vector spaces and extension of field embeddings to algebraic extensions, we obtain that for every real $t>1$ transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$, the compatible lattice order can be chosen such that $0\prec1$, $0\vee i=t$, and $1\wedge t=0$. Consequently, $\mathbb{C}$ admits at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct compatible lattice orders, each extending the usual order on $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: An Anisotropic Entropy for the Rotationally Symmetric Ricci Flow
items.summary: For a rotationally symmetric Ricci flow $g(t)=ds^2+f(s,t)^2g_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}$, $n\ge3$, we study the scale-invariant curvature anisotropy $A=1-f_s^2+ff_{ss}$ introduced by Angenent--Knopf. At the critical power $p_*=(n-1)/(n-2)$, with $Φ=sgn(A)|A|^{p_*/2}$, we prove the distributional identity \[ (\partial_t-Δ)|A|^{p_*} =-\frac4{n-1} \left|Φ_s+(n-1)\frac{f_s}{f}Φ\right|^2. \] Integration against a conjugate heat kernel gives an anisotropic entropy formula. As an application, we obtain an entropy threshold for Type-I singularities on $\mathbb S^n$: if the entropy associated with a singular-time kernel is at most $1$ at an earlier regular time, every tangent flow at the corresponding singular point is a round shrinking sphere. This criterion follows from the $0/1$ quantization of the singular-time anisotropic density.
