items.title: A New Parametric Uncertainty Approach to Systems with Time-Varying Delay and Feedback Stabilization
items.summary: Delay Differential Equations (DDEs) with an uncertain time-varying state delay are often modeled as a feedback interconnection of a nominal time-invariant system with a time-varying uncertainty operator. However, typical choices of uncertainty operators do not admit tight characterizations of input-output properties. In this paper, we propose a new representation of a DDE with time-varying delay system as a feedback interconnection of a nominal fixed delay DDE with a time-varying multiplicative parametric uncertainty operator, where the parameter is bounded in $L_\infty$ norms -- yielding an operator norm bound on the uncertainty. We then provide a modified uncertainty representation which uses the $L_2$ norm of the parameter to bound the operator norm of the uncertainty. Finally, we show that by representing the nominal system using Partial Integral Equations (PIEs), these characterizations of the uncertainty operator can be used for stability analysis or stabilizing feedback controller synthesis. The effectiveness of the approach is illustrated with simple numerical examples.

items.title: Probabilistic Sequential Safety for Stochastic Dynamical Systems
items.summary: In this letter, we investigate a notion of probabilistic safety for a stochastic dynamical system. Standard safety notions are based on the idea that an unsafe region of the state-space must be avoided at each instant. In contrast, we study a sequential safety notion which is based on avoiding a tuple of target regions of the state-space. The proposed safety notion is inspired by many practical systems, ranging from modeling jailbreak attacks in large language models (LLMs) to predicting hazardous chemical reactions. In solving the sequential safety problem, we solve a sequential reachability problem for a stochastic dynamical system.

items.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: dynamic problems
items.summary: The coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections requires deciding both the trajectories of the vehicles and their crossing order, with the additional difficulty that the set of vehicles to be coordinated changes as traffic flows through the intersection. Since the resulting mixed-integer optimal control problem is hard to solve online, we propose an arrival-triggered receding-horizon scheme built around a schedule-refinement heuristic: for a fixed crossing order, a single nonlinear program (NLP) optimizes all trajectories and crossing times, and the first-order sensitivities of the cost with respect to the vehicle schedule are used to select adjacent swaps that are likely to reduce the overall cost. Replanning is triggered only when a new vehicle arrives, the new vehicle is appended at the tail of the current crossing order, and a memory of evaluated swaps that persists across replanning steps avoids redundant computations. Simulations of traffic scenarios involving streams of a few hundred heterogeneous vehicles show that the proposed scheme recovers most of the optimality gap incurred by first-in-first-out scheduling.

items.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: static problems
items.summary: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.

items.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
items.summary: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.

items.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
items.summary: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity ($1.625$ m/s$^2$) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

items.title: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry
items.summary: In reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal returned to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Near the correlation zero, an archived SGD comparison finds truncated inversion 0.000813 lower in cross-entropy than polar correction, with a paired 95% interval for the difference from -0.001853 to 0.000060, and a retained-mode quadratic proxy slightly favors truncation. Selecting the return port with the largest received power falls short of the predicted five-point alignment advantage over random selection at both tested spacings, gaining at most 0.97 points, while the local inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient is supported. Seven specified interference-induced accuracy-collapse predictions are rejected, and independent zero-mean interference preserves the conditional mean under a fixed linear chain. Per-subcarrier correction and spherical-wavefront compensation do not deliver their predicted accuracy gains. Focusing leaves both methods near chance in a single-mode model and adds no observed gain in a model with a line-of-sight component plus scattering. A successful port assignment under nonsymmetric motion refutes an exact-symmetry requirement. The competing positioning-error prediction is supported. Gaussian rail jitter with a standard deviation of 0.383 wavelengths yields high terminal test accuracy, whereas a fixed bias of the same magnitude yields near-chance accuracy. These cases distinguish valid local physical relations from unsupported training forecasts through task support, noise injection, and update moments.

items.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields
items.summary: A Gaussian random wave field is sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture. After displacement, re-indexing leaves a residual in the Voronoi cell. We study whether the empirical lag correlation has positive real part throughout the cell. For each realization in a single-output reciprocal link with noiseless over-the-air return, this is equivalent to the negative returned gradient being a descent direction for all residuals and differentiable losses with nonzero error signals. Return noise is treated exactly. For isotropic fields, ball-shaped apertures, unshifted lattice points, and dilations approaching the critical covering radius, every minimizer is a deep hole except with exponentially small probability. A Gaussian vector on the deep holes determines the limiting failure probability, with explicit covariance and lattice-independent limiting normalization. Square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices have two, three, four, and twelve sign classes. At fixed target failure probabilities below the critical limiting value, this covariance determines the exact leading aperture constant. When the margin and target failure probability vanish jointly, that constant is common to lattice shapes within each dimension. A cubic correction yields vanishing relative tail error in a moderate-deviation regime. A non-asymptotic two-sided aperture law has explicit constants. With a Rayleigh-faded specular path and positive diffuse margin, a failure floor occurs at every positive path power exactly when the cosine of its phase change is negative somewhere in the cell. The floor vanishes for all directions exactly when the covering radius is at most a quarter wavelength.

items.title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) has proven to be a powerful tool for decoding neural activity in real-life scenarios, including the perception and processing of emotions elicited by music. Among the various musical features that modulate these responses, musical mode and melodic direction (or contour) play a central role. This work proposes a novel EEG feature extraction framework based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose EEG signals recorded during active piano performance for the detection of these two musical features. Energy-based descriptors were computed from the first four Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) obtained through EMD and used to train a Wide Neural Network classifier. The model performance was benchmarked against several standard classifiers commonly employed in EEG classification tasks. Two experimental scenarios were explored: intra-subject and intersubject. In the former case, the proposed framework achieved average accuracies of 84%, whereas in the inter-subject case, accuracies reached 81% on average using the first IMF, with AUC-ROC values of 0.9 on average in both cases. A frequency-domain analysis revealed a strong correspondence between the IMFs and conventional EEG sub-bands, except for certain specific frequency components that were not fully represented. Predominant activations were observed over the frontal, temporal, and parietooccipital regions, areas consistently associated with music processing. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrated robustness to handedness, successfully classifying EEG data across participants regardless of their dominant hand. These findings highlight the potential of EMD-based feature extraction for identifying music-related neural patterns and contribute to advancing research in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), affective neuroscience, and the broader understanding of the neural encoding of musical structure.

items.title: Robust PPG-Exclusive Heart Rate Estimation During Maximal Exercise Using Population-Based Priors
items.summary: PPG is the main technology for wearable heart rate (HR) monitoring. However, motion artifacts during intense physical activity reduce its reliability due to spectral overlap with the cardiac signal. This study investigates whether severely contaminated PPG signals can yield reliable HR estimates without auxiliary sensors by leveraging prior knowledge of HR dynamics. We acquired simultaneous PPG and ECG signals from 21 subjects during a maximal cycloergometer test. Using Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation, we built HR evolution priors from the ground-truth ECG and applied Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to align normalized HR curves and estimate a barycenter average. DTW aligns normalized HR curves with minimal error across all subjects, validating robust population-based priors. For each test subject, we combined the PPG Power Spectral Density (PSD) with the prior distribution to generate a "posterior PSD". We identified and ranked candidate HR trajectories using heuristic search within the "posterior PSD" and selected the most likely path. Our approach reduced mean absolute error (MAE) in BPM relative to the ground-truth ECG by a median of 63.3% (IQR: 47.3%-74.6%) compared to a PPG+accelerometer benchmark. These results show that physiological priors and DTW-based alignment enable robust, PPG-exclusive HR monitoring during high-intensity exercise.

items.title: On the Performance of RIS-Empowered Transmitters with Receive Combining Techniques
items.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered transmitters offer a promising basis for hardware-efficient multi-antenna architectures in next-generation wireless networks. In particular, combining these transmitters with low-complexity reception techniques such as receive antenna selection (RAS) can further simplify the receiver architecture. In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint on RIS-empowered multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and RAS. Since each RIS element can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS-based transmitters can degrade the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC in the examined system models, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.

items.title: Closed-Form Subspace Loss and Snapshot-Limited Dimension Selection for Beamspace MVDR Radar
items.summary: A beamspace minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processor adapts a window of B beams instead of all N elements of a large array, trading a subspace loss that falls with B against a covariance estimation loss that rises with B for a fixed number K of training snapshots. We give the subspace loss of a DFT beam window in point jamming in closed form: exactly for any jammer power, and in the high interference-to-noise ratio (INR) limit through the Dirichlet kernel of the array. Combined with the known scaled-Beta law of sample matrix inversion (SMI) with a fixed transform, it gives a window size B*(K) for unloaded SMI. On a simulated 32x32 array with carriers from 4 to 8 GHz, noise jammers and Billingsley land clutter, the exact form is within 0.04 dB of the clairvoyant subspace loss for 25- and 49-beam windows at jammer levels from 10 to 50 dB. For a 9-beam window whose three columns are taken by three jammers near the target's elevation, the clutter that the form leaves out costs up to 5 dB. With the nominal K, B*(K) picks the lowest-loss window in all 30 cases with more than one runnable window. The rule is an oracle: it needs the jammer parameters or the true covariance, and errors of 0.25 bin rms in the jammer directions add a mean loss of 0.04 dB. With diagonal loading the best window was larger still wherever the rule chose more than the smallest window.

items.title: Approximation of the Narrowband Velocity Ambiguity Function in Near-Field Sensing Systems
items.summary: This work investigates the velocity ambiguity function in the radiative near-field of a uniform linear antenna array. First, the general ambiguity function is formulated and the velocity cross-section at a target position is considered. The velocity vector is decomposed into radial and tangential components, which are analyzed separately. Next, the closed-form approximations for the velocity ambiguity function are derived and shown to be accurate despite relying on far-field approximations. The results show that the near-field regime does not improve radial velocity estimation, but enables estimation of the tangential velocity. Finally, the velocity ambiguity functions and the achievable resolution are analyzed for different array configurations. For tangential velocity estimation, MIMO and a collection of SISO radars offer improved ambiguity function and resolution as compared to the SIMO/MISO configuration.

items.title: In-Context Learning for MIMO Turbo Receivers
items.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) turbo receivers iteratively exchange information between a soft-input soft-output detector and a decoder. Traditional implementations rely on pilot-based channel estimates, which can be poor in the case of short pilot sequences or mismatched channel models, resulting in significant performance degradation. To address this limitation, we introduce the EXTrinsic In-Context Learning Network (EXT-ICLNet), a Transformer-based detector that takes the pilots as in-context examples and is trained to approximate the symbol extrinsic posterior distribution given the pilots, without explicit channel estimation. EXT-ICLNet is thus compatible with existing turbo receivers, as it implements a log-domain prior skip connection, ensuring that the network learns only the extrinsic information. Numerical results for a $4\times4$ MIMO system with 16-QAM and a quantized front end show that EXT-ICLNet outperforms baselines based on explicit channel state information (CSI) estimation at low-to-medium signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), as well as expectation-propagation (EP) baselines with perfect CSI at high SNRs. The results are further validated by comparing the extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) charts of EXT-ICLNet, a neural EP baseline, and EXT-ICLNet without skip connection, demonstrating how EXT-ICLNet provides a more favorable transfer of a priori and extrinsic information.

items.title: Orthogonal Zadoff-Chu Based Pilot Design For Fractional Channel Estimation in MIMO-OTFS
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence-based pilot design for fractional channel estimation in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation for point-to-point multi-input multi-output (MIMO) scenarios. Orthogonal pilot sequences are assigned to each transmit antenna using ZF sequences. At the receiver, a correlation-based scheme is used to construct the signal for estimation. The estimation relies on a two-dimensional extension of the Aboutanios and Mulgrew (A&M) frequency estimation method. Simulation results show that the proposed approach achieves low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) while maintaining stable performance as the number of transmit antennas increases.

items.title: Placing the Beamspace Window on a Hopping Carrier: Bin Drift, Exact Capture and the Cost of Rounding
items.summary: A frequency-agile radar with a large digital array moves the spatial frequency of its look direction across the beams of a spatial FFT every time it changes carrier, so a beamspace adaptive processor must decide where to put its window at each hop. Because the beamspace transform is orthonormal, the output of the processor depends only on the span of the window, and a hop changes nothing but where the window sits. Centring the window exactly on the fractional bin of the look direction keeps the look vector fully inside it at every carrier, for the price of one phase ramp before the FFT. On a 32 by 32 array over 4 to 8 GHz the look bin drifts by 1.6 to 6.9 bins for look directions from u=0.2 to 60 degrees. Rounding to the nearest bin costs up to 1.34, 0.74 and 0.50 dB of look-direction capture for 3 by 3, 5 by 5 and 7 by 7 windows. In a three-jammer scenario with 41 carriers, a window frozen at the lowest carrier loses 39 to 60 dB at the worst carrier for a look direction of u=0.55, the exact window beats nearest-bin placement by 0.31 to 0.65 dB there, and the advantage reverses for a nine-beam window near broadside, where nearest-bin was 0.61 dB better.

items.title: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware
items.summary: Self-supervised vision transformers are increasingly used as reusable encoders for Earth observation, but their inference cost on the hardware available in the field is rarely characterized. We deploy a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 nodes, from a low-power CPU without AVX2 to an AVX2+VNNI reference, at FP32, FP16 and INT8 on the CPU and, where present, the integrated GPU, and report latency, energy (RAPL and wall plug) and linear-probe accuracy. Quantization is accuracy-neutral: INT8 changes micro-mAP by only +0.0006, within the seed spread, so precision becomes a pure cost decision. INT8 lowers CPU latency on every node, by 1.45x even on the CPU without AVX2, and CPU energy wherever it is measured, and the VNNI reference (1.53x) suggests a further gain beyond AVX2. The Pareto-optimal device shifts from the integrated GPU, which is 4.38x faster than the CPU on the weakest node, to the CPU as the CPU class improves.

items.title: StreamSE: Neural Audio Codec-based Streaming Speech Enhancement for On-device Inference
items.summary: Recent generative speech enhancement (SE) models achieve high perceptual quality, but their non-causal processing and expensive computation make them difficult to use for streaming, on-device inference. We propose StreamSE, a 20M-parameter streaming SE model that operates in the latent space of a frozen pretrained neural audio codec. At each frame, StreamSE directly regresses a clean continuous latent from the noisy continuous latent while conditioning on its own predictions from previous frames. Enhancement therefore requires a single forward pass per frame and no iterative sampling or look-ahead. We further truncate the codec's residual vector quantizer (RVQ) to its coarse levels, halving the number of tokens per frame while improving robustness to reverberation. StreamSE is the only streaming generative model in our comparison, yet it matches or exceeds the perceptual quality of the offline generative baselines. Furthermore, the complete StreamSE pipeline runs in real time on a single smartphone CPU core. Our results show that continuous latent regression provides a practical route to generative SE under fully causal, on-device streaming constraints.

items.title: A Wearable Sensor Array on Conductive Textiles for Body Surface Temperature Mapping
items.summary: Continuous monitoring of body-surface temperature distributions can provide useful information for wearable health and thermal-condition monitoring. However, practical daily-use wearable systems for distributed temperature sensing remain difficult to implement because multiple sensor nodes require power delivery and data collection across a garment. Conventional wiring increases system complexity, reduces placement flexibility, and can compromise the wearability of garment-integrated sensor arrays. To address this issue, we present a conductive-textile-based wearable temperature sensing system in which the textile itself serves as a shared bus for both DC power delivery and data communication. Each sensor node is implemented as a compact, battery-free circular board with a diameter of 21 mm and a weight of 0.9 g, integrating a commercial temperature sensor and custom circuitry for UART/DC superposition. The shared textile bus enables flexible node placement without individual wiring while supplying power to each node. Address-based half-duplex UART with master polling enables collision-free multi-node communication. To demonstrate the system-level capability, we implemented an 18-node sensor array on a garment worn by a mannequin and developed a real-time temperature mapping viewer. In a thermal scanning demonstration using warm air from a heat gun with a set temperature of approximately 50 °C, the 18-node array captured spatiotemporal temperature variations over the garment surface at a refresh rate of 99.2 Hz. These results show that the proposed conductive-textile bus can support real-time, high-refresh-rate distributed temperature mapping, providing a practical basis for garment-integrated body-surface monitoring and future multi-sensor wearable systems.

items.title: Structure-Actuation Co-Design of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators
items.summary: This paper presents a mixed discrete-continuous multiobjective bilevel framework for the structure-actuation co-design of all-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators. The upper level optimizes manipulator geometry and actuation topology, while joint-specific lower-level searches construct feasible archives of discrete motor, gearbox, and screw configurations. A system-level coordinator selects actuator packages according to hardware mass, co-design cost, and loss-aware supply energy, and the resulting actuator masses are fed back to the robot model until a mass-consistent fixed point is obtained. Evaluation on a full-pose SE(3) benchmark with a 100-kg tool payload yields eight feasible nondominated designs, all satisfying the 12 prescribed poses. Actuator-mass coupling converges in three iterations for every reported design. A fixed-design ablation shows that one-pass sequential sizing changes hardware mass by up to 2.13%, co-design cost by 10.20%, and supply energy by 9.40% in magnitude. Payload screening further reveals increasing mass-cost-energy demand and changes in competitive mechanism topology with carried load.

items.title: FRAME-C: A knowledge-augmented deep learning pipeline for classifying multi-electrode array electrophysiological signals
items.summary: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor neuron degeneration, with changes to neuronal excitability being an early phenotype for ALS identified in patients and animal models. Recent advancements in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology have enabled the generation of human iPSC-derived neuronal cultures, which, when combined with multi-electrode array (MEA) electrophysiology, provide rich spatial and temporal electrophysiological data. Traditionally, MEA data is analyzed using handcrafted features based on potentially imperfect domain knowledge, which while useful may not fully capture all the relevant characteristics inherent in the MEA data. Machine learning, in particular deep learning has the potential to automatically learn relevant characteristics (features) from raw data, without solely relying on handcrafted feature extraction. However, handcrafted features remain critical for encoding domain knowledge and improving model interpretability, especially in scenarios with limited or noisy data, as is often the case in most experimental studies. This study introduces FRAME-C, a knowledge-augmented machine learning pipeline that combines domain knowledge, raw spike waveform data, and deep learning techniques to classify MEA signals and identify ALS-specific phenotypes. FRAME-C leverages deep learning to extract important features from spike waveforms, while also incorporating handcrafted features such as spike amplitude, inter-spike interval, and spike duration, thus preserving key spatial and temporal information. We validated FRAME-C on both simulated and real-world MEA data from human iPSC-derived neuronal cultures, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing methods for MEA classification.

items.title: Stealthy bias injection attack detection based on Kullback-Leibler divergence in noisy linear systems
items.summary: This paper studies the design of observer gains to enhance the detectability of stealthy bias injection attacks (BIAs) in linear systems driven by Gaussian noise, where adversaries compromise a subset of sensors and exploit system dynamics and noise to remain stealthy. We formulate the observer-gain design as a max-min optimization problem that enhances the detectability of the least detectable BIAs, with detectability measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) subject to a prescribed attack impact. To reduce the computational complexity of the derived non-convex design problem, we consider attack onset, one-step, and steady-state detectability. We show that the Kalman filter is optimal at attack onset regardless of the subset of attacked sensors. For the one-step and steady-state cases, the observer gain design problems are approximated by bi-convex optimization problems, which can be efficiently solved using alternating optimization (AO) and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Moreover, more tractable linear matrix inequality (LMI) relaxations are developed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed stealth-aware detection framework is demonstrated through an application to a thermal system.

items.title: Optimal transmit field distribution for partially obstructed continuous radiating surfaces in near-field communication systems
items.summary: This paper deals with the optimal synthesis of aperture fields for (radiating) near-field communications in obstructed environments. A physically consistent model based on knife-edge diffraction is used to formulate the problem as a maximization in Hilbert space. The optimal solution is obtained as a matched filter that ``matches" the shape of a diffraction-induced kernel, thus linking wave propagation with signal processing methods. The framework supports hardware implementation using continuous apertures such as metasurfaces or lens antennas. This approach bridges physically grounded modeling, signal processing, and hardware design for efficient energy focusing in near-field obstructed channels.

items.title: Unsupervised Learning for Scalable Downlink Power Control in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
items.summary: In cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems, downlink power control is essential to ensure uniformly high service quality across users. Existing solutions range from computationally demanding centralized optimization to scalable distributed schemes with limited fairness. This letter proposes an unsupervised, physics-informed framework that directly optimizes max-min fairness without optimal labels or user position information. The method scales with the number of UEs, requires no retraining when the number of UEs changes, and admits a fully scalable extension. Numerical results show that it nearly doubles the worst-user spectral efficiency over existing scalable schemes.

items.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque
items.summary: Although the recent development of LLMs has paved the way for multi-modal interaction, minority languages face difficulties keeping pace. This work presents the first open Speech Language Model for Basque, designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction. Based on the LLaMA-Omni architecture, the system integrates a Latxa model as its backbone, transferring its Basque capabilities to the spoken modality by fine-tuning several modules. To address data scarcity, the English VoiceAssistant-400K corpus was translated into Basque, and the audio was synthesized using a Basque TTS. Evaluation results confirm the system's viability, achieving 3.86/5 in content quality, a 9.94% WER for spoken intelligibility, and a 3.07 UTMOS for audio quality. This work demonstrates that advanced spoken interaction systems can be developed using modular architectures and synthetic data even in low-resource languages.

items.title: Digital Twin-Guided Wireless Localization via Probabilistic Inverse Learning
items.summary: This work investigates how site-specific digital twins (DTs) can support wireless localization using simplified distributed infrastructure. We propose PRISM (Probabilistic Refinement using Inverse learning and a Site-specific Model), a DT-guided probabilistic localization scheme with single-antenna access points (APs). Localization is formulated as a probabilistic inverse problem in which a conditional proposal distribution over UE locations is learned from multi-node channel impulse responses (CIRs). The proposal generates candidate locations, with its spread regularized during training and DT consistency used to reweight candidates and refine the estimate at inference. The DT serves as an approximate forward-consistency model, avoiding assumptions of exact channel fidelity or differentiability with respect to user position. Numerical experiments demonstrate gains over data-driven and classical fingerprinting benchmarks, while achieving a median error of approximately $0.7$ m using 10 single-antenna APs. Without retraining, PRISM remains effective under degraded inference-time DT features. PRISM also yields uncertainty estimates from its proposal covariance, with empirical $χ^2$ calibration approaching ideal behavior as APs increase.

items.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
items.summary: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated posterior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covariance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph reoptimization. Surrounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% horizontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consistency checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% relative to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity decisions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.

items.title: Perceptual Differences and Preferences in Speech Enhancement
items.summary: Speech enhancement (SE) systems are commonly evaluated with objective metrics, with and without references, and with categorical subjective listening tests, all measuring speech quality and intelligibility. So far, it is unclear from such evaluations whether the processed speech is perceptually different or is preferred by everyday listeners. We investigate discrimination and preference as complementary dimensions of SE evaluation through crowdsourced triangle and pairwise preference tests across four SE systems, with comparisons to clean references. Results show that both listeners' ability to distinguish and whether they exhibit systematic preference vary across systems and substantially across acoustic conditions. Pairwise evaluations of objective metrics showed variable correlation with both discriminability and preference, motivating further studies into these novel aspects in speech enhancement evaluation.

items.title: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction
items.summary: Channel state information (CSI) prediction forecasts future channel states from historical observations, supporting transceiver design and resource allocation with reduced measurement overhead. However, existing deep learning predictors mainly encode channel knowledge in model parameters, which can limit their ability to represent diverse patterns of channel dynamics across scenes. In this paper, we propose RAG-CSI, a retrieval-enhanced Transformer framework that augments prediction with relevant historical channel knowledge. Specifically, we construct a global--local CSI knowledge store containing representative observations across scenes and historical observations from the current serving scene. We further develop joint state--dynamics retrieval (JSDR), which jointly characterizes channel states, phase dynamics, and amplitude dynamics to retrieve relevant CSI sequences. A Transformer predictor then uses cross-attention to fuse the retrieved knowledge with the current CSI history and predict future CSI with limited additional model parameters. Experiments on a multi-scene CSI dataset show overall improvements exceeding 10\% across all five evaluation metrics over the best baseline for each metric, including a 15.42\% reduction in normalized mean squared error.

items.title: Spatial MIMO Channel Rendering: A 3D Gaussian Splatting Approach
items.summary: The achievable gains of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems depend on channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition consumes pilot and feedback resources for every user in every coherence interval. Meanwhile, the propagation environment that shapes the channel persists. Exploiting such information will help to greatly reduce the overhead of CSI acquisition. This paper investigates the spatial MIMO channel rendering problem, which learns a latent beamspace channel scene from sparse observations and renders the long-term transmit and receive beam pair power map at unobserved user locations. Motivated by 3D Gaussian splatting in visual scene rendering, the proposed MIMO Gaussian splatting (MIMO-GS) represents the scene with pairs of receive and transmit 3D Gaussians, projects them from the user and base station onto the corresponding beam domains, and accumulates the beam associations through beam pair splatting. On a simulated urban scenario and measured indoor channels, MIMO-GS renders 5.5 times faster than ray tracing without a calibrated replica. Applied to multiuser beam management, the rendered maps allow users and transmit beams to be scheduled without sounding while accounting for the inter-user interference, and the net sum rate reaches 98% of the genie-aided benchmark, 19% above a position-based predictor.

items.title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
items.summary: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs), such as Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), and Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs) are increasingly deployed in power transmission grids to address congestion and improve grid utilization. However, their growing adoption necessitates coordinated operation to fully exploit their benefits. This paper presents a unified co-optimization framework that integrates NTO, DLR, and VID to alleviate congestion and minimize operational costs. NTO is modeled using a node-breaker formulation to provide enhanced switching granularity, while DLR incorporates weather-dependent parameters, including wind speed and ambient temperature, to dynamically adjust transmission limits. The resulting formulation is a mixed-integer nonlinear program due to power flow constraints with bilinear VID terms, and discrete topology decisions. To improve tractability, we propose using a McCormick relaxation approach to linearize bilinear terms. Furthermore, we propose an iterative refinement of the McCormick relaxation scheme to enhance solution accuracy. The proposed framework is validated through detailed analyses on the IEEE 118-bus system, along with additional case studies on other benchmark systems to assess scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves solution accuracy compared to standard McCormick relaxation, achieves solution quality close to the nonlinear formulation, and maintains computational efficiency.

items.title: Control and Stability of a Multilevel Power System for a Future Distribution Network
items.summary: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into distribution networks poses significant challenges to frequency and voltage stability due to their intermittent nature and low-inertia dynamics. This paper proposes a multilevel control framework for a future decarbonized power system, using energy storage systems as power buffers to mitigate frequency and voltage fluctuations. A nonlinear interconnected model is formulated to describe the multilevel aggregated dynamics of the distribution network. To reduce the operational complexity and communication overhead of the control system, a distributed linear quadratic regulator strategy is developed based on bottom-up information exchange, where each level implements local feedback control over a short time horizon. Local stability conditions are established for the open-loop nonlinear model, and the closed-loop stability is characterized by the Hurwitz property of the system matrix. Performance bounds are also derived to quantify the gap between the distributed and centralized control strategies.

items.title: Manifold meta-learning for reduced-complexity neural system identification
items.summary: System identification has greatly benefited from deep learning techniques, particularly for modeling complex, nonlinear dynamical systems with partially unknown physics where traditional approaches may not be feasible. However, deep learning models often require large datasets and significant computational resources for both training and inference due to their high-dimensional parameterizations. To address this challenge, we propose a meta-learning framework that discovers a low-dimensional manifold within the parameter space of an over-parameterized neural network architecture. This manifold is learned from an abundant meta-dataset of input-output sequences generated by a simulator of the class of systems of interest, and thereafter enables efficient model training while preserving the network's expressive power for the considered system class. Unlike bilevel meta-learning approaches, our method employs an auxiliary neural network to map datasets directly onto the learned manifold, eliminating the need for costly second-order gradient computations during meta-training and generally reducing the number of first-order updates required in inference, which could be expensive for large models. Finally, we derive a probabilistic bound that quantifies the performance gap between training on the learned low-dimensional manifold and the full parameterization. We validate our approach on a family of Bouc-Wen oscillators, which is a well-studied nonlinear system identification benchmark. We demonstrate that we are able to learn accurate models even in small-data scenarios.

items.title: A Lightweight Dual-Branch Visual Front-End for Efficient Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction
items.summary: Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction (AVTSE) uses face-related visual cues to extract a target speaker from a speech mixture. In many AVTSE systems, visual features are obtained from convolutional image encoders, and their computation may become a non-negligible part of the overall system when lightweight separation backbones are used. This work proposes a dual-branch visual front-end that reorganizes visual information according to its spatial characteristics. A compact lip region of interest is used to model local articulation cues through convolutional processing, while facial landmark coordinates are used to represent global geometric motion with a lightweight temporal convolutional network. The two representations are integrated into IIANet and SpatialNet with limited fusion overhead. Experiments on LRS3-2mix under a unified reduced training protocol show that the proposed method achieves a performance-computation trade-off close to the lightweight image-based baseline. Compared with the ResNet18-based visual encoder, it reduces the module-level visual encoding computation by more than 90% across both evaluated separation backbones, with a moderate performance gap. This comparison excludes face detection and landmark estimation and therefore applies to systems where landmark coordinates are already available from preprocessing. Demos are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Lightweight-Visual-Frontend-E46E.

items.title: Gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-free guidance mechanism
items.summary: It is well established that some animals, such as sea turtles, sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a primary cue for long-distance navigation across the vast and featureless ocean. This remarkable ability has inspired the development of bio-inspired magnetic navigation (BIMN), which seeks to mimic these animals to develop robust and frugal navigation methods. BIMN exploits the Earth's magnetic field, sometimes described as ''Nature's GPS'', as a natural navigation infrastructure, providing a potential alternative to vulnerable satellite navigation systems. However, unlike geographic coordinates, magnetic coordinates extracted from the Earth's magnetic field do not provide a one-to-one mapping to geographic locations. Different locations can exhibit similar magnetic signatures, creating ambiguity and making BIMN inherently more challenging. Despite this fundamental challenge, we demonstrate that, within predefined regions of the Earth, magnetic inclination and intensity provide sufficient information to navigate to any destination. By formulating BIMN as a gradient flow control and guidance problem, we show that the resulting gradient flow act as current that carries the system and can be controlled to guide it through intermediate waypoints toward the desired destination. The resulting framework provides a GPS-free navigation mechanism with potential applications in both engineering and biology. In engineering, it can be used to establish a geomagnetic navigation infrastructure through which prescribed routes can be defined and followed, while in biology, it can be used to analyse the migration routes of animals known to rely on magnetoreception.

items.title: Wavelet Phase Diffusion for Structurally and Semantically Consistent Sim-to-Real Translation
items.summary: Simulation-to-reality translation must bridge the appearance gap between synthetic and real domains while preserving structural and semantic consistency. Conditioning-based methods achieve spatial alignment but introduce computationally expensive control modules. Paired-data methods achieve realism but rely on complex synthesis pipelines, often altering scene geometry and semantics. Training-free editing methods avoid both constraints but lack a learned appearance prior, limiting their perceptual quality. Recently proposed phase-preserving diffusion presents a promising alternative, but Fourier-domain formulations are constrained by global spectral coupling. This coupling induces spatial artifacts such as ringing and boundary leakage, thereby degrading structural and semantic consistency. We introduce Wavelet Phase Diffusion, which addresses this through two components. First, we operate in the Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform domain, whose localized wavelet packets enable spatially adaptive phase injection without global spectral interference. Second, Low-Frequency Randomization (LFR) replaces the low-frequency packet, decoupling the model from the synthetic illumination prior and enabling in-distribution real-world appearance. Both components train on unpaired open-domain data, and introduce negligible inference overhead. The spatial locality further enables instance-level translation, where individual objects or regions are translated to photorealistic appearance independently while the surrounding scene remains untranslated. On vKITTI $\to$ KITTI image translation, $ψ$-PD outperforms prior methods in realism and semantic consistency while maintaining competitive structural alignment. For CARLA video translation, $ψ$-PD approaches the realism of paired-data methods while reducing VLM planner ADE and FDE by $5.4\%$ and $5.1\%$, respectively.

items.title: Static Multipath Suppression in Power Delay Profile of Time-Varying Channel at 28 GHz
items.summary: This paper investigates static multipath suppression in a time-varying radio channel at 28 GHz using wideband measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Two temporal differencing filters and three Doppler-domain notch filtering configurations are compared in terms of their effects on power delay profiles (PDPs) and root mean square (RMS) delay spread. The results demonstrate that all investigated methods effectively suppress stationary multipath components, improving the visibility of vehicle-related reflections. However, differences in filter frequency responses influence the relative powers of dynamic multipath components and the resulting RMS delay spread distributions. The findings highlight the importance of static multipath suppression and filter selection in characterizing time-varying propagation channels.

items.title: Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz
items.summary: Root mean square (RMS) delay spread is a key parameter characterizing temporal dispersion in radio propagation channels. Its estimation from measured power delay profiles (PDPs), however, depends strongly on the adopted power threshold. This paper investigates the sensitivity of RMS delay spread estimates to relative PDP thresholding in a time-varying millimeter-wave channel at 33 GHz. The analysis uses wideband channel sounding measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. The temporal evolution and empirical cumulative distributions of RMS delay spread are evaluated for thresholds ranging from -20 to -50 dB. Reducing the threshold increases the median RMS delay spread from approximately 140 to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB providing a practical convergence level. The results emphasize the importance of threshold selection for reliable channel characterization and consistent comparison of measurements.

items.title: Verifying Control Invariance of H-Polytopes is coNP-Complete
items.summary: We prove that verifying whether an H-polytope is control invariant for a discrete-time linear system with polytopic input constraints is \textsc{coNP}-complete. This establishes a fundamental computational complexity barrier for set-theoretic control. As an immediate consequence, the exact computation of maximal control invariant subsets of H-polytopes is \textsc{coNP}-hard. These hardness results hold regardless of whether the input constraint set is given in H- or V-representation.

items.title: Deep Behaviour Cloning of Model Predictive Control for Real-Time Operation of a Hydrogen-Diesel Dual-Fuel Engine
items.summary: Hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel (H2DF) combustion engines offer a promising pathway for decarbonising hard-to-electrify transport sectors, yet their highly nonlinear dynamics and coupled process variables demand constraint-aware control strategies. Model Predictive Control (MPC) meets these requirements but requires an online optimisation in every combustion cycle, which limits deployment on low-cost embedded hardware. This paper trains a feedforward deep neural network (DNN) by behaviour cloning (BC) to imitate an MPC expert, using 86,000 engine cycles of demonstration data collected at 1500 min-1 on a modified Cummins QSB 4.5-litre hydrogen dual-fuel engine. Two variants, one with process feedback and one without, are validated experimentally. Both track unseen fast-transient load steps (3-8 bar indicated mean effective pressure, IMEP) with normalised root mean square error (NRMSE) values of 7.80% and 9.03% against the expert's 8.01%, while keeping mean NOx and particulate matter emissions at or below those of the expert. Inference takes 2 ms or less on a Raspberry Pi 400 (ARM Cortex-A72 at 2.2 GHz), including 1 ms communication latency, compared to up to 7 ms for the MPC expert, a 3.5x speedup. Open-loop profiling on a low-cost ESP32 microcontroller at 180 MHz gives 4.3 ms per inference, 4x faster than required for the 18 ms cycle window. Beyond the training range the cloned policy saturates its controls but exceeds the pressure-rise-rate limit. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first experimental BC controller for cycle-to-cycle combustion control of an internal combustion engine (ICE), trained from demonstrations recorded on the engine itself.

items.title: Whittle Index Policy for Three State Collapsing Bandits
items.summary: Partially observable restless multi-armed bandit models have been studied for dynamic resource allocation problems under uncertainty. This paper analyzes three-state restless multi-armed bandits with partial observability. These are called collapsing bandit problems if the state of an arm (bandit) is perfectly observable when it is scheduled for allocation. The state is not observable when the arm is not scheduled. The planner has a budget constraint on the scheduling decisions in each time slot. The planner's goal is to maximize expected cumulative long term discounted reward. We study the Whittle index policy. To analyze index policy, first the $N$-armed collapsing bandit problem is decoupled into $N$ single arm problems, and convexity and monotonicity of the optimal value function in belief vector are derived using monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) ordering on state transition dynamics and monotone reward structure assumption. We next show that the optimal policy is of threshold type in belief under sufficiency conditions on the model. These sufficiency conditions depend on Lipschitz bound on the value function in the belief. We further prove the indexability for an arm using Lipschitz bound on subsidy sensitivity with minimal restrictive assumption on the transition probability model and discount factor $β.$ Our results generalize to three state and strengthen existing results on threshold policy and indexability with weaker model assumptions. We provide index computation algorithm and we present comparison of the Whittle-index, myopic policy and round-robin policies in the simulation study.

items.title: SMEBENCH: Benchmarking Neural Music Editing with Synthetized MIDI Edits
items.summary: Neural music editing requires a system to perform a requested change while preserving the musical content that should remain unchanged. Existing evaluations often lack a paired target edit, making these requirements difficult to measure separately. We introduce SMEBench, a large-scale benchmark of controlled music edits constructed by modifying symbolic MIDI performances and rendering matched source and target audio. Each example contains a source, an instruction, a paired target, edit metadata, and complementary descriptions. The benchmark covers twelve instrumentation, articulation, dynamics, and pitch operations and includes a balanced 3,600-example test set together with a smaller real-audio complement derived from multitrack recordings. The paired targets allow source preservation, target agreement, and textual compatibility to be evaluated independently. We use these references to diagnose common audio-editing metrics and benchmark six representative editing systems, showing that the metric used to rank a system can materially change the conclusion. The dataset is available at our repository.

items.title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents
items.summary: Personalized spoken agents must identify speakers before accessing user-specific memory, yet memory benchmarks typically assume correctly attributed histories. We argue that voiceprints are observations of identity, not identities themselves, and formulate online speaker-memory construction to maintain persistent user entities as acoustic evidence evolves. We introduce EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes and retrieval through a replaceable text-memory backend. We also construct LoCoMo-ID, a spoken-memory benchmark with hidden speaker identities, speaker-sensitive queries, simulated recording-condition shifts, and four-speaker identity-confusion tests. On longitudinal SMIIP-TV, genuine-probe rejection under a frozen near-enrollment threshold rises from 29.8% to 55.6% over approximately one year. On LoCoMo-ID speaker-sensitive queries, gated updating improves identity-gated QA over fixed representations by 3.86 and 11.62 percentage points under clean and shifted conditions, respectively, with no wrong-user authorizations. The advantage persists in the four-speaker test. Yet reducing fragmentation and improving QA can coexist with incorrect cross-user links, revealing a fragmentation--contamination trade-off that QA alone cannot capture.

items.title: Retrofitting centralized air compressor stations with end-use-aware predictive set-pressure control using a physics-constrained pressure-drop model
items.summary: Compressed air systems usually run at a constant set pressure well above the end-use requirement; the excess margin is wasted energy. A lightweight hierarchical nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme, retrofitted to the sequencing controller of a centralized compressor station typical of small and medium-sized plants, lowers the set pressure as far as the end-use requirement allows. It uses only two pressure gauges (receiver and one critical end-use point) and compressor data, without flow meters or piping surveys. The end-use pressure is predicted by a low-order pressure-drop model identified by least squares under stability, damping and steady-state equilibrium constraints, which serve use rather than accuracy: they let the measured pressure drop be held over the horizon with unit gain. Validated in three stages (plant data, a pipe-network simulator checked against measurements, and the actual controller, at most 1.41 s per update), the NMPC meets the required pressure under real demand and reduces the estimated annual energy consumption by 2.8 % relative to the current constant operation (9.3 % relative to 0.70 MPa). A PID cascade with the same gauge saves about as much only when tuned by a standard rule at its recommended setting from a constant-load step test, difficult in an operating plant; the NMPC needs no such test and keeps its performance with its initial model and default weights after plant expansion and network split. The margin becomes a design parameter instead of a fixed excess, and the controller's signals show where the supply system lacks headroom.

items.title: Efficient Localization of Directional Emitters via Joint Beampattern Estimation
items.summary: Localization methods designed for omnidirectional emitters degrade on directional sources, where directive beampatterns induce pronounced received signal strength (RSS) modulations. We present a direct position determination (DPD) approach that augments standard angle of arrival (AOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) measurements with RSS modulation to jointly estimate emitter position and beampattern parameters. Two algorithms reduce the four-dimensional search to two dimensions: a block coordinate ascent (BCA) method that alternates between position and beampattern subproblems, and a profile likelihood method that concentrates the beampattern parameters out via a generalized eigenvalue solve, a weighted least squares fit, and Newton refinement on the constrained Rayleigh quotient. We derive the Cramér--Rao lower bound (CRLB) and benchmark against an AOA-TDOA baseline and a prior-art approach that assumes known beamwidth and estimates only the orientation. The profile likelihood method approaches the CRLB, substantially outperforms all baselines at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and remains robust under model mismatch with the assumed von Mises template. A sensitivity analysis shows performance peaks when receivers lie on the main-lobe edges where RSS gradients are maximized.

items.title: Image Modeling: From Handcrafted Priors to Foundation Image Models
items.summary: This paper unifies six decades of image modeling, evolving from handcrafted mathematical tractable priors to solve inverse problems in imaging to data-driven deep foundation image models for both image generation and solving inverse problems, under a common Bayesian framework that formulates image modeling as an implicit or explicit probabilistic characterization of a data manifold. Every image restoration or generative task fundamentally seeks to answer the same question: What makes an image look like a real image? In the Bayesian framework, this question is encapsulated by the prior probability density p(x), or its more optimization-friendly counterpart, the log-prior log p(x). While early works in solving inverse problems, such as Tikhonov, Total Variation (TV), and Non-local priors relied on explicit handcrafted definitions of log prior to model local smoothness, modern techniques, such as Plug-and-Play (PnP) priors and Denoising Diffusion models, are rooted in algorithmic uncoupling and implicit manifold learning that apply to both inverse problems and conditional image generation. By grounding imaging inverse problems and conditional image generation under a single mathematical engine: the gradient of the log-prior, or the Stein Score Function, we bridge the gap between signal processing and machine learning communities, turning what seems like parallel developments into a single, evolution of image modeling from handcrafted analytical models to models learned from big data, demonstrating that the pursuit of the denoising score is the common thread connecting variational optimization (in MAP estimation) to posterior sampling (in modern foundation image models).

items.title: Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation for Camera-to-mmWave Radar Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides privacy?preserving human activity recognition (HAR), but sparse point clouds limit its representation of body structure and motion. We propose a cross-modal knowledge distillation framework in which a teacher trained on camera-derived two-dimensional (2D) human keypoints supervises a radar-only student. The stu?dent combines PointNet-based point-set encoding, bidirectional temporal modeling, segment-level aggregation, and lightweight shared latent-channel scaling. The teacher retains contextualized states at every time step, whereas the student summarizes the radar sequence into a small number of segments, making fixed timestamp correspondence unsuitable for feature transfer. Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation lets each student segment adaptively retrieve and aggregate teacher temporal evidence into its distillation target. Alignment denotes student-conditioned representation-space matching rather than chronological or monotonic registration. On the Multi-Modal Non-Intrusive 4D Human Dataset (MM-Fi), the method improves radar-only ac?curacy from 87.04% to 89.17%, achieving the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated established and recent distillation baselines. It also obtains higher mean accuracy and macro?averaged F1 score (macro-F1) than the radar student under most evaluated point- and frame-dropout settings. Adaptation to our independently collected millimeter-wave Office Human Ac?tivity Recognition Dataset (mmO-HAR) improves accuracy from 80.33% to 87.75%, supporting the transferability of the distilled radar representation. The teacher and alignment branch are removed after training, enabling privacy-preserving radar-only inference without additional sensing or computational branches.

items.title: Normalized Cuts and Data Clustering via Matrix Fractional Programming
items.summary: The normalized cut (NCut) problem is a fundamental one in the area of data clustering. Despite its fractional structure, the NCut problem is seldom considered from a fractional programming (FP) perspective in the existing literature. The main reason is that the conventional FP method is inadequate for this problem case: the classical Dinkelbach's transform can only handle a single ratio and hence is limited to the two-class clustering, whereas the multi-class clustering involves multiple ratio terms. This work proposes a novel so-called multidimensional quadratic transform that is capable of dealing with the multi-ratio case; it recasts the NCut problem into a bipartite matching problem---which can be immediately solved by linear search. Furthermore, we explore the connection between the proposed FP method and the minorization-maximization (MM) theory, and in turn characterize the convergence behavior of our algorithm. Finally, we conduct experiments to numerically demonstrate the advantages of the proposed FP-based algorithm in a variety of data clustering and image segmentation tasks.

items.title: Structured Wavenumber-Domain Channel Estimation for LoS XL-MIMO
items.summary: Near-field line-of-sight (LoS) channels in extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems exhibit distinctive structural properties in the wavenumber domain. In this paper, we develop a structured wavenumber-domain channel estimation framework that first obtains an initial channel estimate using classical estimators and then refines it through a windowing-based refinement step that suppresses out-of-band noise by exploiting the localized spatial-frequency power distribution. The resulting estimate is subsequently enhanced through a convex constrained formulation that exploits the sparsity and low-rank structure of the wavenumber-domain channel. The corresponding sparsity and rank constraint bounds are selected using a conservative worst-case characterization over the relative position of the transmitter and receiver. Numerical results show that the proposed framework improves estimation accuracy, particularly at low signal-to-noise ratio, by effectively leveraging the structural properties of the wavenumber-domain channel.

items.title: Perturbed Gradient Descent Algorithms are Small-Disturbance Input-to-State Stable
items.summary: This article investigates the robustness of gradient descent algorithms under perturbations. The concept of small-disturbance input-to-state stability (ISS) for discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems is introduced, along with its Lyapunov characterization. The conventional linear Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition is then extended to a nonlinear version, and it is shown that the gradient descent algorithm is small-disturbance ISS provided the objective function satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition. This small-disturbance ISS property guarantees that the gradient descent algorithm converges to a small neighborhood of the optimum under sufficiently small perturbations. As a direct application of the developed framework, we demonstrate that the LQR cost satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition, thereby establishing that the policy gradient algorithm for LQR is small-disturbance ISS. Additionally, other popular policy gradient algorithms, including natural policy gradient and Gauss-Newton method, are also proven to be small-disturbance ISS.

items.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke
items.summary: Automated polysomnography after ischemic stroke is challenging because of altered sleep-related neural activity and concurrent respiratory disturbances. Existing stroke-specific approaches mainly address sleep-stage classification, leaving joint analysis of sleep architecture and respiratory events underexplored. Moreover, adapting pretrained EEG encoders introduces a representation inconsistency when downstream models are trained on embeddings from previously seen patients but evaluated on unseen individuals. We propose MM-Net, a multimodal multi-task framework that resolves this inconsistency through cross-fitting and ridge-based embedding alignment. Sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations and engineered neural descriptors are fused with learned cardiorespiratory features through cross-attention and shared temporal modeling for simultaneous sleep staging and respiratory-event detection. On iSLEEPS (99 patients with subacute ischemic stroke), ten-fold patient-independent evaluation achieved 76.3% staging accuracy (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.656) and 0.825 respiratory-event AUC, outperforming the evaluated baselines under matched protocols. The sleep-adapted encoder improved the downstream model when its embeddings were aligned, raising staging accuracy by 1.4 percentage points over the frozen encoder ($p$ = 0.020) versus 0.2 points without alignment. MM-Net also achieved 86.4% staging accuracy on Sleep-EDF, above every single-EEG architecture reimplemented on the same recordings, and 80.3% staging accuracy with 0.889 respiratory AUC on ISRUC-I, exceeding its retrained staging baselines. Without retraining, the iSLEEPS-trained model retained respiratory AUCs of 0.833 on ISRUC-I and 0.841 on UCD. These findings support representation-consistent neural adaptation and joint physiological modeling across stroke, healthy-sleep, and sleep-disorder cohorts.

items.title: Thermal-Mass Coupled Modeling and Optimal Scheduling of Aluminum Smelting Loads for Safe Demand Response Participation
items.summary: Aluminum smelting loads (ASLs) offer substantial flexibility potential, yet their actual participation in demand response remains conservative owing to the risk of operational failures. Power adjustments disturb the electrolyte temperature and superheat, which may lead to electrolyte freeze-out or yield loss. Existing ASL demand response methods often rely on oversimplified dynamic models of the electrolytic cell's thermal behavior, such as linear models and the Equivalent Thermal Parameter (ETP) model, which may either violate temperature constraints or underestimate the available flexibility. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Thermal-Mass Coupled (TMC) dynamic model. The model captures the essential physical mechanisms of electrolytic cells, including alumina feed dynamics, ledge phase-change dynamics, and state-dependent current efficiency. The resulting nonlinear relations are reformulated into a tractable mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model using Taylor approximations and McCormick-envelope reformulations. In the illustrative PBDR and IBDR case studies, the nonlinear reference-model assessment shows that the TMC model achieves net economic improvements 122.4% and 325.1% higher, respectively, than the ETP model. The proposed framework can therefore support deeper demand response participation by aluminum smelters while explicitly assessing adherence to operational safety constraints.

items.title: A Topology-Aware Neural Network for Fault Location With Missing Measurements
items.summary: This paper proposes a topology-aware neural network-based fault locator (TANFL) for radial distribution feeders, which uses voltage and current phasors obtained after the decay of fault induced transients, as well as feeder connection relationships and line parameters, as inputs. The shared bus encoder, bus readout module, and gated line readout module work together to identify the faulty bus or line and estimate the continuous fault location on the selected line. During training, explicit missing data indicators and random bus data block masking are introduced, enabling a single trained model to handle both complete measurement sets and scenarios where any permitted bus measurement device fails. On the IEEE 15 bus feeder, this paper compares TANFL with a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) and the formula-based localization method under identical data, measurement availability scenarios, and evaluation metrics. On the test partition, TANFL outperforms the conventional MLP; with complete measurements, its line fault location performance is slightly lower than that of the formula-based method, but in the average results for scenarios with one missing bus measurement block, its accuracy is the highest among the three methods at a 5% tolerance.

items.title: Phase-Coordinated Model Predictive Control for AI Training Power Smoothing
items.summary: Periodic power fluctuations from artificial intelligence (AI) training workloads can excite oscillations in power systems. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) framework that exploits short start-time delays to mitigate power fluctuations at the computing source. By coordinating the relative phases of independent training jobs, the proposed method reduces the superposition of oscillatory power components without interrupting running jobs or requiring additional power-smoothing hardware. To obtain a tractable optimization formulation, cosine and sine projections are employed to quantify the dominant oscillatory power components, and their magnitudes are used to construct a convex quadratic power-smoothing objective. The receding-horizon framework updates launch decisions as new workload information becomes available while maintaining scheduling feasibility under limited computation time. Numerical results demonstrate reductions of 74.39\% in mean-square power fluctuations within the 0.2--2-Hz band and 46.6\% in power standard deviation, with an average launch delay of 2.188~s. All launch deadlines are satisfied, and the maximum end-to-end computation time is 0.390~s, below the 0.50-s MPC update period.

items.title: A Singularity Avoiding Track Model for Race Car Optimization
items.summary: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. The surface is a Monge patch, parametrised by a curvilinear arc-length coordinate measured along the minimum-curvature line (MCL) and a signed lateral offset, with a height polynomial of user-selectable degree capturing the cross-sectional elevation profile. The choice of MCL as the reference line is deliberate since anchoring the same surface on the geometric centre-line can cause adjacent normals to cross inside the drivable region on tight corners. The resulting non-injective parametrisation assigns multiple curvilinear addresses to the same three-dimensional point and returns invalid road geometry. The MCL is obtained from a quadratic program that minimises integrated curvature subject to track-boundary, periodicity, and jerk-regularisation constraints. By reducing total curvature while remaining within the track bounds, the MCL moves the region of parametrisation breakdown outside the drivable strip on all circuits studied, keeps the normal map injective across the full track width, and yields a more linear time-to-arc-length transformation for minimum lap-time problems. The fitted surface and the associated track widths are exported as periodic piecewise-quintic $C^4$ B-splines, solved as a nonlinear program.

items.title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations
items.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange must coordinate access to limited chargers with energy supply while considering both energy cost and carbon emissions. This paper proposes a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) for dynamic vehicle scheduling (VS) and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) controller for carbon-aware energy dispatch (ED). SFGH assigns EVs according to reductions in service delays, and TD3 controls battery operation to balance energy costs and carbon emissions while meeting the resulting charging demand. The model allows both PV and battery exports, accounting for export revenue and carbon credits. Simulations on year-long case studies show that SFGH--TD3 achieves the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) configurations.

items.title: Programmable Sequential Memory in Coupled Oscillator Networks
items.summary: The Hopfield network established that static memories can be stored as energy minima of an energy-based model. Real intelligent agents, however, must navigate sequences of memories rather than isolatedcsnapshots. Biological cortex addresses this through a separation of timescales, where fast synaptic dynamics encode individual states while slow neuromodulatory processes govern transitions between them. Inspired by this organization, we propose a sequential memory architecture that is fully continuous and admits exponential storage capacity. The architecture is programmable, since the transition structure is carried by a mechanism that is decoupled from the stored patterns, driven by the input context, and free to be chosen, optimized, or learned from data. Specifically, we construct an autonomous three-timescale dynamical system with three coupled layers. A fast Kuramoto layer stores phase patterns as exponentially stable phase-locked configurations, an intermediate recognition layer sets the dwell times, and a slow attention layer routes the transitions.
