With $64$ transmit antennas and $4$ data streams, it attains $96.3\%$ of the digital sum-rate using only $8$ RF chains. Furthermore, under highly frequency-selective channels and using $4$ RF chains, it provides a $48\%$ sum-rate gain over the conventional hybrid design.

items.title: Fair Dynamic Operating Envelopes using Distributed Multi-Period Optimal Power Flow and Jain Index for Active Distribution Networks
items.summary: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) are increasingly used to publish time-varying export limits that keep distribution networks within operational limits. Purely technical DOE allocation, however, can systematically privilege electrically favorable prosumers, while embedding fairness directly into a single-period optimal power flow (OPF) objective mixes network feasibility, equity and efficiency in a way that obscures the cost of fairness. This paper proposes a two-stage, multi-period framework that addresses both of these. Initially, a technical distributed OPF computes network-feasible export envelopes. The subsequent stage then applies a dynamic aggregate export budget and redistributes capacity through cumulative proportional fairness, limiting the additional curtailment by an admissible efficiency budget. The resulting fair DOEs are treated as first-stage decisions, while battery storage provides scenario-dependent recourse under demand and renewable uncertainty. The operational problem is solved by a calibrated regional alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) on a lossless LinDistFlow model and independently validated using AC power flow. We observe a trade-off between increases in curtailment \emph{versus} improvements on fairness, as expected, reaching Jain fairness indices close to unity. Results show that considering both storage (which alleviates curtailment impact) and multi-period fairness (which increases curtailment) is an interesting approach for modern DOE design, which in turn requires a multi-period, co-designed approach.

items.title: Multi-Agentic AI for Fairness-Aware and Accelerated Multi-modal Large Model Inference in Real-world Mobile Edge Networks
items.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) has transformed applications in natural language processing and content creation, yet centralized inference remains hindered by high latency, limited customizability, and privacy concerns. Deploying large models (LMs) in mobile edge networks emerges as a promising solution. However, it also poses new challenges, including heterogeneous multi-modal LMs with diverse resource demands and inference speeds, varied prompt/output modalities that complicate orchestration, and resource-limited infrastructure ill-suited for concurrent LM execution. In response, we propose a Multi-Agentic AI framework for latency- and fairness-aware multi-modal LM inference in mobile edge networks. Our solution includes a long-term Global Planning Agent, a short-term Prompt Scheduling Agent, and multiple on-node LM Deployment Agents, all powered by foundation language models. These agents cooperatively optimize prompt routing and LM deployment through natural language reasoning over runtime telemetry and historical experience. To evaluate its performance, we further develop a city-wide testbed that supports network monitoring, containerized LM deployment, intra-server resource management, and inter-server communications. Experiments demonstrate that our solution reduces average end-to-end latency by 42.9% compared with a state-of-the-art online-learning baseline and by 80.6% compared with the full-activation baseline, while maintaining a mean service-type Jain's index of 0.925. Moreover, our solution adapts quickly without fine-tuning, offering a generalizable solution for optimizing GenAI services in edge environments.

items.title: Uniform observability criteria for linear time-varying systems
items.summary: Verifying uniform observability of a linear time-varying system generally requires its state-transition matrix. This paper develops necessary and sufficient conditions that can be checked directly from the coefficient matrices for two classes of systems. For constant dynamics with real spectrum and a measurable, essentially bounded output matrix, uniform observability is equivalent to persistent excitation of the output matrix on each eigenspace. An equivalent condition requires persistent excitation of the Kalman observability stack. The second result concerns cascades with a constant observable measured subsystem coupled to a hidden state. Under uniform regularity assumptions, linear combinations of output derivatives eliminate the measured state and yield an equivalent observability test for the hidden dynamics. When those dynamics have real spectrum, the test reduces to excitation on each eigenspace intersected with the kernel of the direct measurements. An application to arbitrary-order integrator chains with measurements of ranges to fixed anchors gives an exact excitation condition for the associated lifted LTV system. A second application treats direct hidden measurements and compares the condition with existing sufficient tests.

items.title: Dual Gradient Consensus for Adaptive Learning to Transient Out-of-Distribution Disturbances in Quadrotor Control
items.summary: Quadrotor trajectory tracking under unmodeled disturbances often relies on online residual adaptation, but short out-domain residuals can corrupt the learned disturbance model when constant-step updates treat every residual gradient uniformly. We propose Dual Gradient Consensus (DGC), an adaptive-learning method for mixed in-domain/out-domain disturbances that retains the random Fourier feature model, offline BPTT policy, and least-squares adaptation of a prior domain-adaptive residual policy (DAPL) while modifying the online update step size. DGC compares each residual gradient with long- and short-term gradient memories, classifies the current adaptation regime, and uses a confidence map to suppress unreliable updates while recovering adaptation after persistent domain shifts. We evaluate DGC in numerical quadrotor trajectory tracking under four residuals that mix an in-domain component with short out-domain events. Compared with $L_1$-augmented MPC, RFF-based MPC, constant-step DAPL, and a frozen-parameter baseline, DGC achieves the lowest mean position RMSE in all four cases.

items.title: Multi-view Semantic-aware Resource Allocation for Edge AI
items.summary: Semantic communication is emerging as a pivotal paradigm to overcome wireless resource scarcity in 6G networks. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework for semantics-aware resource allocation in multi-user Edge AI. We extend the Opportunistic Information Bottleneck (OIB) to a multi-view setting, termed the Multi-view Gaussian Information Bottleneck (MGIB), by fusing complementary source views without variational approximation or network retraining. A resource allocation framework is then formulated for joint compression-level selection, transmission mode selection (i.e., the number of active sources per group), and PRB assignment. The problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), solved efficiently via a proposed Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) algorithm, and benchmarked against the NP-hard optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed LR scheme achieves near-optimal utility, and doubles PRB efficiency versus average allocation.

items.title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
items.summary: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

items.title: Symbolic Direct Construction of Augmented Systems for Levenberg-Marquardt Power Flow
items.summary: Levenberg-Marquardt power flow (LMPF) addresses ill-conditioned equations and provides least-squares stationary points for infeasible operating requests. Conventional implementations form damped normal equations, where J^T J introduces fill, squares the spectral condition number of the undamped part, and adds sparse-product cost. We propose an augmented LMPF formulation with a symbolic-permutation-based Jacobian operator that fills the augmented blocks directly. We prove that the matrix is symmetric quasi-definite for positive damping, enabling fixed-order, pivot-free QDLDL factorization. This property also motivates the solver choice: KLU value-only refactorization can reuse an unsuitable pivot order, forcing fresh full factorizations on difficult LMPF trajectories. We further introduce one-probe adaptive trust-region initialization for the radius and damping. Direct assembly is 7.5-11.9x faster than the fastest coordinate-list path and 18.0-58.8x faster than cached normal-equation sparse-product formation; QDLDL reduces numerical refactorization and triangular-solve time by up to 3.40x on identical matrices. Adaptive initialization solves flat-started RTE cases in 19-25 factorizations, 7.5-11.6x faster than reproduced three-step LM. On case2383wp, our 84-iteration run performs 84 factorizations and 168 resolves in 237 ms, versus published times of 200.780-441.72 s with fewer outer iterations, corresponding to speedups of 847-1860x. These results require complete factorization and resolve accounting and reveal initialization and legacy-parameter effects. DC-initialized NR exhibits fast quadratic convergence throughout every tested solvable loading range, motivating clearer, reproducible definitions of ill-conditioned power-flow benchmarks.

items.title: Reinsertion-Aware Parameter Estimation of the WECC Composite Load Model via Closed-Loop Equivalent-Network Co-Estimation
items.summary: Measurement-based parameter estimation of the WECC composite load model (CMLD) commonly relies on voltage replay, where measured voltage is imposed on an isolated CMLD and its parameters are optimized to reproduce measured active and reactive power. However, this open-loop formulation neglects the two-way dynamic interaction between the load and grid, potentially causing large errors when the estimated model is reinserted into dynamic grid simulations. To address this limitation, we propose a closed-loop parameter estimation framework that alternately estimates the CMLD parameters and a five-parameter equivalent network representing the external grid. This framework restores load-grid interaction during estimation and enables voltage, active power, and reactive power to jointly constrain the parameter estimation. Compared with four baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves the highest reinsertion accuracy in both the CMLD benchmark and transmission and distribution (T&D) co-simulation environments. In the T&D case, it reduces active-power, reactive-power, and voltage errors by 73%, 64%, and 62%, respectively. The identified model also maintains improved reinsertion accuracy under disturbances not used for estimation, demonstrating transferability beyond the identification event.

items.title: Space-Time Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces for Doppler-Resilient LEO Broadcasting
items.summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade programmable layers in front of a feed. In the SIM designs reported so far, including those proposed for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, the layer coefficients are space-only controls or are varied randomly in time to support opportunistic scheduling, so that every radiated beam carries the frequency of the feed. This paper introduces space-time SIMs (ST-SIMs), whose layers are modulated in time and use the temporal dimension of the stack deterministically: each spatial mode of the aperture is paired with its own prescribed frequency translation. The application is LEO broadcasting, where a common waveform reaches terminals with different Doppler shifts, and any common Doppler correction leaves residuals of up to half the Doppler span. We derive the harmonic-domain model of the stack, solve the minimum-energy space-frequency synthesis in closed form, and prove that full column rank of the steering matrix is necessary and sufficient for decoupling K terminal-specific translations, a result that extends to groups of terminals. We further propose a phase-only synthesis algorithm with guaranteed stationarity, together with quantization and control-rate laws. Simulations at 20 GHz over 50 random drops show that a four-layer ST-SIM with a single radio-frequency chain removes the Doppler floor of a static SIM for footprint radii above about 45 km and, under the ideal phase-only model and at equal radiated peak energy, approaches ideal digital per-terminal precompensation within 0.5 dB for resolvable terminals, whereas, in the evaluated geometries, a single time-modulated layer cannot synthesize the required modes.

items.title: GNSS Anomaly Detection in Urban Canyons: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Visibility Inference
items.summary: Reliable GNSS positioning in dense urban environments depends on assessing satellite visibility and identifying measurements degraded by non-line-of-sight (NLOS) reception and multipath. This survey organizes reception-state inference into three complementary evidence families: receiver-side signals, 3D maps and environmental models, and auxiliary sensors. Receiver-side approaches span antenna/electromagnetic, tracking/baseband, and observable-domain evidence, interpreted through rule-based, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. Map-based approaches are examined by reviewing environmental representations and methods such as geometric screening, shadow matching, 3D ray tracing, and neural implicit visibility prediction. IMU, camera, and LiDAR measurements provide complementary kinematic, visual, and geometric evidence for online screening. Across these families, we compare accuracy, interpretability, hardware and calibration requirements, map dependence, computational cost, and suitability for real-time deployment. We identify open challenges in dataset quality and labeling, domain generalization, map freshness, and resource-efficient implementation. The resulting synthesis connects signal processing, environmental modeling, and sensor fusion to guide the design of robust urban GNSS measurement-screening systems.

items.title: End-to-End Neural Modeling of EM Response and Design Performance for Free-Form RFIC Passives
items.summary: Passive matching networks are critical components in radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFICs), but their design is bottlenecked by expensive finite-difference-based electromagnetic (EM) simulation. We propose an end-to-end neural framework for free-form RFIC passives that predicts both EM response and downstream design performance under varying frequency and circuit contexts, combining a frequency-conditioned neural simulator with a circuit-conditioned neural solver. To improve design performance prediction, the simulator outputs a neural EM response consisting of both the explicit EM response and a complementary response, together with a dependence regularizer that encourages the two responses to capture orthogonal information. To evaluate the proposed framework, we construct a large-scale dataset of free-form passive layouts, synthesized from both expert-designed contours and random paths. Our 21M-parameter model achieves high accuracy across a broad frequency range, circuit contexts and passive matching settings, with $R^2>0.98$ for almost all targets, while providing orders-of-magnitude faster evaluation than traditional EM simulation. Code available at https://github.com/ETH-IDEAS/RFIC-NeuralSim.

items.title: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
items.summary: In this project, I explored controller design and trajectory generation for a quadrotor. Differential flatness was used for trajectory generation based on one of the references. A minimum snap trajectory is generated from the given algorithm based on waypoint navigation, and a simple proportional plus derivative (PD) controller is used to track the trajectories. Simulation results are presented which generate smooth trajectories for position and velocity of the quadrotor.

items.title: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator
items.summary: This paper presents two controllers for a quadrotor equipped with a two-DOF robot manipulator that physically interacts with the environment. Cartesian impedance and adaptive sliding mode controllers are implemented and compared for a simple hovering task in the presence of some bounded disturbance. A full dynamic model is developed, and the two above controllers are implemented with the same initial conditions and desired position.

items.title: In-Context Adapter Generation for Compositional Generalization in Large Audio Language Models
items.summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance on standard speech and audio understanding tasks, yet their ability to systematically generalize to novel task compositions remains underexplored. Taking a meta-learning view, we extend Text-to-LoRA (T2L) to LALMs, generating instruction-conditioned LoRA adapters with a Transformer hypernetwork rather than learning a single fixed adapter shared across instructions. To exploit fine-grained task information, we introduce in-context adapter generation (ICAG), a token-level hypernetwork architecture; we call the resulting method T2L-ICAG. We evaluate this approach on two representative LALMs using SIFT-50M for supervised fine-tuning and construct a controlled compositional evaluation suite covering five task classes. Across two LALM backbones, T2L-ICAG consistently improves over static LoRA and also the global embedding-based T2L baseline. Coverage and capacity analyses further show that these gains are larger on structurally out-of-domain tasks and cannot be explained by parameter count alone. These results suggest that generating task-specific adapters from instructions is a promising direction for improving compositional generalization of LALMs.

items.title: AV-QTSS: Class-Query Target Sound Spatialization in Multi-Source 360$^\circ$ Videos
items.summary: Spatial audio is central to immersive 360$^\circ$ media, yet existing audio-visual spatialization renders the scene as a whole, leaving no control over an individual source. We introduce Audio-Visual Query-conditioned Target Sound Spatialization (AV-QTSS): given a monaural multi-source mixture, a 360$^\circ$ video and a class query from the 13-class DCASE sound-event ontology, it generates the first-order Ambisonics (FOA) signal of the queried source alone. The omnidirectional mixture contains no explicit spatial cues, so direction has to be inferred from the video, where several objects may sound at once. We propose a query-conditioned dense binding localizer that predicts a spherical probability map over the whole scene, coupled to the renderer so both are optimized jointly. Experiments with one to four concurrent sources show improved localization and spatial accuracy relative to established methods and ablated variants, and the localizer transfers to real 360$^\circ$ recordings after adaptation.

items.title: Optimal Steady-State Regulation of Nonlinear Systems: A Feedback Optimization Approach
items.summary: This paper studies the optimal steady-state regulation problem for a class of nonlinear systems. The regulated output is required to track a trajectory that minimizes a steady-state cost depending on both the output and the exo-system. To characterize the desired steady-state behavior, we introduce a generalized regulator equation and develop a two-layer framework. The optimization layer generates the optimal reference online through a steady-state generator combined with gradient-feedback optimization dynamics, while the control layer employs backstepping to stabilize the plant and achieve the desired optimal steady-state regulation. Under suitable immersion and minimum-phase assumptions, global asymptotic stability is established.

items.title: Recursive Neighbor Pruning: Decentralized Community Detection with Certified Behavior from Saturated Opinion Dynamics
items.summary: Detecting communities, i.e., groups of densely connected nodes, usually requires a central entity that knows the whole network. We study Recursive Neighbor Pruning (RNP), a fully decentralized alternative inspired by social learning. Each agent holds a private opinion but only shows its neighbors a coarse public action, namely its opinion amplified and clipped to a fixed range. Agents repeatedly move their opinion toward the actions of their neighbors and, once opinions settle, drop the links with neighbors whose action has the opposite sign. Repeating this procedure on the remaining network splits it into communities, without any agent knowing the network or the number of communities. We use tools from nonlinear control to characterize this behavior. We show that splitting requires the amplification to exceed a threshold set by how strongly the network is bottlenecked. We also show that a group in which every member has enough of its links inside the group can no longer be split once its members agree, and that a single run separates such groups exactly when started from suitable opinions. Finally, we bound the number of runs and messages. On two standard families of synthetic networks, RNP is as accurate as the best centralized method as long as each node has fewer than about forty percent of its links outside its community, and it fails close to the value predicted by our analysis. It is more accurate than two decentralized competitors below this level, but exchanges many more messages.

items.title: Synergizing Wireless Foundation Models and LLMs: A Multi-Task Framework for MA Systems
items.summary: While movable antennas (MAs) provide enhanced spatial flexibility through dynamic repositioning, they confront critical challenges in acquiring complete channel state information (CSI) and efficiently optimizing antenna positions. Encouragingly, wireless foundation models (WFMs) capture generalizable channel priors for high-quality CSI extrapolation, while large language models (LLMs) enable parameter-efficient, token-level optimization for wireless tasks. In this paper, we synergistically integrate a WFM and an LLM into a multi-task framework for MA systems. First, to address the mismatch between existing WFM pre-training and MA channel characteristics, we develop an MA-oriented ``ExtLWM'' based on the large wireless model (LWM) architecture. Second, we design a unified ExtLWM-Connector-LLM architecture that flexibly adapts to different MA configurations without structural redesign. Third, we reformulate discrete MA positioning as a sequential decision-making problem, where candidate positions are represented by numerical tokens and optimized using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to exploit the serial generation capability of the LLM. Finally, a multi-stage training strategy is developed to maintain multi-task performance under limited training samples while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results show that ExtLWM can produce high-quality channel embeddings while outperforming various benchmarks in CSI extrapolation. Meanwhile, the proposed LLM-based approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and computational complexity.

items.title: RIS-Assisted Downlink Pinching-Antenna Systems With NLOS Environments
items.summary: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted downlink pinching-antenna system (PASS) in the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) users caused by unavoidable obstacles. An RIS is deployed to extend the coverage of the physically constrained PASS by establishing virtual line-of-sight (LOS) links. To improve system performance, we propose a zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming-based alternating optimization (AO) framework that minimizes the transmit power by jointly optimizing the RIS reflection coefficients and pinching-antenna (PA) activation positions. Specifically, the RIS reflection coefficients are optimized using the Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) method, while a novel projected gradient-based method is developed to efficiently optimize the PA activation positions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AO framework outperforms baseline schemes in terms of both transmit power and computational efficiency under different system configurations including the rate requirements and RIS sizes.

items.title: Forecasting Ionospheric Irregularities on GNSS Lines of Sight Using Dynamic Graphs with Ephemeris Conditioning
items.summary: Most data-driven ionospheric models operate on gridded products, which do not preserve the time-varying sampling structure of satellite-based sensing. We instead model the ionosphere as a dynamic graph over ionospheric pierce points, with connectivity that evolves as satellite positions change. Because satellite trajectories are predictable, the graph topology over the forecast horizon can be constructed in advance. We exploit this property to condition forecasts on the future graph structure, which we term ephemeris conditioning. This enables prediction on lines of sight (LoS) that appear only in the forecast horizon. We evaluate our framework on Global Navigation Satellite System data from a co-located receiver pair in Singapore spanning 2023 to 2025. The task is forecasting irregularities defined by the Rate of TEC Index (ROTI) up to 2 hours ahead as per-node binary classification. The resulting model, IonoDGNN, achieves a Brier Skill Score (BSS) of 0.55 and an area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) of 0.77. These correspond to improvements over persistence of 53% in BSS and 58% in PR-AUC, with larger gains at longer lead times. Ablations confirm that graph structure and ephemeris conditioning each contribute meaningfully. Under simulated coverage dropout, the model retains predictive skill on affected nodes through spatial message passing from observed neighbors. Compared to interpolation baselines, the proposed model achieves better recovery, especially at higher dropout levels. These results suggest that dynamic graph forecasting on evolving LoS is a viable alternative for ionospheric modeling. The project and the dataset are available at https://github.com/Mert-chan/IonoDGNN.

items.title: Semantic-Aware Deformable Feature Alignment for Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound
items.summary: Accurate segmentation of thyroid nodules in ultrasound images is essential for clinical diagnosis yet remains challenging due to boundary ambiguity, speckle noise, and complex geometric variability. Existing methods often fail to reconcile global semantic understanding with precise local boundary delineation, leading to errors in irregular cases. To address this, we propose SDFA-Net, a framework built on semantic-aware deformable feature alignment that explicitly decouples the learning of robust global semantics and detailed local geometry. Our approach integrates three main components: a clustered linear context aggregation module for efficient long-range dependency modeling, an affinity-driven token modulation mechanism using dynamic prototypes to suppress background interference, and a cascaded spatially-aligned feature fusion strategy that achieves sub-pixel geometric alignment across multiple resolution stages. By filtering and aligning multi-scale features, SDFA-Net ensures robust fusion that is both semantically meaningful and geometrically accurate. We validate our method through extensive experiments on three public thyroid ultrasound datasets, TN3K, TUCC, and DDTI, where it demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework offers a generalizable solution for precise medical image segmentation in boundary-ambiguous scenarios.

items.title: Fading Suppression in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using Frequency-Domain Replica Reconstruction and Noise-Whitened Principal Component Combining
items.summary: Frequency-selective Rayleigh fading in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (phi-OTDR) calls for effective diversity, but existing rotated-vector-sum (RVS) combining of nonoverlapping subbands incurs a spatial-resolution penalty. In this letter, we propose frequency-domain replica reconstruction and noise-whitened principal component combining (PCC) that combines a full-band replica and overlapping subbands using fixed weights estimated across probing periods after whitening correlated replica noise. This approach retains wider subbands and reduces reliance on noisy first-period alignment, balancing diversity with nominal spatial resolution. Experiments over approximately 7.1 km of fiber with 16-microsecond linear frequency-modulated (LFM) pulses recover 500-Hz vibrations with reduced background phase excursions and a 2.46-2.76-dB improvement in the vibration-to-background ratio (VBR) over the first-period RVS.

items.title: ADReasoner: Acoustic-Linguistic Cue-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Explainable Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Speech
items.summary: Speech-based Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection holds significant promise due to its scalable and non-invasive nature. However, current Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs), similar to conventional AD detection systems, still treat AD detection primarily as a simple categorical classification task. This paradigm provides limited interpretability of predictions, while leaving the inherent expressiveness and reasoning capabilities of SpeechLLMs largely underutilized. In this work, we take the first step toward reframing AD detection as a deep reasoning task via Reinforcement Learning (RL). We propose ADReasoner, an RL-enhanced SpeechLLM designed to generate accurate diagnostic predictions with interpretable rationales grounded in fine-grained acoustic-linguistic cues. To achieve this, we first systematically construct ADCoT-7K, an AD speech reasoning dataset combining real data and our quality-filtered synthetic data, where each instance features Chain-of-Thought (CoT) annotations and detailed captions. Second, observing the weak perception of AD-related acoustic-linguistic cues in current SpeechLLMs, we leverage Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to develop a cue-perception-enhanced foundation model, ADReasoner-Base, thereby improving AD speech understanding. Third, alongside two standard rule-based rewards, we introduce a reasoning reward and a reasoning-label consistency reward into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for RL. Furthermore, a shrinkage mechanism is employed to suppress misleading reasoning signals, while a gating mechanism progressively introduces both rewards to stabilize policy training. Experiments on three AD datasets (Pitt, PROCESS-1, PROCESS-2) demonstrate that ADReasoner outperforms previous state-of-the-art models in both detection performance and explanation quality, advancing AD detection toward interpretable reasoning from speech.

items.title: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Adaptive Stabilizability of Continuous-Time Markov Jump Linear Stochastic Systems
items.summary: The purpose of this paper is to provide a mathematically rigorous solution to a well-known problem in stochastic adaptive control, i.e., to find the weakest possible structural condition for global stabilizability of continuous-time Markov jump linear stochastic systems with known candidate modes but with an unobservable Markov parameter process. Under some regularity assumptions, it is shown that the necessary and sufficient condition for global adaptive stabilizability hinges on the solvability of the same coupled Riccati equations as in the non-adaptive case. This result highlights a fundamental difference between the continuous-time case considered here and the discrete-time case studied earlier by Xue and Guo (2001), in which the coupled Riccati equations for adaptive and non-adaptive stabilizability are different.

items.title: Evaluating Wi-Fi HaLow for Next-Generation Capsule Endoscopy
items.summary: Capsule endoscopy is limited by its wireless link: insufficient throughput restricts image resolution and frame rate, whereas high-rate radios typically use higher carrier frequencies that experience greater attenuation through tissue. This work evaluates Wi-Fi HaLow (IEEE 802.11ah), a sub-GHz Wi-Fi standard, as an image link for capsule endoscopy. Across all tested combinations of modulation and coding scheme and bandwidth, the saturation TCP throughput reached 15.55 Mbps, and the fastest configuration also achieved the lowest energy per bit. Through power optimization strategies, the combined power consumption of the HaLow module and microcontroller at 1 frame per second (FPS) was reduced from 101.70 to 14.00 mW, which is comparable to that of Bluetooth Low Energy systems. In a simulated in vivo setting, the default rate control selected the highest tested MCS and bandwidth, indicating sufficient link quality; this configuration also had the lowest measured power in both the 1 FPS mode (13.59 mW) and the 30 FPS mode (174.21 mW). The capsule-to-receiver latency was 20.68 ms for a 24 KB frame, while the receiver-to-capsule latency was 4.77 ms for a command; this low-latency bidirectional communication supports real-time detection and manipulation for next-generation capsule endoscopy.

items.title: Cascaded Posterior Sampling With Diffusion Priors for highly Accelerated MRI
items.summary: Diffusion models are powerful priors for inverse problems, including accelerated MRI. However, modeling the distribution of high-resolution images requires large networks with high computational cost. We propose a posterior sampling framework that uses cascaded diffusion models as multiscale priors. Conditioned on a coarse image, the distribution of fine-scale detail is local and well conditioned, and it can therefore be captured by a small network. Similarly, a small unconditional network is sufficient to represent low-resolution images, and it is used to recover the coarse image from the k-space center. This estimate then conditions the high-resolution prior, which is combined with all measurements to recover the final image. Both priors are trained on images alone, so they apply to any sampling pattern, and data consistency remains linear at every scale. In multi-coil brain MRI, the proposed method improves on the best single-scale diffusion baseline by 4-6 dB in PSNR at 15x acceleration, while each of its separately trained networks is about 10x smaller. The gain grows as the problem becomes more ill-posed, and ablations show that it arises from informative low-resolution conditioning.

items.title: Environment-Adaptive Dynamic KV Cache for Multi-Path Parameter Prediction
items.summary: Multipath parameter prediction provides a structured and physically interpretable representation of wireless propagation for environment-aware communication systems. However, existing Transformer-based methods repeatedly encode the same environment when predicting multiple BS--UE links, resulting in redundant computation. To address this issue, we propose an environment-conditioned dynamic KV caching framework for multipath parameter prediction. Specifically, we decouple environment-dependent computation from BS--UE geometry, enabling environment-side representations and intermediate KV states to be reused across multiple link queries while only the geometry branch is updated. Building on this reusable cache, we further introduce a dynamic compression mechanism that uses environment-side attention scores to retain informative tokens and adaptively allocates a fixed cache budget across Transformer layers. Experiments on the WAIR-D dataset show that the proposed method reduces KV memory from 0.2500 MB to 0.1406 MB, while the delay NMSE increases only slightly from 0.0673 to 0.0678. Code is available at https://github.com/LZhaoyang/kv.

items.title: AGENS: Agentic Link Construction for Environment and Intent Aware 6G Communication
items.summary: The emergence of diverse intelligent services is driving 6G networks toward an intelligent communication ecosystem with increasingly complex operating scenarios. However, existing AI-based communication methods mainly focus on isolated tasks or individual physical-layer mod- ules, which is insufficient for AI-native 6G systems that must jointly perceive dynamic environments, understand specific user intents, coordinate multiple coupled PHY-layer modules, and remain compatible with existing communication infrastructures. To address this gap, this paper, for the first time, explores auto- matic environment- and intent-aware full-link construction, which aims to generate executable PHY-layer configurations according to channel conditions and service requirements. We propose AGENS, an agentic communication decision-making framework for AI-native 6G link construction. Rather than replacing the existing PHY-layer protocol stack with a black-box end-to-end model, AGENS operates on top of the modular communication framework and jointly optimizes end-to-end PHY-layer configu- rations. Specifically, AGENS encodes CSI and natural-language user instructions, aligns communication states with user intents through cross-modal fusion, and leverages a pretrained LLM for intent-aware reasoning. An LSTM-based sequential action generator further captures dependencies among coupled sub- actions and produces structured full-link strategies. To enable stable training in the high-dimensional discrete action space, AGENS adopts a two-stage learning framework, where heuristic supervised initialization is followed by multi-objective reinforce- ment learning to jointly optimize reliability, throughput, and power consumption.

items.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
items.summary: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Experiments on benchmark datasets evaluate the proposed framework in surgical phase recognition and target tracking, including scenarios involving occlusion and entity overlap. Phantom experiments further demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution performance compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

items.title: Do Bio-Inspired Algorithms Save Energy in Data Centres? Separating Server Packing from Migration Search in Virtual Machine Consolidation
items.summary: Energy-efficient virtual machine (VM) consolidation matters as data centre electricity demand rises. Bio-inspired metaheuristics, including ant colony optimisation (ACO), particle swarm optimisation (PSO), and genetic algorithms, have reported substantial energy savings. However, these improvements are commonly evaluated against conventional allocation policies that differ in both initial VM placement and subsequent migration optimisation, making it difficult to determine the contribution of metaheuristic search. This study reproduces an existing consolidation implementation in CloudSim Plus and introduces a matched control that retains the same initial packing and empty-host deactivation mechanisms but excludes migration search. ACO, PSO, and a modified genetic algorithm (MGA) are evaluated across two fleet configurations and four workload regimes, with ten stochastic replications per condition. The matched control achieves energy savings of 0.8-81.4% relative to the spreading baseline, the amount available falling sharply as load rises, without migrations or incomplete workload execution. Across 24 comparisons, metaheuristic search increases energy consumption in 11 cases, produces identical outcomes in seven, and reduces consumption in six. Of these, ten increases and five reductions remain statistically significant after Holm correction. Five of the six apparent reductions coincide with unfinished tasks and disappear after normalisation by delivered computational work. Only ACO under light heterogeneous load retains a 3.22-percentage-point improvement (95% CI 2.96-3.47). These findings demonstrate that initial packing and host deactivation account for most of the measured energy savings in the examined implementations, highlighting the importance of matched control conditions and workload-completion measures for reliable evaluation of VM consolidation algorithms.

items.title: Optimal Linear Filtering of Markov Jump Systems
items.summary: This paper deals with the optimal state estimation problem for discrete-time Markov jump linear systems in the sense of linear minimum mean-square error where the noises corrupting the system are mode-dependent and need not be Gaussian. An orthogonal projection extension-based equation (OPEBE) is established, which can decompose a random vector into several parts where the random vector contains conditional expectation of another random vector. Using the OPEBE and some results obtained in this paper, an optimal linear filter for the system under consideration is proposed. The computational and storage load of the proposed filter does not increase with time. Also, the proposed filter is finite-dimensionally computable and has a recursive structure. Computer simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness and performance of the proposed optimal linear filter.

items.title: Dynamic Metasurface-Enabled Generalized Pinching-Antenna Systems
items.summary: This article investigates dynamic metasurfaces as an electronic realization of generalized pinching antennas (GPA). By jointly optimizing the locations and radiation coefficients of activated elements, the dynamic metasurface-enabled GPA (DM-GPA) architecture exploits additional design flexibility to enhance spatial reconfigurability beyond that attainable through antenna placement in the conventional pinching-antenna system (PASS). Based on this architecture, we study weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization for multiuser downlink transmission. 1) For two-user transmission, the sum-rate improvement of DM-GPA over conventional PASS is quantified through a lower bound that reveals when the benefit of channel orthogonalization achieved by adjusting the radiation coefficients outweighs the channel power loss caused by the Lorentzian constraint. Furthermore, when conventional PASS yields a rank-deficient channel, DM-GPA is shown to achieve spatial multiplexing and transmit diversity, with a strict sum-rate advantage at sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratios. 2) For general multiuser transmission, a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based alternating optimization algorithm is developed for joint pinching beamforming and digital precoder design. A sequential element-wise search is developed to optimize the locations of the activated elements, with a closed-form solution for the radiation coefficient at each candidate location. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate that: (i) DM-GPA achieves higher WSR than other PASS architectures and fixed-array benchmarks, (ii) increasing the number of activated elements further improves the WSR of DM-GPA, and (iii) radiation coefficient adjustment is particularly beneficial when candidate activation locations are limited.

items.title: Water as a Battery: Using Hydropower Flexibility to Support the Grid
items.summary: This study presents a two-layer optimization framework to determine the optimal sizing of PV, wind, and battery storage co-located with existing hydroelectric plants to support rapidly increasing data center loads while minimizing cost, grid reliance, and transmission upgrades. The outer layer uses Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to select capacity combinations, while the inner layer performs rolling-horizon dispatch simulations to model hourly energy balance among PV, wind, hydro, and BESS, considering operational constraints. Two case studies were analyzed. At The Dalles Dam (Oregon), favorable wind resources and land availability enabled deployment of 111.2 MW PV and 117.9 MW wind, with no BESS required. Hydro flexibility allowed the system to meet the load with minimal grid support. In contrast, Conowingo Dam (Maryland) faced land constraints and limited renewables to 130 MW PV, leading to higher grid dependence. Co-locating hydro with renewables significantly enhances reliability and cost effectiveness by leveraging hydro's dispatchability to balance daily and seasonal variable generation from PV + Wind, reducing the need for storage or costly grid imports. This analysis provides a framework to meet the 99.9% availability targets of this new load type on the grid with sustainable energy resources.

items.title: Secure Integrated Sensing and Communications with Movable Beyond-Diagonal RIS
items.summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), when the sensed target is itself an eavesdropper, the illumination required for sensing coincides with the leakage that secrecy must suppress. This paper shows how a beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) with movable elements decouples the two tasks in a monostatic setting, where the echo returns to the base station through the surface. We prove that a lossless reciprocal BD-RIS maps $K$ incident fields onto $K$ prescribed fields if and only if the two sets share the same Gram matrix and their bilinear Gram matrix is symmetric; unlike a diagonal RIS, it can thus steer a two-dimensional incident subspace onto any prescribed subspace. With a single stream, sensing incurs an unavoidable rate loss, whereas a closed-form zero-forcing design with a confidential and a Gaussian sensing stream nulls the data at the target and the sensing at the user, so that sensing costs only an SNR offset. Since all variables follow in closed form for any placement, the joint design reduces to a monotone search over the element positions, without alternating optimization. Simulations show that the dual-stream design loses only $1.1$ bit/s/Hz when the sensing requirement grows by $30$ dB, against $8.3$ bit/s/Hz for a single stream, while movement, interconnection, and the robust derivative-null design add up to $1.9$, $0.9$, and $2.6$ bit/s/Hz, respectively.

items.title: A Framework for Learning and Reliability Certification in Neural Polar Decoding
items.summary: This paper investigates a framework that connects network training, independently certified population risk and sequential reliability in neural polar decoding. Network outputs determine information-bit decisions by their signs. Posterior mean-squared error (MSE) controls bit-error rate (BER), and a first-error identity connects errors evaluated with true preceding bits to sequential block-error rate (BLER). Three methods exploit sequential decoding structure to certify changes to trained receivers. First, distances from trained outputs to the zero decision threshold, termed learned margins, yield reliability bounds for over-parameterized neural network (ONN) updates subject to separate mean-squared output-change constraints at information positions. Second, a shared loss takes the largest block-error indicator difference between candidate decoders and successive cancellation (SC) on each frame. Its expectation bounds the corresponding BLER differences, termed excess BLER, for all fixed combinations of information-position implementations. An exact expression quantifies the gap between this shared bound and the largest BLER difference among fixed decoders. Third, verified linear programming (LP) and candidate-set subdivision tighten these guarantees with controllable computation at fixed confidence. ONN experiments assess conditional fitting and weight updates. Polar factor-graph experiments demonstrate reusable combination guarantees and storage reduction under prescribed excess-BLER allowances. Component timing identifies the dominant graph-propagation cost.

items.title: Exponential Wake-Up Overshoot in Explicit Gaussian Point-Process Filters
items.summary: When events resume after a long silence, explicit Gaussian point-process filters amplify the first update exponentially in the silence duration. We give the exact distribution of this update and a computable index that predicts when it overshoots. For the explicit (single-scoring-step) filter and its implicit posterior-mode counterpart, we derive second-order silence expansions of the state variance with opposite-sign logarithmic corrections. The crossing index determines when the post-wake prediction exceeds the resumed rate, separating the bin width at which the amplification exponent reaches one from the larger width at which the true rate is overshot. At fixed bin width, the implicit filter's expected loss grows logarithmically with silence duration, whereas a continuous-time counterexample rules out a bound uniform in bin width and silence duration. Experimental evaluation confirms these predictions in all 73 crossing cells and on exchange trade data, while variance caps reduce explicit overshoot but mostly hurt the implicit filter.

items.title: Self-Supervised Passive WiFi CSI-Based Motion Tracking with Physics-Informed Deep SSM
items.summary: Inferring target position from WiFi channel state information (CSI) is challenging due to the noisy and heterogeneous nature of CSI-derived observations. Measurements such as angle, delay, and Doppler provide only imperfect information about target position and velocity, particularly in dynamic multipath environments where observation reliability varies. Motivated by this challenge, this paper proposes a physics-informed Bayesian state space framework for passive CSI-based tracking. We introduce a context-conditioned deep state space model (DSSM) that captures temporal motion and environmental dynamics, while adaptively modeling time-varying observation uncertainties. By incorporating geometric constraints, this framework enables heterogeneous CSI measurement modalities to jointly regularize the consistency and confidence of the tracking process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework yields smoother trajectory estimates with reduced temporal fluctuations and outperforms existing methods in tracking accuracy.

items.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Distributed speculative decoding has emerged as a promising approach for device--server collaborative large language model (LLM) inference, but its decoding speedup is often limited by the vocabulary-scale communication overhead. In existing distributed speculative decoding methods, exact rejection sampling requires transmitting full token distributions over the LLM vocabulary between the device and the server, which becomes costly in bandwidth-constrained environments. To address this issue, we propose DISCO, a communication-efficient framework for distributed speculative decoding, that eliminates vocabulary-scale distribution transfer while preserving the exact target distribution. DISCO achieves this by introducing a server-side replica of the draft small language model (SLM), which enables the server to locally obtain the draft-side distribution required for rejection sampling. As a result, DISCO exchanges only drafted token indices and scalar probability values between the device and the server. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that DISCO consistently achieves higher decoding speedup than existing distributed speculative decoding methods, particularly under stringent bandwidth constraints.

items.title: Bi-Objective Receding-Horizon Scheduling of Nurses and Hospital Service Robots
items.summary: This paper studies the joint scheduling of nurses and hospital service robots as a bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming problem. The formulation represents heterogeneous nursing skills, alternative skill-coverage modes, nurse availability and temporal rules, workload balance, robot task capability, charging and battery dynamics, and human supervision. Robot workload relief is credited only when an eligible service is actually executed, and explicit supervision-load variables deduct the corresponding nurse capacity from clinical coverage. The receding-horizon formulation also includes a cross-window night--morning constraint and a terminal battery reserve. The computational study is presented as numerical verification on synthetic hospital-like instances rather than clinical validation. Under the proposed formulation, the eight-nurse reference case gives $Z_1=0.78$ and $Z_2=3.164$. A common-budget comparison on B20 seed~1 yields total shortage $53.70$ for the integrated model, compared with $58.03$ for sequential nurse--robot scheduling and $59.46$ for the nurse-only baseline. Additional experiments examine multiple epsilon budgets on a larger B30 instance, sensitivity to robot-relief/supervision parameters and objective weights, and one-day versus two-day rolling horizons against a static full-horizon reference. The battery and routing representations remain aggregate planning approximations, and the scalability evidence is interpreted accordingly. No patient records or real hospital staff data are used, so the results establish model behavior and comparative numerical evidence rather than practical clinical effectiveness.

items.title: Graph Signal Estimation With Unknown Topology
items.summary: Graph-signal estimation is commonly designed assuming that the underlying topology is known. In this paper, we consider estimation from general nonlinear measurements when the active topology is latent but is known to belong to a given family of candidate graphs. We first develop a class of topology-blind graph-spectral estimators that jointly exploit the candidate graphs, and characterize the performance loss compared to unconstrained linear estimation. We derive the minimum-mean-squared-error (MSE) multi-basis estimator and show that its optimal operator is the weighted projection of the topology-blind linear MMSE (LMMSE) operator onto the multi-graph filter space. This characterization provides exact expressions for the excess MSE and conditions for attaining the topology-blind LMMSE. To reduce the number of parameters, we develop estimators based on shared spectral responses and low-rank representations, and consider data-dependent estimators that infer the topology from the measurements, by maximum a-posteriori probability (MAP) selection or posterior weighting (multiple-model). We further extend the framework to networks of different sizes by jointly optimizing a common spectral function. We derive its MSE-optimal coefficients and decompose the resulting estimation loss into graph-filter approximation error and the additional cost of sharing a spectral response across networks. The proposed estimators admit sample-based implementations, while the shared spectral function can be applied to unseen graphs without retraining its coefficients. Simulations on IEEE power networks demonstrate the benefits of the proposed graph-spectral estimators under topology uncertainty and cross- network transfer.

items.title: Cross-User Adaptation for sEMG Gesture Recognition via Continual Learning
items.summary: Prosthetic and assistive interfaces increasingly depend on decoding hand gestures from surface electromyography (sEMG). Because the signal is shaped by person-specific factors, the recurrent neural networks (RNNs) commonly used to model these temporal streams must adapt to new wearers and new gesture classes after deployment. Continual learning (CL) enables this adaptation without retraining from scratch, yet applying it to recurrent sEMG models is not straightforward. Standard recurrent training practices can destabilize learning, and which CL strategy holds up under realistic cross-user drift is unestablished. We evaluate three representative CL strategies under domain- and class-incremental drift on NinaPro DB1, and find experience replay to outperform elastic weight consolidation (EWC) and naive fine-tuning. It reaches 83.3% final accuracy for class-incremental drift while limiting forgetting to 1.8-5.8% accuracy drop, as against 16.2-28.5% for EWC and naive training. We further show these models must be trained on shuffled, independently-windowed segments. Streaming windows in temporal order collapses the network into predicting a single dominant gesture, while a shuffled, stateless regime trains stably. Finally, hand-crafted time-domain features raise per-task accuracy by up to about 40% over raw signals, but only replay preserves that gain under class-incremental drift.

items.title: Unifying Performance and Equity via Percentile Optimization and Cell-Free Massive MIMO
items.summary: Improving the throughput of the weakest users is a central objective of wireless resource allocation, and the objective around which the user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (UC-mMIMO) architecture is built. This paper brings the two together by formulating and solving percentile programs for UC-mMIMO networks. We maximize the sum-least-qth-percentile (SLqP) rate via downlink power control, a utility that targets the user equipments (UEs) in the lowest q percentile of the rate distribution and subsumes max-min-rate and sum-rate maximization as special cases. The problem is non-convex, non-smooth and NP-hard. The cyclic maximization approach of one of the previous percentile optimization series does not carry over: the coherent joint transmission technique introduces cross terms in the powers that destroy the block-concavity on which it relies. We develop a change of variables that restores block-concavity, yielding an algorithm with closed-form auxiliary updates and a concave power update, and we give a self-contained proof of non-decreasing convergence to a directional stationary point. Simulations establish two facts: first, percentile optimization retains its value in an architecture with no cell edges; relative to the weighted minimum mean-square error benchmark, it raises the average rate of the lowest-10th-percentile UEs by 56--72% and Jain's fairness index from below 0.92 to above 0.99. Second, compared directly with massive MIMO and small cells under the same SLqP utility, UC-mMIMO delivers the highest lower-percentile rates at every access point density tested, by up to 62% and 2.7$\times$ respectively, at the same fairness, and its advantage widens with densification.

items.title: VLN on the Fly: An Onboard Vision-Language Navigation Stack for Aerial Robots
items.summary: Running vision-language navigation fully onboard an aerial robot is hard, since grounding, planning, and control must share limited compute and a single-stage error is difficult to isolate in flight. End-to-end aerial policies fuse these stages into one network, giving up the observability and safety checks a modular stack keeps available. We propose VLN on the Fly, an onboard stack that keeps grounding, planning, and control as separate, inspectable stages. A quantized VLM grounds an instruction to a coarse image cell, depth lifts it to a 3D goal, a fast B-spline planner returns a feasible trajectory, and a pretrained reinforcement learning policy tracks it to motor commands across quadrotors. Across 15 onboard flights over three everyday referents in a controlled indoor volume, the stack reaches the target in 13 of 15 trials with 5.72 cm mean goal error and 39.3% average GPU utilization. In 6 additional cluttered-environment trials, the stack tracks collision-free trajectories under onboard perception gating.

items.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Are Speech Emotion Recognition Models Learning?
items.summary: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is important in human-machine interactions, enabling machines to detect and classify human emotions from solely human speech. Speech emotion recognition (SER) benchmarks routinely report accuracies above 90 percent, yet these models fail when deployed or tested on diverse speakers. The papers overlook a fundamental issue: models may be learning speaker identity and tone rather than generalized emotional cues. We introduce a two-condition audit protocol that measures, for any published SER model, how much of its reported performance survives when speakers are held out. Each model is evaluated twice under identical architecture, features, and training recipe: a control condition that reproduces the common random-split practice, and a strict speaker-independent condition with disjoint speakers. We apply the protocol to seven model configurations from five published papers, spanning convolutional, recurrent, transformer, vision-transformer, and self-supervised wav2vec2 architectures, on RAVDESS, EMO-DB, and SAVEE, with a fourth corpus (EARS) as an external check. Across 21 model-dataset pairs, published headline numbers reproduce close to the control but drop by 6.9 to 63.1 percentage points under strict speaker independence. Our results quantify speaker memorization as a dominant, previously unmeasured component of published SER performance, and we recommend two-condition reporting as a community standard.

items.title: Asymmetric-Information Resource Allocation Games: An LP Approach to Purposeful Deception
items.summary: In this work, we introduce the Deceptive Resource Allocation Game (DRAG), which studies purposeful deception within a Bayesian game framework. In DRAG, a Defender allocates resources across the true asset and several decoys to influence an Attacker's beliefs and actions, with the goal of diverting the Attacker away from the true asset. We seek to characterize purposeful deception, whereby the Defender deceives only when doing so improves its performance. To this end, we solve for the Perfect Bayesian Nash Equilibrium (PBNE) of the corresponding game. We show that, despite the coupled belief-policy interdependence, the problem admits an efficient, non-iterative linear programming formulation. Numerical results demonstrate that the resulting policies naturally balance effective allocation and belief manipulation, giving rise to purposeful and emergent deceptive behaviors.

items.title: FastSAR: High-Throughput, High-Fidelity Open-Source SAR Image Formation on CPUs, GPUs and TPUs
items.summary: Exact backprojection of a spaceborne SAR collection needs one interpolated read per pixel for every pulse; for the 12,207 by 8,808 pixel Umbra image of the Panama Canal this balloons to 1.6 trillion reads. FastSAR is an open-source library for SAR image formation on CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs, with factorized backprojection, exact backprojection and polar format behind one Python interface and readers for the vendors' phase-history files. Its factorized kernels form the Panama image in 11.2 s on a 16-vCPU instance, 3.0 s on an NVIDIA L4, 0.6 s on an H100 and 2.9 s on a TPU v6e, with errors of -56 to -63 dB relative to a float64 exact backprojection in three regions over six cloud devices; the L4, a modest GPU, gives the lowest cost of the six at 0.59 US dollars per thousand images. At exact backprojection FastSAR is as fast as the MatX backprojection example, by far the fastest open-source implementation found (10.9 against 11.6 s at the same accuracy, with MatX's pixel coordinates in float64); its factorized algorithm is 3.8 times faster than MatX, and its polar format forms the image in 1.4 s on the L4 at -32 dB. On five Capella collections in three modes the worst-region error is below -59 dB.

items.title: Residual-Calibrated Multimodal Spatiotemporal Learning for Future Beam Prediction
items.summary: We propose a residual calibrated multimodal spatiotemporal framework for future beam prediction on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23. The framework integrates visual observations, location features, and historical beam labels to predict the beam label of the next dataset record. A pretrained Swin-Tiny encoder extracts features from four consecutive RGB frames. Bidirectional cross-attention integrates visual and two dimensional Unit 1 location representations, while a temporal Transformer incorporates historical beam label embeddings to model dependencies across the observation window. A supplementary offline residual head adjusts the frozen supervised logits using immediate correctness rewards and an auxiliary classification loss. A fixed probability mixture of the supervised and residual outputs is selected using validation accuracy. From 11,387 aligned records, we construct 11,255 temporal windows and partition them by capture run into 7,854 training, 1,905 validation, and 1,496 test samples. The supervised predictor achieves Top-1, Top-2, Top-3, and Top-5 test accuracies of 62.83%, 74.80%, 79.75%, and 81.08%, respectively. The residual predictor achieves corresponding accuracies of 61.76%, 75.07%, 79.41%, and 81.02%. Residual adjustment increases Top-2 accuracy by 0.27 percentage points, while the supervised predictor retains higher Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies. The validation-selected mixture coincides with the residual predictor. The proposed framework combines cross-modal sensing features with explicit beam-history conditioning and a separately trained residual adjustment stage for one-record-ahead beam prediction. Initial evaluation on held-out capture runs characterizes the candidate-ranking performance of both prediction stages and favors the supervised variant for Top-1 selection. These findings motivate further study of historical conditioning and residual refinement.

items.title: Align, Then Adapt: Few-Shot fMRI Visual Reconstruction For New Subjects
items.summary: Reconstructing visual images from fMRI data is a central but challenging problem in neuroscience. Despite recent progress, current methods fall short when data and computation are limited-precisely the conditions under which this task is most critical. We introduce Adapter Alignment, a staged, architecture-agnostic training procedure for adapting a pre-trained reconstruction model to a new subject with little data. Rather than letting a shared representation space emerge implicitly, lightweight subject-specific adapters are first explicitly aligned to a pre-trained reference subject on a small set of shared calibration images, and the full pipeline is then fine-tuned while preserving this alignment. The resulting representations not only place different subjects in a shared space but also align them semantically. Our results demonstrate significant gains in low-data regimes, improving reconstruction metrics by up to 8%, and pre-diffusion retrieval shows that these gains reflect additional image-specific information in the fMRI embeddings rather than the generative prior. We also propose a coverage-based algorithm to select representative calibration images. Using both techniques together, we surpass baseline models fine-tuned with one hour of data using only 24 minutes of subject-specific data. The procedure is effective across architectures, reference subjects, and datasets, including adapting 3T subjects to a 7T reference.

items.title: SCALE-X: A Systematic Complexity-Aware Low-Precision Approach for Digital Predistortion
items.summary: This letter presents SCALE-X, a systematic, complexity-aware, low-precision, model-based digital predistortion (DPD) technique for power amplifiers with enhanced capabilities. The proposed approach employs a novel complexity-aware coefficient pruning method, which, when combined with optimized fixed-point modeling, enables more accurate capture of quantization effects and supports better informed decisions for implementation. Targeted configuration of model order, memory depth, and coefficient bitwidth delivers dramatic cuts in computational overhead without much sacrificing accuracy. Field-programmable gate array implementation demonstrates practical trade-offs with improved overall efficiency.

items.title: Explainable GeoAI for urban wildfire structure loss: vegetation and built environment in the 2025 Palisades Fire
items.summary: Urban wildfire resilience depends on interactions among built form, vegetation condition, and extreme fire weather, yet city-scale risk models often overlook whether predictive skill transfers across neighborhoods. We developed a spatially validated GeoAI workflow for the January 2025 Palisades Fire, linking 12,081 CAL FIRE damage inspections to pre-fire Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, Landsat surface temperature, LANDFIRE fuels, terrain, and OpenStreetMap buildings and roads. Among 9,883 inspected residential structures, 5,566 were destroyed. Random cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC 0.92 for the integrated XGBoost model, but 1 km spatial block validation reduced performance to 0.75; logistic regression performed similarly and was better calibrated. Building count within 100 m was the strongest predictor, with destruction odds increasing 4.12-fold per standard deviation. Vegetation moisture and greenness showed opposing conditional associations: NDMI at 100-300 m was protective (OR 0.52), whereas NDVI at 30-100 m was positively associated with destruction after accounting for moisture (OR 1.74). Predictive information was concentrated at the 100-300 m neighborhood scale. A separate post-fire track mapped burn severity and vegetation recovery without leakage. The results support neighborhood-scale susceptibility screening, moisture-aware vegetation management, and spatial block validation as a minimum standard for single-event urban wildfire modeling.

items.title: A Sentinel-2 benchmark dataset for deep-learning active-fire segmentation across 25 California wildfires, July 2020-August 2026
items.summary: This article describes an open image dataset for developing and evaluating active-fire segmentation methods in satellite imagery. The dataset contains 2,148 image-mask pairs from 25 California wildfires, with acquisitions spanning July 2020 to August 2026. Each image is a 512x512-pixel, three-channel composite derived from Sentinel-2 Level-2A bands B12, B11 and B8A at 20 m spatial sampling. A fixed linear rendering is applied throughout the dataset. Corresponding masks distinguish background, SWIR-rule active fire and invalid observations. The masks were generated from shortwave-infrared brightness and near-infrared contrast, followed by constrained neighborhood growth. The release includes chip-level metadata and an incident-disjoint partition containing 18 training, three validation and four test fires. Among the image pairs, 841 contain active-fire labels; these labels occupy 0.0766% of all grid cells. A mask-blind analyst review covers 233 test chips and provides a separate assessment of the rule-generated labels at chip and connected-component levels. Reference training and evaluation code accompanies the data, including a ResNet-34 U-Net implementation with validation-based checkpoint and threshold selection. The archived images, masks, metadata and review annotations support research on rare-class segmentation, learning from algorithmic labels and transfer across fire incidents. The versioned dataset is deposited on Zenodo, with preparation and reuse software maintained in a public GitHub repository.

items.title: Agentic Digital Twin-Assisted Multimodal Predictive Handover
items.summary: Rapid mobility, blockage, and propagation changes can invalidate instantaneous handover decisions in dense mid-band and millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks. We therefore propose a flexible, model-agnostic \emph{Agentic Digital Twin (DT)} framework for predictive cell handover. The DT generates synchronized multimodal states, while three agents autonomously select forecasts, plan handover actions, and adapt decisions using execution feedback. The proposed Agentic DT provided the best collective balance among handover activity, the reliability of the selected links, and the accuracy of target next-generation Node B (gNB) selection relative to the best available future link. It reduced average handovers from $11.0$ for Event~A3 to $8.0$ per trajectory while maintaining $98.2\%$ ray-path availability.

items.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~II: Fisher-Majorized Certified Policy Iteration
items.summary: Building on the uncertainty description developed in Part~I, this paper introduces a Fisher-majorized domain-randomized generalized policy iteration framework for data-driven linear quadratic regulator (LQR) synthesis. At each iteration, partial Bellman evaluation over a fixed batch of uncertainty realizations produces a structured Sylvester policy-improvement step. A residual-weighted Fisher curvature controls the policy-induced variation in the stationary covariance and converts the Sylvester model into a certified upper bound on the cost change, thereby guaranteeing descent for every accepted step. A check-and-correct mechanism then certifies stability over the entire uncertainty support, rather than only over the sampled realizations. Consequently, every iterate is robustly stabilizing and monotonically decreases the fixed-batch objective. The Fisher truncation and stability correction become inactive after finitely many times. The objective gap then contracts linearly to a floor determined by the dispersion of the realization-wise Riccati targets and by measurement noise. In the absence of measurement noise, this floor vanishes when the realization-wise targets coincide.

items.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~I: Certified Uncertainty Refinement
items.summary: Learning controllers from trajectories corrupted by process and measurement noise is difficult when the system matrices and the noise covariances are unknown: noisy regressors bias least squares, and model uncertainty cannot be quantified without the noise covariance, which can only be estimated from residuals of the uncertain model. This paper, Part~I of a two-part study, resolves both obstacles with a finite-sample framework that certifies, and iteratively refines, uncertainty sets for the model, the noise in the collected data, and the noise covariance. A closed-loop parametrization based on delayed instrumental variables (IVs) removes the bias and assigns to every candidate model exactly one noise sequence that reproduces the data. Learning this noise breaks the circular dependence: the noise sequences give the covariance estimate directly, models whose noise violates the prior or the statistical certificates are discarded, and the surviving models yield a tighter covariance certificate. Several delayed instruments further tighten the model set and give a certified test of data consistency. We prove finite-sample containment of the true model, noise, and covariance, recursive nesting, and convergence at the IV rate. Part~II uses these certificates for domain-randomized linear quadratic regulator synthesis.

items.title: Data-based Low-conservative Nonlinear Safe Control Learning
items.summary: This paper develops a data-driven safe control framework for nonlinear discrete-time systems with parametric uncertainty and additive disturbances. The proposed approach constructs a data-consistent closed-loop representation that enables controller synthesis and safety certification directly from data. Unlike existing methods that treat unmodeled nonlinearities as global worst-case uncertainties using Lipschitz bounds, the proposed approach embeds nonlinear terms directly into the invariance conditions via a geometry-aware difference-of-convex formulation. This enables facet- and direction-specific convexification, avoiding both nonlinearity cancellation and the excessive conservatism induced by uniform global bounds. We further propose a vertex-dependent controller construction that enforces convexity and contractivity conditions locally on the active facets associated with each vertex, thereby enlarging the class of certifiable invariant sets. For systems subject to additive disturbances, disturbance effects are embedded directly into the verification conditions through optimized, geometry-dependent bounds, rather than via uniform margin inflation, yielding less conservative robust safety guarantees. As a result, the proposed methods can certify substantially larger safe sets, naturally accommodate joint state and input constraints, and provide data-driven safety guarantees. The simulation results show a significant improvement in both nonlinearity tolerance and the size of the certified safe set.

items.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
items.summary: Streaming automatic speech recognition transcribes at low latency but produces an unattributed word stream, while real-time applications such as customer-service analytics need each word tied to a speaker role. Role attribution is usually a separate stage, either an offline or streaming speaker-diarization model aligned to the words or a text-based large language model applied to the transcript, and role labels for training are scarce. We present RoleHear, a semi-supervised pipeline that makes a single cache-aware streaming transducer emit roles inline through lightweight in-vocabulary role tokens: a fast turn-boundary marker followed by a per-role token a few words later. An offline transducer teacher, fine-tuned into a role-attributed recognizer, relabels unlabeled audio, and a multimodal large language model supplies silver role labels where gold annotations are unavailable.
